variables.name: Licensing jurisdiction boundary
variables.description: The area where the vehicle's licence allows pickups (NYC for TLC vehicles); trips may end outside it, but pickups outside are effectively unavailable.
variables.values_or_range: Inside five boroughs: pickups allowed. Outside: drop-off only. EWR: yellow 57 pickups vs 15,829 drop-offs (Oct 2019); HVFHV 228 vs 63,278 (Jun 2021). Uber JFK pickups only for TLC-licensed drivers
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own counts from TLC records; [S] Uber JFK driver-information page
variables.data_source: TLC trip records; Uber airport driver pages; county taxi rules [U]
variables.how_to_model: Pickup-eligibility mask by polygon and licence type

variables.name: Robotaxi operating geofence (ODD)
variables.description: The polygon and road types where an autonomous vehicle is allowed and able to drive and serve riders.
variables.values_or_range: Example: Waymo NYC test permit (Aug 2025 to 31 Mar 2026) covered Manhattan south of 112th St + Downtown Brooklyn, 8 cars, safety driver, no paying riders. Scenario options: core-only / core + airports / citywide
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Vital City Waymo map methodology (GitHub, 6 May 2026, citing THE CITY, CNBC and the Aug 2025 Mayor's Office release): 8 cars with safety drivers in Manhattan south of 112th St and Downtown Brooklyn, state testing permits expired 31 Mar 2026, NY law effectively bars driverless commercial service; [P*] 34 RCNY 4-17: an NYC test permit needs NYS DMV approval, a test operator in the driver's seat, DOT-approved areas and hours and a $5,000 yearly fee [uncertain: 'passenger service would need a TLC licence' not re-checked]
variables.data_source: 34 RCNY 4-17; Vital City waymo-map (https://github.com/vitalcity-nyc/waymo-map); no machine-readable NYC geofence found
variables.how_to_model: Geofence polygon + road-class whitelist; requests outside are unservable or lost to competitors

variables.name: Spatial resolution
variables.description: The unit at which positions and demand are represented: taxi zone, hex grid or road segment.
variables.values_or_range: Taxi zone (~3 km2 mean, 263 units) / H3 hex res 8 (~0.7 km2) / OSM drivable road graph (tens of thousands of nodes)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] Finer resolution lets positioning skill show but costs compute and data; zone level matches public trip data
variables.data_source: TLC zones; OpenStreetMap (https://www.openstreetmap.org); NYC DCP LION
variables.how_to_model: Start at zone level with a random point inside the zone; upgrade to a road graph for routing, curbs and hails

variables.name: Zone adjacency and travel-time skim
variables.description: A zone-to-zone neighbour list and travel-time matrix used for repositioning and fleet rebalancing.
variables.values_or_range: 263 x 263 matrix of travel times by hour (minutes); neighbour lists
variables.impact_evidence: [design] Needed by both single-car repositioning and fleet rebalancing; R10 supplies the times
variables.data_source: Derived from OSM graph + TLC trip durations; NYC DOT traffic speeds (cross-link R10)
variables.how_to_model: Precompute skims per hour band; agent tools query ETA between zones

variables.name: Repositioning target (where to wait or cruise)
variables.description: The agent's choice of which zone or street to drive to, or wait in, when empty; the core geographic skill the benchmark measures.
variables.values_or_range: Any reachable zone or road node; options: stay, cruise a loop (taxi only), drive to zone z, go to a hub or airport, go home [corrected by fact-check: 34 RCNY 4-11(b) bars vehicles other than taxis from cruising to search for passengers, so app cars and robotaxis may only wait legally or drive to a chosen spot]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Haggag, McManus and Paci (2017, AEJ Applied 9(1):70-95; citation confirmed): neighbourhood-specific experience raises taxi driver productivity and changes search; Buchholz (2022, REStud 89(2):556-591): search frictions leave some areas unserved while others have excess cabs; [P*] 34 RCNY 4-11(b) cruising ban for non-taxis
variables.data_source: Logged from agent actions; benchmark compares with TLC-derived demand
variables.how_to_model: Action space: reposition(zone or node), wait(here), cruise(route); travel time from R10

variables.name: Road hierarchy class
variables.description: Each road segment's class (expressway or parkway, arterial avenue, collector, local) sets its speed, capacity and how good it is for finding hails.
variables.values_or_range: OSM highway = motorway / trunk / primary / secondary / tertiary / residential. Mean in-trip speed: ~10.2 mph for Yellow Zone pickups vs ~20.9 mph for airport pickups (yellow Oct 2019)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation (distance / duration) from TLC yellow Oct 2019
variables.data_source: OpenStreetMap; NYC DCP LION street centerline (lanes, width, direction)
variables.how_to_model: Graph edges carry class: free-flow speed and capacity; congestion handled in R10

variables.name: One-way streets and circuity
variables.description: Manhattan's mostly one-way grid and the rivers make driving distance longer than straight-line distance, and a pickup on the wrong side costs a loop.
variables.values_or_range: Most avenues and most cross streets one-way [corrected by fact-check: some avenues are two-way, e.g. Park Ave, Central Park West, West End Ave, York Ave [U]]; major two-way crosstown streets (14th, 23rd, 34th, 42nd, 57th, 72nd, 79th, 86th, 96th, 110th, 125th); circuity ~1.2-1.4; turn-around loop ~2-4 blocks
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge of the NYC grid; LION has a traffic-direction field
variables.data_source: NYC DCP LION (TrafDir); OSM oneway tag
variables.how_to_model: Directed graph; car heading matters for pickup ETA

variables.name: Turn restrictions
variables.description: Banned turns (many Midtown left turns, some by time of day) lengthen routes and ETAs.
variables.values_or_range: Restricted turns per intersection; time windows such as 7am-7pm
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge
variables.data_source: OSM turn-restriction relations; NYC DOT signage
variables.how_to_model: Turn-restriction table in the router

variables.name: Speed limits
variables.description: Legal maximum per segment; caps free-flow speed (robotaxis obey exactly, humans may exceed).
variables.values_or_range: Citywide default 25 mph; Sammy's Law lets the city set 20 mph streets and 10-15 mph school zones (all school zones 15 mph by 2029 planned); highways 40-50 mph
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] NYC Admin Code 19-177(a) and 34 RCNY 4-06(a): 25 mph unless signed otherwise; 19-177(d)-(e): 20 mph slow zones and 15-20 mph near schools; [S] Streetsblog (Oct 2026), West Side Spirit: Sammy's Law rollout [corrected by fact-check: the base limit is not in doubt; it is 25 mph by law]
variables.data_source: NYC DOT speed-limit data on NYC Open Data [U]; OSM maxspeed
variables.how_to_model: Edge attribute; robotaxi speed = min(limit, traffic speed)

variables.name: Enforcement camera locations
variables.description: Where speed, red-light and bus-lane cameras are, which creates fine risk for human drivers.
variables.values_or_range: Speed camera fine $50 (+$25 late); bus-lane fine $50 first offence rising to $250; cameras cover all bus lanes
variables.impact_evidence: [S] NYC DOT bus-lane rules; news coverage of speed cameras [uncertain: fine amounts, late fee and bus-lane camera coverage not re-checked; sources blocked]
variables.data_source: NYC Open Data parking and camera violations [U]
variables.how_to_model: Per-edge violation probability x fine, applied when the agent's driving style breaks rules

variables.name: Road access by vehicle class
variables.description: Some roads are closed to some vehicles: parkways ban commercial vehicles (taxis and FHVs count as passenger cars) and robotaxis may be kept off freeways.
variables.values_or_range: Parkway allowed yes/no; robotaxi freeway allowed yes/no (scenario)
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; medium for robotaxi if freeways are excluded
variables.data_source: OSM access tags; NYSDOT parkway rules [U]
variables.how_to_model: Edge mask per vehicle class

variables.name: Elevation and grade
variables.description: Hills slightly raise energy use; NYC is mostly flat with steep spots (Washington Heights, Staten Island, parts of the Bronx).
variables.values_or_range: Grade 0-10%+; elevation 0 to ~125 m
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge
variables.data_source: USGS 3DEP; NYC 1-ft DEM on NYC Open Data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Edge grade feeds an energy multiplier in R08

variables.name: River crossings as chokepoints
variables.description: Manhattan and Staten Island are islands and the Bronx is cut off from Manhattan and Queens by water, so most links between boroughs and all links to New Jersey are bridges or tunnels; they concentrate delay, incidents and tolls. [corrected by fact-check: Brooklyn and Queens share a land border and the Bronx joins Westchester by land, so bridges and tunnels are not the only links]
variables.values_or_range: East River: Brooklyn, Manhattan, Williamsburg, Queensboro bridges (free), Queens-Midtown and Hugh Carey tunnels and RFK (tolled); Hudson: GWB, Lincoln, Holland (PANYNJ); Harlem River bridges free except the MTA Henry Hudson Bridge (tolled); Verrazzano, Throgs Neck, Whitestone, Cross Bay, Marine Pkwy (MTA, tolled); Staten Island to NJ: Goethals, Bayonne, Outerbridge (PANYNJ, tolled) [corrected by fact-check: added the Henry Hudson Bridge and the Staten Island-NJ crossings [U]]
variables.impact_evidence: [P] 5.9% of yellow trips paid a toll, mean $6.63 (Oct 2019, own computation, reproduced); [U] network facts [corrected by fact-check: impact high -> medium; tolls are mostly passed to riders and crossing delay is modelled in R10]
variables.data_source: OpenStreetMap; NYC DOT bridge traffic volumes [U]
variables.how_to_model: Crossing edges with their own capacity, incident probability (R03) and travel-time variance (R10)

variables.name: MTA bridge and tunnel tolls
variables.description: Toll charged at MTA crossings, by crossing, payment type and direction.
variables.values_or_range: Car E-ZPass at major crossings $6.55 until Aug 2023 and $6.94 from Aug 2023 (most common toll on yellow trip records), raised ~6% on 4 Jan 2026 [uncertain: 2026 car rate not checked]; smaller crossings (Henry Hudson, Cross Bay, Marine Pkwy) about half (bus E-ZPass $3.39 vs $6.42; a $3.18 car toll is common in 2023-24 records) [U]; East River bridges and the other Harlem River bridges free [corrected by fact-check: the Henry Hudson Bridge is tolled, so not all Harlem River crossings are free]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] tolls_amount in yellow 2023-24 records ($6.55 in Jul 2023; $6.94 in Sep 2023 and Jan 2024); [S] MTA franchise-bus toll page (rates effective 4 Jan 2026); news on ~6% E-ZPass rise; [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(e)-(f): taxi passengers pay the actual E-ZPass toll, with directional rules on Cross Bay, Marine Pkwy and Verrazzano
variables.how_to_model: Toll table by crossing x direction x payment; passed to the rider when loaded, paid by the driver when empty

variables.name: Port Authority Hudson crossing tolls
variables.description: GWB, Lincoln and Holland charge only when entering New York, so a car returning empty from NJ pays; one-direction tolling (also Verrazzano, into Staten Island only [U]) makes return legs cost more than outbound legs. [corrected by fact-check: for yellow and green taxi trips to Newark, Westchester and Nassau the passenger must pay tolls to and from the destination (35 RCNY 58-26(c), (f)(2)), so the taxi's return toll is reimbursed; app drivers get the higher out-of-town pay rate instead]
variables.values_or_range: Car E-ZPass $16.79 peak / ~$14.79 off-peak, toll-by-plate ~$23.05-23.30 [uncertain: toll-by-plate amount not checked] (from 4 Jan 2026); peak = weekdays 6-10am and 4-8pm, weekends 11am-9pm
variables.impact_evidence: [S] ROI-NJ (Jan 2026); PANYNJ Truckers Guide (Apr 2026); [P*] yellow records show PANYNJ car tolls $14.75 / $12.75 (2023) and $15.38 / $13.38 (Jan 2024), consistent with yearly indexing to $16.79 / $14.79 in 2026
variables.how_to_model: Inbound-only toll on NJ-to-NY crossing edges; charged to the driver on empty legs except where the passenger reimburses return tolls (taxi trips to EWR, Westchester, Nassau)

variables.name: Congestion Relief Zone (CRZ)
variables.description: Manhattan at or south of 60th St (excluding FDR Drive, West Side Highway / Route 9A and Hugh Carey Tunnel links) where each taxi/FHV trip to, from, within or through the zone pays a per-trip charge.
variables.values_or_range: $0.75 per yellow, green or other FHV trip; $1.50 per HVFHV trip; since 5 Jan 2025; private cars $9 peak (2025-27), $12 (2028-30), $15 (2031), $2.25 overnight [uncertain: later phases and the overnight rate not re-checked]; unenrolled fleets pay a daily toll
variables.impact_evidence: [S] MTA taxi/FHV toll page; several 2026 GitHub analyses agree on $0.75 taxi / $1.50 HVFHV / $9 peak from 5 Jan 2025 and treat the charge as still in force in 2026; [S] TLC trip-record dictionaries (Mar 2025) list cbd_congestion_fee 'starting Jan. 5, 2025' (via sibling dossier R07, read there as P*)
variables.applies_to: all; robotaxi fleet pays as TLC vehicle or daily toll
variables.data_source: MTA CBD taxi zones dataset (https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/mta-central-business-district-taxi-zones); cbd_congestion_fee field in 2025+ TLC trip records [S]
variables.how_to_model: Polygon; flag trips whose route touches it (excluding exempt edges); rider-paid but shifts demand (R05) and speeds (R10)

variables.name: State congestion surcharge zone (96th St line)
variables.description: A second, larger zone: trips that begin, end or pass through Manhattan south of 96th St pay a state surcharge.
variables.values_or_range: $2.50 yellow, $2.75 green and FHV, $0.75 shared ride
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 51-03: 'Congestion Zone' = Manhattan south of and excluding 96th St; [P*] amounts seen in trip records: yellow $2.50, green $2.75 (Oct 2019), HVFHV $2.75 and shared $0.75 (Jan 2023); [S] TLC taxi-fare page
variables.how_to_model: Second polygon; per-trip surcharge in the fare engine

variables.name: Fee-avoiding route choice
variables.description: Because the FDR and West Side Highway are outside the CRZ and some bridges are free, a route can avoid a charge at the cost of time.
variables.values_or_range: k alternative routes per OD with toll and time trade-off
variables.impact_evidence: [S] CRZ exclusion list; [design]
variables.how_to_model: Offer k-shortest paths with costs; agent or router chooses

variables.name: Curb regulation at the stop point
variables.description: The sign type at the curb decides whether a quick pickup or drop-off is legal.
variables.values_or_range: No Parking (stop OK) / No Standing (quick passenger pickup OK, no waiting) / No Stopping (not allowed) / bus stop (OK if no bus is blocked) / taxi stand (taxis only; other cars may only briefly load, and TLC fines an FHV driver $350 for a first pickup at a taxi stand) / 'For-Hire Vehicles Only' curb ($115 if standing beyond a quick pickup [uncertain: fine amount not checked]) [corrected by fact-check: added the taxi-stand pickup ban for FHVs]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-11(c): taxis and FHVs may briefly stop to pick up or drop off where standing or parking is banned, within 12 in of the curb, but not where stopping is banned, in a bike lane or in a crosswalk; 34 RCNY 4-08(c)(1); 35 RCNY 80-19(d)(2); [S] NYC DOT parking sign legend; NYC DOF violation codes
variables.data_source: NYC DOT Parking Regulation Locations and Signs (NYC Open Data) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Curb-segment attribute; illegal stop = fine probability or forced re-loop

variables.name: Rider-driver rendezvous time
variables.description: Minutes between the car arriving and the rider getting in, driven by building entrances, curb space, double parking and crowds.
variables.values_or_range: Uber trips, Jan 2023: pickup minus on-scene time median 0.8 min, 75th percentile 1.8, 90th 2.0, 0.5% over 5 min (values bunch just above 2 min) [corrected by fact-check: the original said '0.5-5 min typical [U]'; Lyft (HV0005) records leave on_scene_datetime empty in 99.9% of trips]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Fact-check computation on HVFHV Jan 2023 (18.48M trips; fields request_datetime, on_scene_datetime and pickup_datetime confirmed) [corrected by fact-check: impact medium -> low for human drivers, about 1 min per trip; could be medium for robotaxis if riders must walk to the car [design]]
variables.applies_to: all; longer for robotaxi (rider walks to car)
variables.data_source: TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime, on_scene_datetime, pickup_datetime)
variables.how_to_model: Per-zone x hour lognormal dwell fitted from HVFHV records, added to each pickup

variables.name: Bus lanes
variables.description: Lanes reserved for buses (and Access-A-Ride vans) that other cars may enter only to make a right turn (through an intersection only within 200 ft of entering the lane), to reach the curb, or to quickly pick up or drop off passengers. [corrected by fact-check: the 200 ft limit applies to right turns, not to driveways only; 34 RCNY 4-12(m)]
variables.values_or_range: Curbside pickup allowed; stopping in the centre of the lane not allowed; fines $50 rising to $250; cameras on all bus lanes
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-12(m)(1); [S] NYC DOT bus-lane rules; TLC bus/bike lane brochure [uncertain: fine schedule and camera coverage not re-checked]
variables.data_source: NYC DOT bus lanes (NYC Open Data) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Lane attribute with hours; fine risk when misused

variables.name: Busways and transit-priority streets
variables.description: Streets where through car traffic is banned for set hours, but taxis and FHVs may enter for local pickups and must turn off at the next street.
variables.values_or_range: 14th St busway (3rd to 9th Ave, 6am-10pm daily; cars may enter to pick up or drop off and must turn right within a block or two, no left turns) [corrected by fact-check: the original said 3rd to 8th Ave]; others such as Main St Flushing, Jamaica Ave, Archer Ave, 181st St [U]; 34th St bus priority (2025)
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-12(m)(2): only buses and Access-A-Ride vans during restricted hours except where signs allow; [S] NYT (Oct 2019, GitHub copy) and Village Sun / amNY on 14th St busway rules; NYC DOT 34th St documents
variables.how_to_model: Edges with through-traffic ban + forced turn after a stop

variables.name: Car-free park drives and plazas
variables.description: Roads closed to cars inside demand areas, so pickups move to the edges and routes detour.
variables.values_or_range: Central Park loop drives car-free since 27 Jun 2018 (transverses open); Prospect Park loop car-free; Times Square / Broadway plazas; Open Streets time windows
variables.impact_evidence: [S] ABC7, Central Park Conservancy (2018)
variables.data_source: OSM; NYC DOT Open Streets data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Remove edges (permanently or by time); snap pickups to the nearest legal curb

variables.name: Taxi stands and hotel queues
variables.description: Designated stands (hotels, transit hubs) where only taxis may wait in line for passengers.
variables.values_or_range: Stand present yes/no; queue length 0-30 cabs [U]; the first two cabs must stay in the driver's seat; green cabs may use stands only in the Hail Zone
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-08(c)(1): only taxis may stand at a taxi stand; 35 RCNY 80-19(d): queue rules and green-cab limits; [S] NYC DOT sign legend
variables.how_to_model: FIFO queue node fed by hotel or hub demand

variables.name: Taxi/FHV relief stands
variables.description: Curb spaces where taxi and FHV drivers may park for up to one hour to take a break.
variables.values_or_range: 113 stands: Manhattan 70, Queens 28, Bronx 12, Brooklyn 3, Staten Island 0 [uncertain: count not re-checked]; one-hour limit
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-08(c)(2): taxis and FHVs may park at a relief stand for no more than one hour; [S] Manhattan CB1 letter (2026) citing NYC DOT; NYC DOT relief-stand page
variables.data_source: NYC Open Data 'Taxi and For-Hire Vehicle (FHV) Relief Stands' (https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/taxi-and-for-hire-vehicle-fhv-relief-stands)
variables.how_to_model: POI layer; a break elsewhere costs parking search time or ticket risk

variables.name: Legal waiting spots (staging)
variables.description: Whether the car can legally sit still near a hotspot while waiting for the next request instead of cruising.
variables.values_or_range: Share of curb where standing is legal per zone; parking $0-15+/h [U]; NYC anti-idling limit 3 min (1 min next to schools); a taxi awaiting a fare may stand only at a taxi stand (or at a hydrant with the driver in the seat); non-taxis may not cruise for passengers [corrected by fact-check: idling limits confirmed and staging rules added]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] NYC Admin Code 24-163(a), (f); 34 RCNY 4-11(a)-(b); [S] Schaller (2017): in the Manhattan CBD, app cars had 55K passenger hours vs 37K empty hours (60% busy), and utilisation fell from 67% (taxis, 2013) to 62% (taxis and apps, 2017) [uncertain: the '11 min vs 8 min empty between trips' figures were not found in the checked excerpts]
variables.data_source: NYC DOT parking regulations; licensed garages on NYC Open Data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Per-zone wait cost (fuel, ticket risk, parking fee) vs cruise cost; agent chooses wait, cruise or reposition

variables.name: Robotaxi pickup-point placement
variables.description: A robotaxi stops only at a legal, safe point, which may be up to a block away, adding rider walk time and cancellations.
variables.values_or_range: Walk 0-200 m [design]; density of valid pickup points per km of curb
variables.impact_evidence: [design] / [U] Operator practice not verified
variables.how_to_model: Snap each request to the nearest legal curb node; walk time adds to rendezvous; cancel chance rises with walk

variables.name: Pedestrian volume by location
variables.description: How many people walk past a point; drives street-hail chances and is a proxy for latent ride demand.
variables.values_or_range: DOT counts at 114 locations (100 on-street, mainly retail corridors; 13 bridges; Hudson River Greenway), counted each May and September
variables.impact_evidence: [S] NYC Open Data dataset description (confirmed via GitHub copies: 114 locations, 100 on-street mostly retail corridors, 13 East River and Harlem River bridge points, Hudson River Greenway); Buchholz (2022, REStud): taxis are drawn to search in the most concentrated pedestrian areas [uncertain: this paraphrase of Buchholz was not checked against the paper]
variables.how_to_model: Street-hail arrival rate per edge proportional to pedestrian intensity x hour profile, calibrated to yellow pickups

variables.name: Pedestrian demand class of each street
variables.description: NYC DOT's Pedestrian Mobility Plan puts every street in one of five pedestrian-demand classes.
variables.values_or_range: Baseline (~60% of roads), Community Connector (~25%) [uncertain: shares not re-checked], Neighborhood Corridor, Regional Corridor, Global Corridor (mostly Manhattan)
variables.impact_evidence: [S] NYC DOT Pedestrian Mobility Plan and data.gov dataset (modified Mar 2026); class names confirmed in GitHub uses of the Pedestrian_Demand file; [P*] 34 RCNY 5-11 uses the plan's corridor categories; MIT critique that some outer-borough streets are under-classified
variables.how_to_model: Categorical edge attribute feeding hail rate and curb friction

variables.name: Subway entries and exits by hour
variables.description: Hourly subway ridership per station shows where crowds appear and when transit thins out, shaping first/last-mile and substitute demand.
variables.values_or_range: Hourly counts by station complex: 2017-19 (t69i-h2me), 2020-24 (wujg-7c2s), 2025+ (5wq4-mkjj); OD estimates (jsu2-fbtj) [uncertain: one GitHub project reports wujg-7c2s data starting in Feb 2022; t69i-h2me and jsu2-fbtj exist in the MTA catalog but their titles were not confirmed]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] data.ny.gov catalog entries; IDs 5wq4-mkjj (2025+) and wujg-7c2s (2020-24) confirmed by several GitHub pipelines
variables.how_to_model: Demand covariate; subway outages (R03) move demand to cars near affected stations

variables.name: Road-to-pedestrian ratio ('pickup-ability')
variables.description: The user's idea: compare how many pedestrians gather on a block with how much drivable road and stoppable curb it has; busy but curb-starved streets mean many riders but slow, congested pickups.
variables.values_or_range: Index = legal-stop curb metres / pedestrians per hour (or lanes / pedestrian class); bands low / medium / high; low examples Times Sq, SoHo
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; Buchholz (2022): competition pushes taxis to spread search beyond the densest pedestrian areas [S] [uncertain: paraphrase not checked against the paper]
variables.data_source: DOT pedestrian counts + Pedestrian Mobility Plan + LION width/lanes + DOT parking signs
variables.how_to_model: Per-edge index raises hail rate (+) and pickup dwell / lowers through-speed (-)

variables.name: Transit accessibility
variables.description: Distance from a zone to the nearest subway station; areas far from rail rely more on cars for hire.
variables.values_or_range: 0-3+ km to nearest station; transit-desert flag
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Top HVFHV pickup zones include East New York, Crown Heights North, Bushwick South (Jun 2021); [U] transit-substitution mechanism
variables.data_source: MTA GTFS static (https://new.mta.info/developers); NYC subway entrances (NYC Open Data)
variables.how_to_model: Demand covariate; raises late-night demand when subway headways lengthen

variables.name: Population and job density
variables.description: Residents and workers per zone are the base of trip generation.
variables.values_or_range: Residents/km2 and jobs/km2 per zone
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Standard trip-generation practice; Correa, Chow and Ozbay model demand from the spatial distribution of activities [S]
variables.how_to_model: Demand-generator covariates when extrapolating beyond replayed data

variables.name: Hail visibility by street type
variables.description: Street hails happen mostly on avenues and busy corridors that cabs pass often; side streets yield few hails.
variables.values_or_range: Hail multiplier: avenue 1.0, cross street 0.2-0.5 [design guess]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] / [U]; yellow records carry exact coordinates only until June 2016 (zone IDs from July 2016) [S] toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data README
variables.data_source: Pre-2016 TLC yellow records with lat/lon
variables.how_to_model: Generate hails per edge; a cruising agent only sees hails on edges it drives

variables.name: Cruising route for street hails
variables.description: For a taxi, which streets to drive while empty, trading distance (fuel, time) against passing more pedestrians.
variables.values_or_range: Route through high-hail edges vs waiting at a stand; cruise speed in traffic
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; Schaller (2017): yellow taxis average 8 min empty between trips in the Manhattan CBD [S] [uncertain: figure not found in the checked excerpts]; [P*] 34 RCNY 4-11(b): only taxis may cruise for passengers
variables.applies_to: taxi; robotaxi with street hail (none today)
variables.data_source: Pre-2016 TLC yellow coordinates for calibration [U]
variables.how_to_model: Agent picks the next edge or a loop; hails generated only on traversed edges

variables.name: Land-use mix per zone
variables.description: Share of residential, office, retail, nightlife, industrial and park land; sets the daily shape of demand.
variables.values_or_range: MapPLUTO land-use classes (11) by lot area per zone
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Share of core yellow pickups ending in outer boroughs: 1.4% at 8am vs 17.7% at 4am (Oct 2019), showing home-bound night flows
variables.how_to_model: Zone feature vector; demand time profile depends on land-use mix

variables.name: Office and business districts
variables.description: Midtown, Financial District, Hudson Yards, Downtown Brooklyn and Long Island City pull weekday daytime trips.
variables.values_or_range: Jobs per zone; weekday vs weekend ratio
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Midtown Center 4.2% and Midtown East 3.7% of all yellow pickups (Oct 2019)
variables.how_to_model: Work-hour peaks per zone (remote-work days in R02)

variables.name: Nightlife density
variables.description: Bars, clubs and late restaurants create late-night demand and longer, outbound trips.
variables.values_or_range: On-premises liquor licences per zone; key areas LES, East Village, Meatpacking, Williamsburg, Bushwick
variables.impact_evidence: [P] East Village is the #2 HVFHV pickup zone (Jun 2021); Meatpacking among the highest-tip drop-off zones (27%)
variables.data_source: NYS Liquor Authority licences (data.ny.gov) [U]; DOHMH restaurant inspections [U]
variables.how_to_model: Late-night demand multiplier; destinations drawn toward residential zones

variables.name: Tourist and hotel density
variables.description: Hotels and attractions create airport trips, taxi-stand queues and riders less likely to use transit.
variables.values_or_range: Hotel rooms per zone; attraction POIs
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Times Sq/Theatre District = 3.5% of yellow pickups (Oct 2019)
variables.data_source: OSM tourism tags; NYC hotel lists on NYC Open Data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Hotel POIs as taxi-stand queues and airport-bound demand

variables.name: Hospitals, universities and institutions
variables.description: Large hospitals produce steady trips around shift changes and discharges (plus paratransit rides); campuses shift demand with the academic calendar.
variables.values_or_range: Beds per site; shift changes ~7am / 7pm [U]; enrolment per campus, term on/off
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; [P*] HVFHV records carry access_a_ride_flag (confirmed in the Jan 2023 schema)
variables.data_source: NYS DOH health facility data (health.data.ny.gov) [U]; NCES IPEDS (campuses)
variables.how_to_model: POI with a daily time profile and seasonal multiplier (R02)

variables.name: Venues, stadiums and convention centres
variables.description: Fixed big venues whose location, capacity and exits shape event surges (the events themselves are in R03).
variables.values_or_range: Capacity 2k-50k (MSG, Barclays, Yankee Stadium, Citi Field, USTA, UBS Arena, Javits, Lincoln Center); exit curb capacity
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; MSG sits on Penn Station (zone 186, top-5 yellow pickup zone) [P]
variables.how_to_model: Venue nodes with capacity; R03 schedules events on them

variables.name: Retail and shopping corridors
variables.description: Shopping streets create daytime and weekend short trips.
variables.values_or_range: Retail floor area per zone
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; most DOT pedestrian count sites are retail corridors [S]
variables.data_source: MapPLUTO retail area; DOT pedestrian counts
variables.how_to_model: Daytime / weekend demand covariate

variables.name: Intercity rail and bus hubs
variables.description: Penn Station/Moynihan, Grand Central, Port Authority Bus Terminal, Atlantic Terminal and Jamaica produce rider pulses timed to public train and bus arrivals.
variables.values_or_range: Penn Station/Madison Sq West = 3.6% of yellow pickups, PU/DO 1.40 (Oct 2019); arrival schedules public in GTFS
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, TLC yellow Oct 2019
variables.data_source: GTFS feeds (MTA, NJ Transit, Amtrak); TLC records
variables.how_to_model: Hub nodes with arrival-driven pulses + taxi-stand queues

variables.name: Airport trip share and value
variables.description: Airport trips are few but long and lucrative.
variables.values_or_range: Yellow Oct 2019: 7.9% of trips, 22.2% of driver revenue (fare + extras + tips); JFK pickup mean $51.19 over 15.3 mi, LGA $37.81 over 9.1 mi. HVFHV Jun 2021: 5.4% of trips touch an airport
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, TLC yellow Oct 2019 and HVFHV Jun 2021
variables.how_to_model: Airport zones with their own demand profile tied to flight schedules (R03/R12)

variables.name: Airport pickup/drop-off asymmetry
variables.description: For yellow cabs airport pickups far exceed drop-offs, while app trips are roughly balanced.
variables.values_or_range: Yellow PU/DO: JFK 3.81, LGA 2.06 (Oct 2019); HVFHV: JFK 0.84, LGA 0.88 (Jun 2021)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation
variables.how_to_model: Emerges from the OD matrix; decides whether an airport drop-off can be followed by an airport pickup

variables.name: Airport holding-lot queue
variables.description: After an airport drop-off, a driver can join a lot queue for an outbound fare or deadhead back; queue length sets the expected wait.
variables.values_or_range: Yellow JFK central taxi hold: historically ~2-3 h average, up to 5 h [uncertain: wait times not re-checked]. FHV: virtual FIFO queue (JFK Cell Phone Lot / Limo Lot; LGA lot), free parking up to 3 h, place lost if offline or after repeated declines
variables.impact_evidence: [S] NBC New York (bribery case); Uber JFK driver page; Yazici, Kamga and Singhal (2016, TR-A 91:48-60): proximity is the strongest predictor of the airport-pickup decision; [P*] 35 RCNY 80-19(e)-(f): taxis queue through holding areas and feed lines (separate short- and long-haul lines at some stands); FHVs may not accept a dispatch while parked in JFK/LGA pickup areas
variables.data_source: No public queue data; infer from TLC airport drop-off and pickup times [design]
variables.how_to_model: Per-airport FIFO queue fed by flight arrivals; agent joins or leaves; app shows queue position

variables.name: Airport queue decision
variables.description: After an airport drop-off, the agent decides whether to join the airport queue, leave it, or deadhead back to the city.
variables.values_or_range: Join / skip / leave after t minutes; information: queue position (app) or lot count (taxi)
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Yazici, Kamga and Singhal (2016): NYC taxi drivers' airport-pickup decisions depend mainly on proximity, then time, weather and shift variables [uncertain: finding not re-checked against the paper; publisher hosts blocked]
variables.how_to_model: Action at airport zones; payoff = expected airport fare minus queue time vs city alternative

variables.name: Airport fare and fee triggers
variables.description: Fare rules switched on by airport geography (amounts owned by R07).
variables.values_or_range: Taxi: JFK to/from Manhattan flat $70 (+$5 weekdays 4-8pm); LGA +$5 to and from; airport access fee on JFK/LGA taxi pickups $1.25 until Mar 2023 and $1.75 from Apr 2023 (trip records), possibly $2.00 in 2026 [uncertain: 2026 amount from a code comment only]. HVFHV: $2.50 airport fee on pickups and drop-offs at JFK/LGA/EWR, already in Jan 2023 records [corrected by fact-check: the original said 'since Apr 2023'; the April 2023 change was the taxi access fee rising to $1.75]. Newark taxi trips: meter + $20 surcharge + tolls both ways [corrected by fact-check: $20 is the rule in force, not a proposal]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(2)(iii), (b), (c)(3); [P*] airport_fee values in yellow 2023-24 and HVFHV Jan 2023 records; [S] 2026 fare config quoting the TLC rate card; VisaVerge / Fox5 on the FHV fee
variables.data_source: TLC fare page; airport_fee fields in trip records
variables.how_to_model: Airport polygons trigger fare-engine branches

variables.name: Airport terminal layout and pickup rules
variables.description: Where at the airport pickups are allowed (terminal curbs, FHV zones, remote lots), adding minutes and confusion.
variables.values_or_range: JFK: FHV pickups barred at Terminals 5 and 7 'until further notice' [uncertain: from 2021-era driver guides; may be outdated], with Howard Beach FHV Hold Lot 3; arrivals-level pickups only; JFK rebuilding (New Terminal One) changes roads [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Uber JFK driver page (French version); Inshur driver guide (2021)
variables.applies_to: all; robotaxi airport access needs Port Authority approval [U]
variables.data_source: PANYNJ ground transport pages; Uber airport driver pages
variables.how_to_model: Airport sub-graph with pickup nodes per terminal and extra walk/drive time

variables.name: Newark Airport (EWR) special status
variables.description: EWR is in New Jersey: NYC drivers drop off there but almost never pick up, so each EWR drop-off implies an empty return. [corrected by fact-check: for taxis the passenger pays a $20 Newark surcharge and tolls both ways (35 RCNY 58-26(c)(3)), so the return toll is reimbursed; app drivers are paid the out-of-town rate]
variables.values_or_range: Yellow: 15,829 drop-offs vs 57 pickups (Oct 2019; 829 pickups under a lighter filter, mostly zero-distance records), rate code 3 = 0.24% of trips; HVFHV: 63,278 vs 228 (Jun 2021); return toll $14.79-16.79 E-ZPass; a taxi may refuse an EWR trip after 8 h of operation
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own counts (reproduced); [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(c)(3), 80-20(b)(8); [S] PANYNJ 2026 tolls
variables.how_to_model: EWR zone = drop-off only for NYC-licensed cars; forced deadhead; inbound toll paid by the driver for app cars and reimbursed by the passenger for taxis

variables.sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
variables.name: Out-of-city trip share
variables.description: Share of trips ending outside NYC (NJ, Westchester, Nassau, Long Island, Connecticut).
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV Jun 2021: 3.67% end outside NYC (zone 265) + 0.42% at EWR. Yellow Oct 2019: rate code 4 (Nassau/Westchester) 0.08%, negotiated (code 5) 0.17%, Newark (code 3) 0.24%
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation
variables.how_to_model: OD matrix includes external destination nodes by county

variables.sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
variables.name: Out-of-city fare and pay rules
variables.description: How trips leaving the city are priced and paid, which decides whether the empty return is compensated (amounts owned by R07).
variables.values_or_range: Yellow: meter to the city line, then double meter beyond for Westchester/Nassau, plus tolls both ways; other places negotiated flat fare. HVFHV minimum pay from 1 Mar 2026: in-city $1.283/mi + $0.681/min (non-WAV); out-of-town $1.757/mi (non-WAV), $2.193/mi (WAV), $0.725/min [uncertain: 2026 posted values not re-checked; they match the rule's base rates after yearly CPI indexing]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(c)(1)-(2), (f)(2): double meter and tolls both ways confirmed; 35 RCNY 59D-22(a): out-of-town base rates ($1.700/mi, WAV $2.122, $0.574/min) are double the in-city base and are not divided by the utilisation rate; [S] TLC driver-pay-rates page
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi; robotaxi pricing is a setting
variables.how_to_model: Fare-engine branch when the destination is outside the NYC polygon

variables.sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
variables.name: Empty-return distance and legality
variables.description: After an out-of-city drop-off the driver normally returns to NYC empty, because pickups outside the city need a local licence.
variables.values_or_range: Return 10-60+ km; street hails outside NYC not allowed; app pickups outside NYC depend on NJ / county licensing [U]; taxi passengers reimburse tolls both ways for EWR, Westchester and Nassau; taxis may refuse those trips after 8 h of operation
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Near-zero pickups at EWR and zone 265 in TLC records; [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(c), 80-20(b)(8); [U] county licensing details [corrected by fact-check: impact high -> medium; such trips are ~0.5% of yellow and ~4% of app trips and are partly compensated, though a single one can cost up to an hour]
variables.how_to_model: Compute deadhead route back to the city line or home; charge time, energy and inbound toll

variables.sub_box: Out-of-city trips and the empty return
variables.name: Night outward drift
variables.description: At night more trips leave the core for residential outer boroughs, leaving drivers far from demand.
variables.values_or_range: Share of core yellow pickups ending in outer boroughs: 1.4% at 8am, 9.5% at 10pm, 13.1% at midnight, 17.7% at 4am (Oct 2019)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, TLC yellow Oct 2019
variables.how_to_model: Emerges from hour-specific OD matrices; makes 'go home after last trip' and repositioning decisions matter

variables.name: Driver home location
variables.description: Where the driver lives, which sets the start and end commute and the 'take me home' preference.
variables.values_or_range: Zone ID sampled from a driver-residence distribution (mostly Queens, Brooklyn, Bronx; some NJ / Long Island) [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Residence distribution not verified (search budget used up)
variables.data_source: None verified; TLC licensee data if published [U]
variables.how_to_model: Home node per driver; unpaid commute at shift start and end

variables.name: Distance and time to home
variables.description: Live network distance from the car to home; near shift end it decides whether to accept a trip or use a destination filter.
variables.values_or_range: 0-40 km; destination-filter uses per day (Uber historically 2/day) [U]; taxi 'returning to garage or home' rule
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge of platform destination filters; [P*] 35 RCNY 80-19(a)(5): an off-duty taxi driver heading home or to the garage may take a passenger only if the destination is directly on the route and the trip record says 'Returning to garage (or home)' [corrected by fact-check: added the taxi go-home rule]
variables.how_to_model: Recompute each step; 'take me home' mode biases matching toward trips ending near home

variables.name: Garages, depots and shift-change points
variables.description: Yellow cab garages and robotaxi depots are where shifts start or end and cars are cleaned or charged, adding deadhead.
variables.values_or_range: Garage zone; two-shift taxis change around 4-5pm [U]; robotaxi depot locations set by scenario
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge; [design] for robotaxi depots
variables.how_to_model: Depot nodes; mandatory returns for shift change, charging or cleaning

variables.name: Fuel station locations
variables.description: Where gas stations are and the detour to reach them; Manhattan has few.
variables.values_or_range: Stations per borough; detour 0-15 min
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Background knowledge
variables.how_to_model: POI layer; refuel action routes to the nearest station

variables.name: EV charger locations, power and access
variables.description: Location, speed and availability of chargers (public, curbside, fleet-only hubs), which set detour and downtime for EVs.
variables.values_or_range: DC fast 50-350 kW; Level 2 7-19 kW; NYC DOT curbside chargers; fleet hubs
variables.impact_evidence: [S] TLC license reviews weigh EV charging availability; [U] charger mix [uncertain: TLC licence-review claim not re-checked]
variables.how_to_model: Charger POIs with ports, power and queues; charge action (R08)

variables.name: Restrooms, food and break spots
variables.description: Where a driver can take a legal break with a toilet and food, which affects break length and dead time.
variables.values_or_range: Public restroom POIs; 113 relief stands [uncertain: count not re-checked, see R01-031]; break detour 0-20 min
variables.impact_evidence: [S] WNYC 'Relief in short supply for the city's taxi drivers'; [U]
variables.data_source: NYC Parks public restrooms (NYC Open Data) [U]; OSM amenity=toilets
variables.how_to_model: Break action needs a nearby POI; cost = detour + dwell

variables.name: Neighbourhood income
variables.description: Median household income of pickup and drop-off areas, which tracks card use, trip length and tipping.
variables.values_or_range: ACS median income per tract mapped to zone; card-trip tip/fare 25.9% for Yellow Zone pickups vs 19.3% outer boroughs; lowest drop-off zones 18.8-19.2% (Stuyvesant Heights, Central Harlem North, Crown Heights North) vs ~27% (UES, UWS, West Village)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation, yellow Oct 2019 card trips (tips are recorded only for card payments); reproduced, and robust alternatives give the same gap (tip/fare ratio of sums 23.9% vs 17.9%; medians 26.3% vs 22.2%)
variables.data_source: US Census ACS; TLC tips (yellow card trips; HVFHV tips column)
variables.how_to_model: Zone covariate for tip probability and size (behaviour owned by R05)

variables.name: Payment mix by zone
variables.description: Share of cash vs card trips by area; affects recorded tips and cash handling for taxis (app trips are cashless).
variables.values_or_range: Card share, yellow Oct 2019: Yellow Zone 74.2%, upper Manhattan 58.8%, outer boroughs 51.7%, airports 64.7%
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Own computation
variables.how_to_model: Per-zone payment-type probability

variables.name: Perceived safety and crime
variables.description: Crime and drivers' sense of risk make some drivers avoid areas at night, thinning supply there and raising surge for those who stay, with a small real incident risk.
variables.values_or_range: Complaints per 1,000 residents by precinct and hour; avoidance probability 0-1 [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] / [design]; benchmark must not reward illegal refusal
variables.how_to_model: Lower competitor supply in high-perceived-risk zones at night; small incident probability

variables.name: Geographic refusal rules
variables.description: Taxis must take passengers to any destination in the city, Westchester, Nassau or Newark Airport and may not ask the destination before the rider is seated, so the agent cannot legally refuse by neighbourhood; app drivers can decline but acceptance rate counts against them.
variables.values_or_range: Taxi refusal = mandatory penalty under 35 RCNY 80-02(e) (about $500 for a first offence [S]); allowed refusals include more than 8 h of operation for EWR/Westchester/Nassau trips; app accept/decline with destination shown [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-20(a)(1), (a)(4), (b) [corrected by fact-check: the rule also covers Westchester, Nassau and Newark; tag upgraded from U]
variables.how_to_model: Block destination-based refusal for taxis; track acceptance for app drivers (R06/R07)

variables.sub_box: A. Clock, calendar and day types
variables.name: Simulation clock and hour-of-week key
variables.description: The local wall-clock time (America/New_York) that every other profile is looked up by, stored as date, minute and a 168-slot hour-of-week index.
variables.values_or_range: 1-minute resolution; 168 hour-of-week slots; 365/366 calendar days; time zone UTC-5/UTC-4
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023: same-city demand ranges 4,892 to 48,069 trips/hour depending only on hour and weekday
variables.data_source: None needed (derived); profiles from NYC TLC trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
variables.how_to_model: Global clock object; every generator queries rate(slot, day_type, month) multipliers

variables.sub_box: A. Clock, calendar and day types
variables.name: Day-type classification
variables.description: The category a calendar date falls into, which selects the demand, speed and rule profile for that day.
variables.values_or_range: Mon, Tue-Thu, Fri, Sat, Sun, federal holiday, bridge day, major-event day, DST day
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023: holidays run at 0.45-0.90 of a normal same-weekday, bridge days 0.56-0.79
variables.data_source: US federal holiday list (OPM), https://www.opm.gov/policy-data-oversight/pay-leave/federal-holidays/ ; NYC DOE calendar
variables.how_to_model: Lookup table date -> day_type; profiles fitted per day_type from TLC history

variables.sub_box: A. Clock, calendar and day types
variables.name: Scenario replay date
variables.description: Which real calendar date (or synthetic typical day) an episode replays, chosen by the benchmark designer.
variables.values_or_range: Ordinary weekday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, holiday, event day; or synthetic median day
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023: Christmas 2023 had 45% of a normal Monday's yellow trips; NYE night pays +60% per engaged hour [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Harness picks dates from a stratified day-type list; same date and seed across models (common random numbers)

variables.sub_box: A. Clock, calendar and day types
variables.name: Working-hours choice
variables.description: The agent's choice of when to start and stop driving and how many hours to work (human driver), or how many cars to keep online per hour (fleet).
variables.values_or_range: Start 00:00-23:59; shift 1-12 h; per-hour online fleet share 0-100%
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023: pay per engaged hour ranges $49.7 (weekday 4 pm) to $64.4 (weekday 4 am), demand 4.9k-37.7k/hour; Chen et al. 2019 show Uber drivers' value from choosing hours [U] [uncertain: Chen, Chevalier, Rossi and Oehlsen, J. Political Economy 2019, not re-read this session]
variables.how_to_model: Agent action go_online/go_offline; harness scores profit per online hour and per calendar day

variables.sub_box: A. Clock, calendar and day types
variables.name: Calendar awareness given to the agent
variables.description: Whether the agent is told the date, weekday, holiday name and known calendar effects, as an experiment arm like event awareness.
variables.values_or_range: None / weekday+hour only / full calendar incl. holidays / calendar plus historical hourly profile
variables.impact_evidence: [design] mirrors the team's with/without event-info test; holiday and weekday effects of 0.45-1.11x shown in TLC data
variables.how_to_model: System-prompt variants; same world, different information

variables.name: Weekday hourly demand curve
variables.description: The number of ride requests per hour on an ordinary Monday-Friday, shaped by commuting and evening activity.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV citywide trips/hour: 03h 4,892; 08h 36,283; 12h 23,630; 18h 37,694; 23h 25,607 (peak/trough 7.7x). Yellow: 03h 274 vs 18h 7,534 (27x)
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [P*] own calc yellow Jan 2023
variables.how_to_model: Non-homogeneous Poisson arrivals per zone with rate = base(zone) x hour-of-week profile x day-type x month

variables.name: Weekend hourly demand curve
variables.description: The hourly shape on Saturday and Sunday, with late mornings, strong evenings and Friday/Saturday nights running into the next morning.
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
variables.how_to_model: Separate Sat and Sun profiles; the 00-04h of Sat/Sun belong to the previous evening

variables.name: Morning rush
variables.description: The 7-10 am commuter peak, with short Manhattan-bound trips, slow traffic and the longest rider waits of a weekday.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV 08h 36.3k trips/h; median request-to-pickup 5.0 min at 07h (vs 3.3 at 10h); 14 mph
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
variables.how_to_model: Profile peak plus commute-direction bias (outer boroughs to Midtown/FiDi) in the OD matrix

variables.name: Lunch hour (rider demand)
variables.description: Midday trips around the average lunch time; small in ride-hail because most lunch trips are walked.
variables.values_or_range: Midtown+FiDi weekday pickups per 15 min: 590-613 at 10:00-10:45, 681-696 at 11:30-12:00 (about +12%), dip 12:30-12:45 [corrected by fact-check: 571-613 at 10:00-10:45; pickups recover to 664-700 at 13:00-13:45, so most of the +12% is the late-morning ramp and the lunch-specific bump is under 5%]; lunch typically 12:00-13:00, 30-60 min [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; ATUS eating-time pattern not verified this session [U]
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; BLS American Time Use Survey, https://www.bls.gov/tus/
variables.how_to_model: Small Gaussian bump centred 11:45 on business-zone pickups; slower midday speeds come from R10

variables.name: Evening rush
variables.description: The 4-8 pm peak when offices empty, the highest weekday volume but the slowest traffic and lowest pay per engaged hour.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV 17-18h 35-38k trips/h; 12.3 mph; $49.7-49.9 per engaged hour; yellow adds $2.50 surcharge [corrected by fact-check: 12.3 mph is 17h only (18h 13.3 mph); $49.7-49.9 is 16-17h, 18h pays $52.4]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [P*] surcharge visible in yellow 'extra' field
variables.how_to_model: Profile peak plus outbound OD bias; couples with R10 speed curve

variables.name: Dinner and evening out
variables.description: The 7-10 pm leisure wave of restaurant, show and social trips, stronger Thursday-Saturday.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV weekday 19-21h 31-36k trips/h; Sat 19h 48.1k; trip length rises from 4.1 to 5.2 mi after 8 pm
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
variables.how_to_model: Leisure-purpose demand layer by hour and day with nightlife/restaurant zone weights

variables.name: Late-night nightlife demand
variables.description: Thursday-Saturday 10 pm-3 am demand from bars, clubs and parties, concentrated in a few neighbourhoods.
variables.values_or_range: Nightlife zones (East Village, LES, West/Greenwich Village, Williamsburg etc.) 1,680-1,920 pickups per 15 min at midnight Sat/Sun vs 456 on weekdays; HVFHV 21-24h: Sat 133k, Fri 120k, Mon 64k
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
variables.how_to_model: Zone-specific late-night multipliers by weekday; waits rise (Sat 23h median 5.2 min)

variables.name: Bar-closing taper
variables.description: The end-of-night exit when bars close (4 am in NYC; 2 am in many US cities), which in NYC tapers smoothly rather than spiking.
variables.values_or_range: NYC nightlife pickups fall steadily from 1,700/15 min at 01:00 to 590 at 04:00 and 222 at 05:00 (Sat); no spike at 04:00. Close time 04:00 NYC; 02:00 elsewhere [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023 (re-computed: 1,699 at 01:00, 992 at 03:00, 591 at 04:00, 222 at 05:00); NY on-premises closing 4 am [U] [uncertain: NY Alcoholic Beverage Control Law hours not read this session] [corrected by fact-check: was medium; in NYC the taper is already inside the late-night curve (R02-012) and has no closing spike, as the dossier summary itself says; medium only for a 2 am city]
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; NY State Liquor Authority hours rules
variables.how_to_model: Exponential decay after 01:00 in nightlife zones; for 2 am cities add a closing pulse

variables.name: Dead hours (03-05 am)
variables.description: The overnight trough when demand is lowest but trips are long, fast and airport-heavy.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV weekday 03h 4,892 trips/h; 04h avg 7.2 mi, 25 mph, $64.4 per engaged hour, 28.6% of trips go to airports; yellow 274/h
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
variables.how_to_model: Low arrival rate with OD skewed to JFK/LGA/EWR; idle time dominates the agent's hourly profit

variables.name: Sector-specific hourly shape
variables.description: The yellow taxi and app-ride markets have different hourly and weekly shapes, so a taxi agent and an app agent face different best hours.
variables.values_or_range: Yellow-to-HVFHV trip ratio 0.23 at noon falling to 0.175 at 8 pm; yellow busiest day Thursday, HVFHV busiest Saturday
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023 and yellow Jan 2023
variables.how_to_model: Fit profiles per sector (street hail vs e-hail) rather than one shared curve

variables.sub_box: C. Hour-of-day trip quality and the driver's day
variables.name: Hourly speed profile
variables.description: Average vehicle speed by hour, which sets trips per hour and how per-minute versus per-mile pay adds up.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV citywide weekday: 25.0 mph at 04h, 12.3 mph at 17h; yellow (Manhattan-heavy): 24.7 mph 04h, 11.5 mph 08h
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023; [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
variables.data_source: NYC TLC trip records, https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; NYC DOT traffic speeds, https://data.cityofnewyork.us/
variables.how_to_model: Time-dependent link speeds (R10) indexed by hour-of-week, day-type and month

variables.sub_box: C. Hour-of-day trip quality and the driver's day
variables.name: Hourly trip length and destination mix
variables.description: How long trips are and where they go changes by hour (commutes, airport runs, outer-borough returns).
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV weekday avg trip 4.1 mi at 18h vs 7.2 mi at 04h; airport drop-off share 28.6% at 04h vs 0.3% at 23h; airport pickup share 8.2% at 00h
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC HVFHV Jan 2023
