variables.how_to_model: Rule engine adds by pickup time

variables.name: Taxi weekday rush surcharges
variables.description: Fixed surcharges on yellow/green trips in the weekday 4-8 pm peak, including on the JFK flat fare.
variables.values_or_range: $2.50 metered 16:00-20:00 Mon-Fri excl. legal holidays; JFK flat fare $70 + $5 rush 16-20h weekdays
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] yellow 2023/2024 'extra' and RatecodeID 2 fare $70 + $5 at 16-19h; TLC fare page [S] [upgraded by fact-check: 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(2)(i) and (b)(1) read via verbatim copy [P*]]
variables.how_to_model: Rule engine by pickup time and day_type

variables.name: Congestion Relief Zone toll time bands
variables.description: The Manhattan congestion toll costs less overnight; taxi and app trips instead pay a flat per-trip charge at all hours.
variables.values_or_range: Peak 05-21h weekdays, 09-21h weekends; overnight 75% lower (car E-ZPass $9 peak, $2.25 overnight [U]) [upgraded by fact-check to S: ABC7 via R01 gives $9 peak in 2025-27, rising to $12 in 2028-30 and $15 in 2031, $2.25 overnight]; per trip $0.75 taxi/green, $1.50 HVFHV, all hours [S]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] MTA CRZ pages and TLC Industry Notice 24-10 via search snippets
variables.how_to_model: Toll by entry time for private vehicles (traffic level, R10); per-trip charge passed to rider (R07)

variables.name: Time-of-use electricity price
variables.description: EV charging costs depend on the hour, cheapest overnight, which shapes when EVs and robotaxis should charge.
variables.values_or_range: Off-peak roughly 00:00-08:00; summer weekday afternoons most expensive; DC fast-charging prices may also vary by hour [U] [uncertain: Con Edison tariff pages unreachable (DNS blocked)]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Con Edison TOU tariff not read this session; cross-link R08
variables.data_source: Con Edison time-of-use rates, https://www.coned.com/en/accounts-billing/your-bill/time-of-use ; AFDC stations, https://afdc.energy.gov/
variables.how_to_model: Price per kWh by hour-of-week in the energy model

variables.name: Curb and bus-lane time windows
variables.description: Kerbside and bus-lane rules change by hour, limiting where a car may stop or wait at peak times.
variables.values_or_range: Typical 'No Standing 7-10 am / 4-7 pm' on avenues; bus-lane camera hours vary (peak only to 24/7) [U] [uncertain: NYC DOT regulation data not read]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] not measured; cross-link R01/R07
variables.data_source: NYC DOT parking regulations (NYC Open Data), https://data.cityofnewyork.us/
variables.how_to_model: Time-windowed curb attributes on links; fines if agent stops illegally

variables.name: Platform log-in limits and scheduled hours
variables.description: In NYC, app platforms may stop drivers going online in low-demand hours and let higher-tier drivers book hours ahead.
variables.values_or_range: Online allowed / blocked by hour and zone; pre-booked slots by tier [U] [corrected by fact-check: since 1 Aug 2025, 35 RCNY 59D-22(c) requires an HVFHV to give 72 hours' notice before restricting a driver's access on a calendar day, and to let a driver who has logged on stay available for at least 16 hours (restarting after 8 h off), with a $500 fine per violation [P*]; so 2025-26 replays need day-level, pre-announced lockouts, while 2023-24 replays should allow hour-by-hour lockouts, reported as near-constant in 2024 [S]]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] reported since 2022-23 in response to TLC utilization-based pay; not verified this session; cross-link R07 [fact-check: lockouts widespread in 2024 per Bloomberg (10 Oct 2024) via a secondary summary, and Uber paused them in Sep 2024 [S]; rule text 59D-22(c) [P*]; high for 2023-24 replays, lower after Aug 2025]
variables.how_to_model: Platform admission rule: online request accepted if hour-zone utilization above threshold or slot booked

variables.name: Hours-of-service caps
variables.description: Rules and app policies cap how long a driver may work in a rolling window.
variables.values_or_range: TLC: about 10 h passenger time per 24 h and 60 h per week [U]; Uber app: 12 h online then 6 h offline [U] [fact-check: confirmed in 35 RCNY 80-14(f): at most 10 h carrying passengers in any 24 h (the count resets after 8 consecutive hours without passengers) and 60 h in a Monday-Sunday week; a trip begun before the limit is a defence; fines $50-400 by hours over [P*]; Uber 12 h/6 h per TechCrunch Feb 2018 via R09 [S]]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] verify current TLC fatigue rule; cross-link R09 [upgraded by fact-check: rule text read via verbatim copy [P*]]
variables.how_to_model: Rolling-window counters force offline time

variables.name: Robotaxi operating-hours window
variables.description: Robotaxi services may be allowed only in certain hours (night-only launches, daytime-only testing), as part of their operating design domain.
variables.values_or_range: 24/7, night-only (e.g. 22:00-05:30), or daytime-only; NYC testing with safety driver only [U] [corrected by fact-check: 34 RCNY 4-17(d)(4) requires a trained test operator in the driver's seat and the permit application must state hours of operation [P*]; Waymo's NYC test permit (Aug 2025, 8 cars, no riders) expired 31 Mar 2026 [S, via R06/R07], so NYC has no robotaxi service and its hours are a counterfactual setting]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Cruise SF 2022 night-only launch, Waymo 24/7 in Phoenix/SF; not verified this session [uncertain: CPUC permit pages unreachable]
variables.data_source: CPUC AV deployment reports, https://www.cpuc.ca.gov/ ; NYC DOT AV permits
variables.how_to_model: Fleet availability mask by hour-of-week

variables.name: Fleet off-peak charging and maintenance window
variables.description: When the fleet takes cars offline to charge, clean and inspect, ideally in demand troughs.
variables.values_or_range: 0-100% of fleet offline per hour; trough 03-06h weekdays, 05-08h weekends
variables.impact_evidence: [design] from TLC trough timing [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Fleet action schedule; depot capacity constraint; charging cost from TOU price

variables.sub_box: J. Daylight, DST and time handling
variables.name: Sunrise, sunset and darkness
variables.description: Day length and the time of dusk, which change through the year and drive lighting, prayer times and perhaps some mode choice.
variables.values_or_range: NYC sunset 16:28 (8 Dec) to 20:30 (21 Jun); daylight 9.2-15.1 h; darkness effect on demand undetected (17-19h share -1% after both DST shifts)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] astral/NOAA solar calc; [P*] own calc yellow 2023 DST test
variables.how_to_model: Compute sun position per minute; feed lighting, Ramadan and Sabbath windows

variables.sub_box: J. Daylight, DST and time handling
variables.name: DST transition days
variables.description: Clocks jump forward in March (23-h day) and back in November (25-h day), shifting late-night demand in clock time.
variables.values_or_range: Spring 2023: no 02h; 03h yellow trips 4,267 vs ~2,300 normal (1.8x); Fall: 01h 8,435 (two hours) vs 5,400-6,000; 02h 2,217 vs 4,000-5,300
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
variables.how_to_model: Run the clock in UTC, convert to local for profiles; nightlife demand follows body time across the switch

variables.sub_box: J. Daylight, DST and time handling
variables.name: TLC timestamp and DST artefacts
variables.description: TLC timestamps are local time without zone, so DST nights create impossible or inflated durations that must be cleaned before calibration.
variables.values_or_range: Fall-back night 2023: 795 of 8,435 trips at 01h with zero/negative duration; spring: 992 trips starting 01h with ~84 min mean duration inflated by the skipped hour [added by fact-check: the yellow 2023 file, whose SHA-256 matches TLC's, is missing about 95% of trips from about 13:00 on 21 Sep to 24 Sep 2023 (4,633-5,732 trips/day vs about 105,000); flag or drop these days]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, TLC yellow 2023
variables.how_to_model: Localize with tz rules, flag ambiguous hour, drop or repair durations before fitting

variables.sub_box: J. Daylight, DST and time handling
variables.name: Data release lag and contamination
variables.description: TLC posts data about two months after the month ends, and models may already know past dates, which matters for fair 'public info only' tests.
variables.values_or_range: Lag ~2 months [U] [uncertain: TLC page unreachable; the checksum catalog lists files to Aug 2026, consistent with a lag of about two months]; replay dates before vs after model knowledge cutoff
variables.impact_evidence: [U] lag per repo catalog note; [design] contamination concern
variables.how_to_model: Tag each replay date relative to each model's cutoff; optionally shift dates or perturb

variables.sub_box: J. Daylight, DST and time handling
variables.name: Simulation tick granularity
variables.description: The length of one simulation step, which limits how precisely the agent can time pulses like let-outs.
variables.values_or_range: 1 min recommended; 5 or 15 min coarser; pulses last 15-30 min [corrected by fact-check: in zone 230 let-out pickups stay raised for about 45-60 min at 15-min resolution, peaking about 30 min after onset]
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; let-out spikes last 15-30 min in zone 230 data [P*] [corrected by fact-check: 45-60 min]
variables.how_to_model: Event-driven or 1-minute ticks; agent decision every N minutes

variables.sub_box: J. Daylight, DST and time handling
variables.name: Episode day boundary
variables.description: Where one simulated day ends and the next begins; cutting at midnight splits Saturday night.
variables.values_or_range: Boundary at 04:00-05:00 (demand trough) recommended vs 00:00
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; HVFHV trough at 03-05h while Sun 00-01h still carries 41k and 33k trips/h of Saturday night [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Day runs 05:00 to 04:59 next day; multi-day episodes chain days

variables.sub_box: J. Daylight, DST and time handling
variables.name: Time compression and day-night lighting
variables.description: How fast simulated time runs in the live map and how lighting follows the sun for the social-media visualisation.
variables.values_or_range: Speed-up 60x-1440x; lighting from sun elevation (civil dusk to dawn)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] from team visualisation notes
variables.how_to_model: Renderer maps sim clock to frame time; sky colour from sun elevation

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Event catalogue for the scenario day
variables.description: The list of planned events active on the simulated day, each with type, venue, start, end, attendance and closure footprint.
variables.values_or_range: Typical NYC evening: ~30-40 Broadway shows, 0-3 arena or stadium events, 0-2 conventions, dozens of permitted street events on weekends; peak days (NYE, Marathon, UNGA) add a citywide event [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, 2023 yellow trips: event days move venue-zone pickups from 0x normal (Times Sq after 17:00 on NYE) to 15x normal (Flushing Meadows during the US Open)
variables.data_source: NYC Permitted Event Information (NYC Open Data tvpp-9vvx, next month only) and NYC Permitted Event Information - Historical (bkfu-528j, approved events from 2008) for replay dates [corrected by fact-check: tvpp-9vvx lists only approved events 'within the next month', so past scenario days need bkfu-528j; IDs and descriptions read from verbatim copies of the Socrata metadata, P*]; plus venue and league schedules (see R03-061)
variables.how_to_model: Load event objects per scenario date; each adds arrival and let-out demand, closures and speed effects through the variables below

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Venue registry and zone mapping
variables.description: Fixed table of venues with location, taxi zone, capacity, pickup and drop-off nodes and taxi stands.
variables.values_or_range: MSG/Penn zone 186 (~19-21k); Yankee Stadium zone 247 (46.5k); Citi Field and USTA tennis centre zone 93 (~42k; Ashe ~24k); Javits zone 246; Broadway zone 230 (~40 theatres); Randalls Island zone 194; Barclays zone 181 (Park Slope), at the corner with 189 (Prospect Heights) and 97 (Fort Greene) [corrected by fact-check: originally 'zone 25 or 189 (verify)'; point-in-polygon test on a GitHub copy of the TLC zone GeoJSON, S]; outside NYC: MetLife, UBS Arena, Prudential Center (zone 265). Capacities [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: Yankee night games lift zone-247 drop-offs 16-20h 4.7x (34.1 vs 7.2 per day) [corrected by fact-check: originally 4.5x (31.9 vs 7.1); the Sep 21-24 data-gap days are now excluded]; Mets and US Open lift zone 93, confirming the zone mapping
variables.data_source: TLC taxi zone shapefile (NYC Open Data 755u-8jsi); OpenStreetMap venue polygons
variables.how_to_model: Geocode each venue to a road node and taxi zone; attach capacity, pickup lot node and taxi stand

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Broadway curtain and let-out pattern
variables.description: Weekly theatre schedule that creates evening and matinee let-out waves around Times Square.
variables.values_or_range: Tue 7pm curtain (let-out ~21:30); Wed and Thu a mix of 7pm and 8pm curtains; Fri-Sat 8pm (let-out ~22:30-22:45); matinees Wed and Sat 2pm (let-out ~16:30), Sun mostly 3pm (let-out ~17:30); most theatres dark on Monday [corrected by fact-check: originally 'Wed-Sat 8pm' and 'Sun 2pm'; own 2023 zone-230 15-min counts show a 21:30 peak on Thursdays (84 vs 57 on Mondays) as on Tuesdays, both 21:30 and 22:30-22:45 peaks on Wednesdays, and a Sunday bump at 17:30 (63 vs 47 at 17:15), P*; evening curtains 'typically 7pm or 8pm', S]; ~12M admissions a season [uncertain: about 12.3M in 2022-23 and 2023-24 from memory, and 2024-25 reportedly a record of about 14.7M; not re-checkable this session]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc, zone 230 yellow pickups 22:00-23:00 in 2023: Mon 177/day vs Tue 270, Wed 331, Fri 298, Sat 285, Sun 129; Tuesday peak moves to 21:30 (88 vs 57 per 15 min on Mondays)
variables.data_source: Broadway League weekly grosses and attendance (broadwayleague.com); show schedules (Playbill, IBDB) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Recurring weekly event set per theatre with a let-out distribution; scale by the week's reported attendance

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Pro sports home schedules
variables.description: Home games of New York teams, which create arrival and let-out waves at stadiums and arenas, including playoff games whose dates are uncertain.
variables.values_or_range: MLB Yankees and Mets: 81 home games each (2023: 63% and 69% at night); NBA Knicks and Nets, NHL Rangers ~41 each; Islanders at UBS Arena; NFL Giants and Jets at MetLife (NJ); MLS, WNBA; playoffs add home dates, and games 5-7 of a series are 'if necessary' and confirmed only 1-2 days ahead [corrected by fact-check: '0-11' had no basis; under current formats a team can host up to 14 MLB postseason games (Wild Card 3, Division Series 3, LCS 4, World Series 4) and up to 16 NBA or NHL playoff games, U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Retrosheet 2023 game logs + own calc: yellow drop-offs near Yankee Stadium 8.4 per 10k attendees on night games (Mets 4.9); corr(attendance, drop-offs) 0.53 for the Yankees [corrected by fact-check: originally 8.1 and 0.52, with two data-gap night games included]
variables.data_source: Retrosheet game logs (github.com/chadwickbureau/retrosheet); MLB Stats API, NBA and NHL schedule feeds [U]
variables.how_to_model: Import per-date games with start time, attendance and duration; generate waves through R03-011 to R03-016

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Multi-session tournaments (US Open tennis)
variables.description: Two-week events with day and night sessions every day, giving repeated arrival waves and late-night let-outs.
variables.values_or_range: US Open: late Aug to early Sep, 14 days (2023: Aug 28-Sep 10) [uncertain: from 2025 the main draw reportedly starts on a Sunday, giving 15 days; not re-checkable this session]; day session ~11:00, night session ~19:00; night matches often end after midnight [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc 2023: Flushing Meadows (zone 93) yellow pickups 188.7/day vs 12.5 on other days (15x); 21-24h 29x; 0-2h pickups up to 162 a night vs 0.7; these trips average 10.0 mi and a $45 fare
variables.how_to_model: Daily two-session event with a heavy-tailed end time for the night session

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Conventions and trade shows (Javits)
variables.description: Multi-day exhibitions that add morning arrivals and evening departures at the convention centre, plus hotel and airport trips.
variables.values_or_range: NY Comic Con ~200k over 4 days [U]; Auto Show 10 days; 100+ events a year at Javits [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc 2023 zone 246: Comic Con (Oct 12-15) drop-offs 7-13h 1.97x and pickups 16-21h 1.39x the same weekdays a week before and after; Auto Show (Apr 7-16) pickups 1.22x
variables.how_to_model: Daily open and close times with attendance and a business-traveller price profile

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Concerts and music festivals
variables.description: One-off or multi-day concerts and festivals at arenas, parks and islands, mostly with young, transit-heavy crowds.
variables.values_or_range: Arena shows 15-20k; park festivals 30-60k a day (Governors Ball, Electric Zoo) [U]; stadium shows 50-80k
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc 2023: Electric Zoo (Randalls Island, zone 194) drop-offs 12-22h 45-48 vs 5-8 on normal days; Governors Ball (zone 93) 1.85x; yellow taxis carry only a small share of these crowds
variables.data_source: Ticketmaster Discovery API, SeatGeek API, setlist.fm (history) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Event objects with an audience profile (young, transit-heavy) that gives a low car share

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: New Year's Eve in Times Square
variables.description: The year's biggest single night: an afternoon-to-midnight frozen zone around Times Square, then a citywide after-midnight spike.
variables.values_or_range: Times Sq vehicle access restricted from late morning on Dec 31 until after midnight [corrected by fact-check: originally 'closed to cars from ~16:00-17:00'; own data show zone-230 pickups already 75-86% below a normal Sunday from 12:00 (37-66 vs 238-277 an hour), 10 at 16:00 and zero from 17:00, P*; official closure times U]; citywide demand 1.4-3x normal 00:00-04:00; app prices ~1.8x
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: zone 230 yellow pickups fell to 0 from 17:00 on Dec 31 2023 (normal Sunday ~240/h); Jan 1 2024 0-4h citywide yellow pickups 1.4-3.2x, fare per trip $19.80 vs $15.80; HVFHV Jan 1 2023 1-3h fare per mile 7.97-8.40 vs 4.49-4.58, driver pay $97-101 vs $60-61 per engaged hour, waits 8.3-8.7 vs 4.7-4.9 min [corrected by fact-check: 8.40 vs 4.58 was the 01:00 hour only; re-run on the HVFHV file reproduced the rest]
variables.data_source: TLC trip records; NYPD and NYC DOT closure notices [U]
variables.how_to_model: Scripted closure polygon plus a citywide demand and surge multiplier after 00:00

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Commencements and move-in days
variables.description: University graduations at large venues and dorm move-in days that add family groups with luggage.
variables.values_or_range: May-June graduations at Yankee Stadium, MSG, Barclays, Radio City; late-August move-in; 1-5 days a year per venue [U] [uncertain: not re-checkable this session; web search budget used up and source hosts blocked]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] recurring venue and university calendars; not measured here
variables.how_to_model: Small daytime events with high XL and luggage share

variables.sub_box: Venue events and the event calendar
variables.name: Events outside the city boundary
variables.description: Large events just outside NYC (MetLife, UBS Arena, Prudential Center, Belmont Park [uncertain: the Belmont Stakes was run at Saratoga in 2024 and 2025 while Belmont Park was rebuilt; check the scenario year]) whose trips cross licence borders, so drivers drop off but rarely pick up there.
variables.values_or_range: MetLife 82.5k; UBS Arena ~17k [U]; yellow and green taxis cannot take street hails outside NYC, and Newark airport is drop-off-only for NYC cars (R01); whether NYC-licensed app drivers may accept app requests in NJ or Nassau depends on those jurisdictions' rules [corrected by fact-check: originally 'NYC-licensed app cars generally cannot take street pickups outside the city'; app cars never take street hails, so the limit is on app dispatch, which is uncertain: not re-checkable this session]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: the Taylor Swift MetLife weekend (May 26-28 2023) left yellow drop-offs outside NYC unchanged (ratio 1.00), so taxis capture almost none of it; app share not measured
variables.how_to_model: External event that creates outbound trips and only app-dispatched return trips; charge the empty return

variables.name: Attendance
variables.description: Number of people at an event, the main scale factor for event demand.
variables.values_or_range: Yankees 2023 mean 40,863 (sd 4,180; 30.7k-47.3k); Mets 32,994 (sd 6,141); arenas 15-21k; Broadway ~0.6-1.9k a theatre [corrected by fact-check: originally 1-1.9k; a Broadway house has 500 or more seats by definition and the smallest have about 600, U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Retrosheet 2023 game logs; corr(attendance, yellow drop-offs) 0.53 Yankees (0.52 with the two data-gap games) and 0.27 Mets [P*]
variables.data_source: Retrosheet game logs; league box scores; Broadway League grosses [U]
variables.how_to_model: Event demand = attendance x car share x trips per party; capacity is public, realised attendance is sampled

variables.name: Start time and arrival spread
variables.description: Scheduled start and how arrivals spread before it, creating trips into the venue.
variables.values_or_range: Arrivals from T-120 to T+20 min, peak about T-45 [design]; MLB night games 19:05-19:10; Broadway 19:00 or 20:00
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: Yankee night-game drop-offs concentrated 16-20h (34.1 vs 7.2) [corrected by fact-check: originally 31.9 vs 7.1, with data-gap days included]; Comic Con drop-offs 7-13h 2x
variables.how_to_model: Sample arrival trips from a beta distribution ahead of start, with origins from the audience origin map

variables.name: Event duration and end-time uncertainty
variables.description: How long an event runs and how predictable its end is, which decides when let-out demand appears.
variables.values_or_range: MLB 2023 mean 162 min, sd 19.7 (Yankees 162 +/- 18, p10-p90 143-186; 16.5% over 180 min; 6-9% extra innings); Broadway +/- 5 min [U]; NBA ~135 +/- 15 min [U]; concerts end by ~23:00 curfew [U]; tennis night sessions open-ended
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Retrosheet 2023 durations (first pitch-clock season); [P*] US Open after-midnight pickups
variables.data_source: Retrosheet game logs; live score feeds [U]
variables.how_to_model: Sample end = start + duration from an event-type distribution; reveal live progress (score feed) only at higher information levels

variables.name: Early leavers and blowouts
variables.description: Share of attendees who leave before the end, which spreads the let-out wave earlier.
variables.values_or_range: 5-30% depending on score margin, weather and last trains [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] no public measure; visible as early pickups in TLC 15-minute data
variables.how_to_model: Shift a fraction of let-out demand to the 30 min before the realised end

variables.name: Let-out wave shape
variables.description: How fast post-event demand rises and decays near the venue.
variables.values_or_range: Peak 15-30 min after the end; back near normal 60-75 min after
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc HVFHV Jan 2023 zone 186 (MSG/Penn): on the busiest fifth of nights pickups peak at 22:00 with 131 per 15 min vs 53 on quiet nights, down to 69 by 23:15
variables.data_source: TLC HVFHV trip records (request and pickup times)
variables.how_to_model: Gamma-kernel or Hawkes burst triggered at the realised end time

variables.name: Audience car-for-hire mode share
variables.description: Fraction of attendees who take a taxi or app ride, which depends on transit access and audience.
variables.values_or_range: Yellow taxis: ~3-7 extra drop-offs per 10k attendees at the ballparks [corrected by fact-check: originally ~2.5-6; recomputed 6.6 (Yankees) and 2.9 (Mets) above non-game baselines of 7.2 and 6.4 a night]; app share 2-10% at Manhattan venues, 10-30% at transit-poor venues [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc 2023: 8.4 (Yankees) and 4.9 (Mets) yellow drop-offs per 10k attendees, including non-game baselines of 7.2 and 6.4 a night [corrected by fact-check: originally 8.1 and '~7'; US Open fortnight and data-gap days removed]; app share not yet measured [design]
variables.data_source: TLC yellow and HVFHV records joined to event calendars
variables.how_to_model: Venue x audience coefficient; calibrate from HVFHV residuals on event nights

variables.name: Audience price sensitivity and income
variables.description: How willing an event crowd is to pay surge prices and wait, by audience type.
variables.values_or_range: Low sensitivity: Broadway, US Open, conventions (tourists, expense accounts); high: EDM festivals, students, outer-borough fans [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc HVFHV Jan 2023: Times Sq night volume rose together with fare per mile (corr 0.76; +42% on the busiest nights), so riders kept booking at higher prices; segment values [design]
variables.how_to_model: Per-event elasticity applied to surge acceptance and cancellation

variables.name: Event-crowd destinations and trip value
variables.description: Where event leavers go, and so how long and lucrative their trips are.
variables.values_or_range: US Open leavers: 10.0 mi average, $45 fare; MSG leavers partly to Penn Station rail; ballparks to Manhattan and the suburbs
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: 2023 US Open zone-93 pickups; HVFHV zone 186 busiest nights 5.8 mi vs 5.0 mi on quiet nights
variables.how_to_model: Per-venue destination distribution fitted from TLC OD on event nights

variables.name: Post-event group size and rider state
variables.description: Groups, intoxication and mess risk among event riders.
variables.values_or_range: 2-4 riders a trip; more XL requests; mess and cancellation risk 2-3x on late nights [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; cross-link R05 (party size) and R09-046 (mess events)
variables.how_to_model: Event riders draw from a separate group-size and incident profile

variables.name: Event cancellation and postponement
variables.description: Chance that a scheduled event is cancelled, postponed or delayed, which strands drivers who moved there.
variables.values_or_range: 1-3% per outdoor event, higher with storms [design]; MLB rain delays 30-120 min [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc: Electric Zoo day 1 (Fri Sep 1 2023) was cancelled the day before; drop-offs were 7 vs 45-48 on Sep 2-3 [uncertain: the cancellation and its timing are background knowledge; the trip data confirm only that Sep 1 had no event demand]
variables.how_to_model: Per-event Bernoulli with an announcement lead time; R04 storms raise the probability

variables.name: Weather x event interaction
variables.description: Rain or cold at let-out raises the car share and delays or cancels outdoor events.
variables.values_or_range: Rain at let-out: car share 1.3-2x [design]; outdoor events halted in thunderstorms
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; cross-link R04
variables.data_source: NOAA and NWS observations and forecasts (R04)
variables.how_to_model: Multiply mode share by a weather factor at the realised end; storms raise cancellation and delay odds

variables.sub_box: Venue operations, let-out pricing and queues
variables.name: Post-event surge multiplier and decay
variables.description: How much app prices rise around a let-out and how quickly they fall back.
variables.values_or_range: 1.2-1.4x at arena let-outs, ~1.8x on New Year's night; decays to ~1.05-1.10x within 45-60 min [corrected by fact-check: originally ~1.05x; at 23:00 the busiest nights' fare per mile at zone 186 was 4.91 vs 4.48 on quiet nights, 1.10x]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] own calc HVFHV Jan 2023: zone 186 busiest nights fare per mile 6.27 vs 4.73 at 22:00, 4.91 by 23:00; zone 230 +42% fare per mile and +27% driver pay per engaged hour; NYE 1.83x; Brooklyn zones 25 and 189 next to Barclays showed no pay gain on their busiest nights (-2% and -5% pay per engaged hour), so let-out surge is venue-specific [added by fact-check from hv_events_out.txt, P*]
