variables.values_or_range: Mostly standard; XL ~10-15%, Black/Lux ~5% [U]; wheelchair-accessible cars served about 9% of 2025 app trips (21.4M of 243.6M had wav_match_flag = Y) [corrected by fact-check: was ~5-10% of cars [U]; S, FerrisSearch analysis on GitHub]; EV share rising (Green Rides target for 2030).
variables.impact_evidence: Public app trip data has no product field, only wheelchair request/match flags [S, schema read on GitHub]; class shares [U].
variables.data_source: None found for the XL/Comfort/Black mix; HVFHV wav_match_flag gives the WAV share of trips [S]; NYC Open Data active FHV vehicle list (make, model, WAV) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Give each bot a vehicle class and keep separate supply pools per product; the agent's own class (R08) decides which pool it competes in.

variables.name: Shift start (log-on) times
variables.description: When competing drivers start work, by hour and weekday, mixing full-time and part-time drivers.
variables.values_or_range: Weekday start peaks around 5-8 am and 3-6 pm [U]; full-time drivers gave ~80% of app rides (2018); 60-65% of yellow drivers are full-time (2026).
variables.impact_evidence: Parrott & Reich 2018 report for TLC [S]; TLC testimony 17 Mar 2026 [S].
variables.data_source: TLC monthly report (avg_hours_per_day_per_driver, avg_days_drivers_on_road); 2010-2013 yellow trips with hashed driver IDs https://databank.illinois.edu/datasets/IDB-9610843 [U]
variables.how_to_model: Draw each bot's start time from an hour x weekday distribution fitted to supply curves; full-time (10-12 h) and part-time (2-5 h) types.

variables.name: Shift end (log-off) rule
variables.description: What makes competitors stop: hours worked, a daily income target, fatigue, or a legal cap on hours.
variables.values_or_range: Stop after 8-12 h, or at an income target of $200-350/day [design]; TLC fatigue rule: at most 10 h of passenger time in any 24 h (the count resets after 8 consecutive hours with no passengers) and 60 h per Monday-Sunday week; time between trips does not count [corrected by fact-check: P*, 35 RCNY 80-14(f)].
variables.impact_evidence: Camerer et al. 1997 found negative wage elasticity (income targeting) among NYC cab drivers; Uber data shows supply rising with surge (Chen & Sheldon) [S]; later NYC cab work (Farber 2015, QJE) finds little income targeting, so the evidence is mixed [U, added by fact-check].
variables.data_source: 2010-2013 yellow trips with driver IDs (Illinois Data Bank) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Log-off hazard = f(hours online, earnings vs target, time of day), fitted to shift-length distributions.

variables.name: Short-run surge entry
variables.description: How strongly offline drivers log on, or online drivers stay longer, when surge or earnings rise.
variables.values_or_range: Supply elasticity to hourly earnings of 0.2-1.0 within 15-60 min; lag 5-30 min [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Chen & Sheldon (Uber, US cities 2014-15): surge raises driver supply when surge is high [S].
variables.data_source: None public for NYC; calibrate to how fast HVFHV pickup times recover after demand spikes
variables.how_to_model: Entry rate = base x (1 + e x (surge - 1)) with a lag; lower log-off hazard during surge.

variables.name: Surge chasing
variables.description: Share of idle competitors who drive toward surge or busy zones, and how fast, which wears surge away before late arrivals get there.
variables.values_or_range: 10-40% of idle drivers within 2-3 km respond; reaction lag 2-10 min [design]; surge recomputed every ~1-5 min [U].
variables.impact_evidence: Driver interviews report surge often gone on arrival (Lee et al. 2015, CHI) [U]; ranges [design].
variables.how_to_model: Bot policy: with probability p move toward the zone with the best expected earnings within a radius; produces herding.

variables.name: Long-run re-equilibration
variables.description: After fares or earnings stay higher for weeks, drivers add hours until utilisation falls and hourly pay returns near its old level.
variables.values_or_range: Hourly earnings back near baseline about 2 months after an Uber fare rise.
variables.impact_evidence: Hall, Horton & Knoepfle, NBER w30883, Ride-Sharing Markets Re-Equilibrate (2023) [S].
variables.how_to_model: For multi-day and learning runs (10 days then day 11), drift background supply day by day so competitor hourly pay tends to a target; off in single-day runs.

variables.name: Home anchoring of competitors
variables.description: Competitors start and end shifts near home (mostly Queens, Brooklyn, the Bronx, NJ, Long Island), so supply is rich in the outer boroughs early and drains from Manhattan late.
variables.values_or_range: Home mix e.g. Queens 35-45%, Brooklyn 20-25%, Bronx 15-20%, other 15-25% [U]; 10-20% of late-evening idle cars heading home [design].
variables.impact_evidence: NYC app drivers are mostly immigrants living in the outer boroughs (Parrott & Reich 2018) [U]; mix [U].
variables.data_source: None public for app drivers' homes; first and last pickups per shift in 2010-2013 taxi data [U]; Census ACS commute data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Each bot has a home zone; shifts start there and the last hour is biased toward home (uses the destination filter).

variables.name: Competitor breaks
variables.description: Short supply dips when many drivers pause at once for meals, prayer, bathrooms or rest.
variables.values_or_range: Lunch 12-2 pm; dinner or iftar at sunset; Friday midday prayers; 10-45 min break per 4-6 h [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design guess]; an evening dip in Ramadan was reported by Uber in Paris (2017) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Break hazard by time of day per bot type; break spots near food and parking clusters (R01).

variables.name: Competitor multi-apping share
variables.description: Share of competitors logged into Uber and Lyft at once, so one car counts as supply on both and vanishes from both when matched.
variables.values_or_range: US, Q1 2024: ~55% of Lyft drivers also on Uber, ~25% of Uber drivers also on Lyft; NYC share unknown.
variables.impact_evidence: Gridwise driver-panel data [S]; Chicago's TNP driver data flags drivers reported by more than one company (MULTIPLE_TNPS) [S]; NYC's cruising rule already splits a car's idle time across platforms when it is available to more than one HVFHS [P*, 35 RCNY 59D-21(b)(1), added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Flag bots single- or dual-app; dual-app bots sit in both platforms' idle pools and take the better offer.

variables.name: Competitor acceptance and cherry-picking
variables.description: How often competitors decline offers (short, low pay, long pickup, unwanted destination), pushing those offers down the line to the agent.
variables.values_or_range: Acceptance 50-95% by driver type [U]; top Uber Pro tiers need 90%+ acceptance in some markets.
variables.impact_evidence: Uber Pro terms (Hong Kong) require 90%+ acceptance for top tiers [S]; NYC values [U]; NYC lets platforms restrict a driver's access without the usual 72 h notice for excessive cancellation or non-acceptance [P*, 35 RCNY 59D-22(c)(3), added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Bot accept probability = logistic(pay per minute, pickup ETA, destination); declined offers go back to the matcher.

variables.name: Competitor strategy mix
variables.description: Mix of background driver policies (cruiser, hotspot parker, airport queuer, surge chaser, home-anchored commuter, cherry-picker), with skill differences.
variables.values_or_range: e.g. 30% hotspot parkers, 20% cruisers, 15% airport queuers, 15% surge chasers, 10% commuters, 10% random [design]; earnings-per-hour spread of +/-20-30% [U].
variables.impact_evidence: Experience and where/when choices explain earnings gaps among Uber drivers (Cook et al. 2021) [U]; mix [design].
variables.how_to_model: Bot population with archetype policies; mix tuned so zone supply and airport queue lengths match data.

variables.name: Taxi 4-5 pm shift change
variables.description: Yellow taxis go off duty to hand over at garages (mostly in Queens) in the late afternoon, cutting taxi supply just as demand rises.
variables.values_or_range: Taxis on the road fell from 6,688 to 5,452 between 4 and 5 pm (2011), an 18.5% drop vs the hour before [corrected by fact-check: arithmetic; was 'about 20%'].
variables.impact_evidence: TLC 2011 study via DNAinfo; later city GPS review [S].
variables.how_to_model: Two-shift lease bots hand over at 4-5 pm with a deadhead to garage zones; check today's dip in 2024-26 yellow pickups by hour.

variables.name: Cruising versus parking when idle
variables.description: Whether idle competitors cruise (taxis hunting hails) or park and wait for pings (app drivers), which changes hail odds and congestion.
variables.values_or_range: Empty time between passengers in the Manhattan core: 8 min for yellow vs 11 min for app cars (2017); app cars empty 41% of the time south of 96th St (2019).
variables.impact_evidence: Schaller 2017 [S]; TLC data cited in the 2019 cruising-cap ruling [S].
variables.how_to_model: Taxi bots cruise high-hail routes; app bots park near hotspots or drift; both feed the traffic model (R10).

variables.name: Matching algorithm
variables.description: How the platform pairs requests and drivers: send the nearest idle driver at once, or optimise over a short batch.
variables.values_or_range: First-dispatch nearest | batched matching every 2-10 s (Uber: a few seconds) | global minimum total ETA.
variables.impact_evidence: Uber's marketplace page describes batched matching over a few seconds [S]; first-dispatch causes wild goose chases when prices are low (Castillo et al.) [P, re-read by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Pluggable matcher; default batched assignment over idle drivers within the radius every 5 s; sensitivity-test the window.

variables.name: Matching cost metric
variables.description: What 'closest' means: straight-line distance, road travel time, or travel time with penalties for wrong heading, U-turns and bridges.
variables.values_or_range: Straight-line | road ETA (R10) | road ETA + heading penalty.
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; Uber says batching lowers average wait [S]; a Manhattan HVFHV replay found batched min-cost assignment cut rider wait 5.3% and pickup deadhead 8.2% vs greedy nearest-car dispatch (fleetsim, GitHub) [S, added by fact-check].
variables.data_source: OpenStreetMap road graph; NYC DOT speeds (R10)
variables.how_to_model: Use road ETA from the traffic model; penalise drivers pointed the wrong way on one-way avenues.

variables.name: Maximum dispatch radius
variables.description: Furthest a driver can be sent for a pickup; beyond it the request waits or fails.
variables.values_or_range: 8-15 min pickup cap typical [U]; a small radius avoids wild goose chases but leaves riders queued.
variables.impact_evidence: Castillo et al.: a small maximum dispatch radius avoids wild goose chases but creates passenger queues [P, re-read by fact-check].
variables.data_source: None (platform internal); infer from the tail of HVFHV request-to-on-scene times
variables.how_to_model: Parameter r_max in minutes; unmatched requests retry each batch, then cancel by rider patience (R05).

variables.name: Forward dispatch
variables.description: The platform offers the next trip to a driver who is about to drop off, competing with nearby idle drivers.
variables.values_or_range: On/off; look-ahead 0-5 min before drop-off [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Uber and Lyft send next-trip offers before drop-off.
variables.how_to_model: Busy drivers with <= L minutes left join the matching pool; cost = time left + ETA from the drop-off.

variables.name: Offer timeout and decline cascade
variables.description: How long a driver has to accept, and how a declined or expired offer moves to the next driver.
variables.values_or_range: About 10 s traditionally, 15 s in an Uber pilot [uncertain: not re-checked; driver guides often give ~15 s as Uber's standing window]; cascade to the next-best driver 3-5 times [U].
variables.impact_evidence: The Rideshare Guy on Uber extending ping time [S].
variables.how_to_model: Offer queue per request; simulated time pauses for the agent's decision (latency handled as a harness setting, R12).

variables.name: Upfront offer information
variables.description: What the driver sees before accepting: pay, pickup time, trip time, destination, surge. Street-hailed taxis learn the destination only after pickup and may not refuse.
variables.values_or_range: Full (pay, destination, time) | partial (pickup only) | none (street hail).
variables.impact_evidence: Uber and Lyft show upfront pay and destination in most US markets since about 2022 [U]; NYC cab drivers may not refuse any destination in NYC, Nassau, Westchester or Newark Airport, and may not try to learn the destination before the rider is seated, except on Flex Fare e-hail trips or when signed off duty heading home [corrected by fact-check: was 'in-city destinations [U]'; P*, 35 RCNY 80-20(a)(1),(a)(4) and 80-19].
variables.data_source: None (product design); TLC refusal rule 35 RCNY 80-20 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Offer fields set per scenario; this turns cherry-picking on or off.

variables.name: Broadcast offers (Trip Radar)
variables.description: Some requests are shown to several drivers at once and go to the first to accept, which rewards speed.
variables.values_or_range: 0-20% of requests broadcast [design]; first to accept wins.
variables.impact_evidence: Uber Trip Radar blog and driver reports of first-come matching [S].
variables.how_to_model: Broadcast unmatched requests to k drivers; winner is first accept in simulated time, so LLM wall-clock latency does not count.

variables.name: Decline and cancel penalties
variables.description: What declining or cancelling costs: airport queue place, tier perks, short timeouts, lower dispatch priority.
variables.values_or_range: Airport: lose place after several declines or cancels in a row; possible 2-10 min cool-down [U].
variables.impact_evidence: Uber JFK driver page: you lose your place if you do not accept multiple requests in a row or cancel multiple rides [S]; NYC rules let platforms restrict access without notice for excessive cancellation or non-acceptance [P*, 35 RCNY 59D-22(c)(3), added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Track rolling decline and cancel counts; apply queue resets and timeouts.

variables.name: Destination filter (take me home)
variables.description: Platform mode that only sends trips heading toward a chosen place, with a daily limit.
variables.values_or_range: Uber 2 uses/day, Lyft 6/day (driver sources); usually yields short hops toward the target; taxi analogue: an off-duty NYC cab heading home or to its garage may take a rider whose destination is directly on its route after logging 'Returning to garage (or home)' [corrected by fact-check: applies to taxis too; P*, 35 RCNY 80-19(a)(5); fare side in R07-050].
variables.impact_evidence: The Rideshare Guy and Gridwise guides [S].
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (off-duty going-home rule)
variables.how_to_model: When on, offer only requests whose drop-off cuts distance to the target by at least x%; count daily uses.

variables.name: Product eligibility and opt-ins
variables.description: Which request types a car can receive (X, XL, Comfort, Black, Green/EV, wheelchair), including higher classes opting into lower ones.
variables.values_or_range: Yes/no per product; Black and XL drivers can opt into X [U].
variables.impact_evidence: Uber-Waymo: robotaxis matched to UberX, Green, Comfort and Comfort Electric requests [S]; opt-in rules [U].
variables.how_to_model: Each request carries a product; the matcher filters eligible cars; the agent can toggle opt-ins.

variables.name: Wheelchair and Access-A-Ride dispatch
variables.description: Wheelchair-accessible requests and paratransit trips go only to accessible cars, under service-level targets.
variables.values_or_range: Flags wav_request_flag, wav_match_flag and access_a_ride_flag in the app trip data; WAV-requested and WAV-matched trips about 699k of 243.6M in 2025 (~0.3%) [corrected by fact-check: column names re-read on GitHub; share from FerrisSearch analysis [S]]; accessible taxis must accept dispatches from the Accessible Taxi Dispatcher [P*, 35 RCNY 53-08].
variables.impact_evidence: HVFHV columns [S, read on GitHub]; accessible licences are the only new FHV licences in 2026 [S].
variables.how_to_model: Separate accessible request stream; accessible cars get priority dispatch.

variables.name: Shared-ride matching
variables.description: Pooling riders into one car adds detours and changes per-trip pay.
variables.values_or_range: shared_request_flag and shared_match_flag in the data; 2025: about 6.8M shared requests (2.8% of app trips, all Uber), of which 3.9M matched (1.6%) [corrected by fact-check: was 'small share [U]'; S, FerrisSearch analysis on GitHub].
variables.impact_evidence: HVFHV columns [S]; pooling makes wild goose chases worse (Castillo et al.) [P].
variables.how_to_model: Optional insertion heuristic; off in v1.

variables.name: Street-hail encounters and hail rights
variables.description: Chance an empty taxi meets a hailing rider, given foot traffic and how many empty taxis pass first; plus who may street-hail where.
variables.values_or_range: Yellow anywhere (only yellow in the Manhattan core and at airports); green only outside that zone; app cars and robotaxis never; 0-2 hails per block-minute [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Medallions grant street-hail rights citywide [S]; green Hail Exclusionary Zone = Manhattan south of E 96th St and W 110th St plus the NYC airports [verified by fact-check: was 'zone rules [U]'; P*, 35 RCNY 51-03].
variables.data_source: Yellow and green pickups by zone (TLC); foot traffic (R01)
variables.how_to_model: Hail arrivals per street segment; the first empty eligible taxi to pass gets it.

variables.name: Taxi e-hail channel
variables.description: Taxis also get app dispatches through Uber, Curb or Arro, a second request stream.
variables.values_or_range: 5-25% of yellow trips via e-hail [U]; rising since Uber and Curb began dispatching cabs.
variables.impact_evidence: AutoMarketplace: yellow trips +17-20% year on year (Aug-Sep 2025), driven by returning cabs and Uber/Curb e-hail [S].
variables.data_source: Partial: yellow and green payment_type = 0 marks Flex Fare (upfront-priced e-hail) trips, a lower bound on e-hail [corrected by fact-check: was 'none found'; P* via R07 dictionary excerpt]; metered e-hail trips are not flagged
variables.how_to_model: Route a share of app requests to taxis through a taxi e-hail matcher.

variables.name: Agent multi-apping
variables.description: Whether the agent may stay online on Uber and Lyft at once and choose between offers.
variables.values_or_range: Single-app | dual-app.
variables.impact_evidence: Multi-apping is common (~25-55% of drivers, Gridwise) [S]; earnings gain [U]; NYC's cruising rule expects cars to be available to more than one HVFHS [P*, 35 RCNY 59D-21(b)(1), added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Agent gets two offer streams; accepting one removes it from the other; pay rules differ (R07).

variables.name: Ping rate per idle hour
variables.description: How many offers an idle driver gets per hour in a given zone and hour.
variables.values_or_range: About 1.8 trips per online hour citywide, so about 4-8 offers per idle hour; 1-15 by zone [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] from ~667k trips/day [S] and ~58% utilisation [S]; arithmetic re-checked by fact-check (667k trips / ~363k online vehicle-hours = ~1.8).
variables.data_source: Derived from HVFHV trips and the supply field
variables.how_to_model: Emerges from the matcher; report as a metric; check against TLC trips per vehicle per hour.

variables.name: Utilisation rate
variables.description: Share of online time with a passenger; the main multiplier on hourly pay and an input to the TLC pay formula.
variables.values_or_range: About 59% in the Manhattan core (app cars empty 41% of the time south of 96th St, 2019) and about 58% citywide (2024) [S]; platforms held to at least 50-53% (2024) [uncertain: not re-checked]; since 1 Aug 2025 the pay floor divides by fixed applied rates of 53.3% (per minute) and 68.5% (per mile) instead of each company's actual utilisation [corrected by fact-check: P*, 35 RCNY 59D-22(b)].
variables.impact_evidence: TLC data cited in the 2019 cruising-cap ruling [S]; 2024 city deal (Lyft utilisation at least 50%) [S]; 2024 citywide ~58% (Bloomberg, via R07) [S]; TLC defines utilisation as the share of available time or distance spent carrying passengers [P*, 35 RCNY 59D-03(j)].
variables.how_to_model: Track per driver; platform-wide utilisation drives lockouts (R06) and pay (R07).

variables.name: Idle gap between trips
variables.description: Minutes from one drop-off to the next pickup.
variables.values_or_range: Manhattan core: 8 min (yellow) and 11 min (app cars) in 2017; longer in the outer boroughs.
variables.impact_evidence: Schaller 2017 [S].
variables.data_source: Schaller report; TLC trip records (cannot be chained per car publicly)
variables.how_to_model: Emergent; validation target.

variables.name: Pickup ETA (en-route deadhead)
variables.description: Time and miles spent driving to a matched rider, which earns little or nothing.
variables.values_or_range: Uber, Manhattan-internal weekday trips, Jun 2024: request to on-scene median 3.0 min, p90 6.6 min [corrected by fact-check: was 'usually 3-8 min [U]'; S, fleetsim analysis of HVFHV records on GitHub]; longer in thin areas and hours.
variables.impact_evidence: HVFHV data has request_datetime and on_scene_datetime [S, re-read on GitHub]; Lyft rows fill on_scene_datetime for only ~0.3% of trips, so the public pickup-time distribution is Uber-only [S, added by fact-check]; wild goose chases [P].
variables.how_to_model: Road-network ETA; compare the simulated distribution with HVFHV on-scene minus request by zone and hour.

variables.name: Wild goose chase threshold
variables.description: Point where idle supply is so thin that matches go to far-away drivers, pickups lengthen, cancellations spike and pay falls.
variables.values_or_range: Appears when idle density falls below the level where pickup ETA climbs steeply (city-specific) [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Castillo, Knoepfle & Weyl: in thin hours and areas of Manhattan many riders and drivers cancel and waits jump [P, re-read by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Emerges from matcher, r_max and rider patience; include a capped-surge scenario to test it.

variables.name: Airport queue length and position
variables.description: First-in-first-out virtual queue in airport waiting lots; the app shows your position and how many drivers are ahead.
variables.values_or_range: 0 to 500+ cars; position visible; JFK Cell Phone Lot and Limo Lot.
variables.impact_evidence: Uber JFK driver page [S]; Gridwise crowdsourced queue counts [S].
variables.data_source: Uber JFK page; HVFHV pickups in airport zones
variables.how_to_model: One FIFO per airport and platform; inflow from drop-offs and arrivals, outflow = airport requests.

variables.name: Airport queue wait time
variables.description: Time from joining the queue to getting a trip.
variables.values_or_range: Taxi hold lot about 2-3 h (NBC NY); app queues 0-3 h; waits of 90+ min often not worth it (Gridwise).
variables.impact_evidence: NBC New York; Gridwise [S].
variables.data_source: Derived; Chris Whong's 2013 FOIL analysis https://chriswhong.com/?p=838
variables.how_to_model: Emerges from queue length / service rate; check against airport pickups per hour.

variables.name: Airport queue rules
variables.description: Rules for keeping your place: stay inside the zone, stay online, do not decline or cancel repeatedly; lot capacity.
variables.values_or_range: Lose place if offline, outside the zone, several declines or cancels in a row; a rider cancel does not cost the place.
variables.impact_evidence: Uber JFK driver page [S].
variables.how_to_model: Geofence plus queue state machine; overflow turned away when the lot is full [design].

variables.name: Taxi hold lot and short-return ticket
variables.description: Yellow taxis queue in JFK and LGA holding lots; a short trip to nearby areas earns a ticket to an expedited line if they return in time.
variables.values_or_range: 2-hour return window (since 2012); JFK short-return area = Queens, Brooklyn, Five Towns [uncertain: window length and area not re-checked; the notice is on nyc.gov, which was blocked].
variables.impact_evidence: TLC industry notice 12-33 [S].
variables.how_to_model: Ticket state with expiry; priority lane in the taxi queue.

variables.name: Airport rematch and priority tiers
variables.description: A driver dropping off at the airport may get a pickup before joining the queue; top-tier drivers get priority.
variables.values_or_range: Uber Pro Diamond/Platinum priority rematch (Australia, Hong Kong); NYC unknown.
variables.impact_evidence: Uber Australia blog; Uber Hong Kong Pro terms [S].
variables.how_to_model: At drop-off, probability p of a rematch from the queue head, higher for top tiers.

variables.name: Airport queue service rate
variables.description: How fast airport queues drain, set by arriving passengers' ride requests on each platform.
variables.values_or_range: Depends on flight arrivals; 2025 app pickups: LGA 4.92M (~13.5k/day) and JFK 4.07M (~11.2k/day), ~25k/day combined, and the two top app pickup zones by revenue [corrected by fact-check: was ~10-25k/day [U]; S, FerrisSearch analysis of 2025 HVFHV records].
variables.impact_evidence: [S] 2025 HVFHV counts; flight data is a cross-link to R03 and R05.
variables.data_source: HVFHV pickups in airport zones; BTS on-time data https://www.transtats.bts.gov ; Port Authority traffic reports
variables.how_to_model: Airport request process tied to the arrivals schedule, split by platform share.

variables.name: Taxi stands at hubs and hotels
variables.description: Staffed or informal taxi lines at Penn Station, Grand Central, Port Authority Bus Terminal and hotels.
variables.values_or_range: 0-50 cabs; 5-40 min wait [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] values; TLC rules regulate taxi stands and require the first two cabs on a stand to be ready to load [P*, 35 RCNY 80-19, added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Small FIFO queues at stand points, with arrivals tied to train arrivals.

variables.name: Driver strikes and protests
variables.description: Organised refusals to work or to serve a place, which cut competitor supply for a while.
variables.values_or_range: e.g. LGA pickup strike 26 Feb 2023, noon to midnight; Uber claimed 36% more LGA trips that day; 0-3 a year.
variables.impact_evidence: Gothamist and Fox Business reports [S].
variables.how_to_model: Scenario event removing 10-60% of bots from a zone and window; announced in advance in event-aware runs.

variables.name: Holiday supply shortfall
variables.description: Fewer drivers work on major holidays and holiday eves relative to demand.
variables.values_or_range: Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve and Day, New Year's Eve, Eid, Lunar New Year: supply -10% to -40% [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U]; measurable from HVFHV pickup times on those dates.
variables.data_source: HVFHV trip records (on-scene time by date)
variables.how_to_model: Holiday multiplier on log-on rates per bot type.

variables.name: Religious and cultural supply dips
variables.description: Competitor supply drops around iftar in Ramadan and Friday midday prayers, since many NYC drivers are Muslim.
variables.values_or_range: -5% to -25% supply for 30-60 min at sunset in Ramadan [design]; Friday 12-2 pm dip [U].
variables.impact_evidence: Uber France reported an evening driver drop in Ramadan 2017 (Paris) [S]; NYC not measured.
variables.data_source: None for NYC; test in HVFHV on-scene times
variables.how_to_model: Calendar-driven break hazard for a share of bots.

variables.name: Weather supply response
variables.description: How competitor supply changes in rain, snow and heat while demand jumps.
variables.values_or_range: Rain: supply about flat while demand rises [U]; heavy snow -10% to -40% [U]; robotaxis may pause.
variables.impact_evidence: Farber (2015), Why You Can't Find a Taxi in the Rain [U].
variables.data_source: NOAA Central Park daily weather plus HVFHV on-scene times
variables.how_to_model: Weather-dependent log-on and log-off hazards (cross-link R04).

variables.name: Platform outage
variables.description: One platform stops matching for minutes or hours.
variables.values_or_range: 0-2 a year; 15-120 min [U].
variables.how_to_model: Switch off one matcher; riders move to the other platform and to taxis.

variables.name: Event let-out convergence
variables.description: Competitors flock to stadium, concert and venue exits, so a known event draws extra supply and shortens surge.
variables.values_or_range: 0.5-3x normal supply within 1 km in the 30 min before let-out [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Supply rises with surge (Chen & Sheldon) [S]; size [design].
variables.how_to_model: Share of bots that know the event schedule; tie to the with/without event-info treatment so rivals and agent are matched.

variables.name: FHV licence pause and sign-up waitlists
variables.description: Cap on new FHV licences (since 2018; only wheelchair-accessible licences in 2026) and platform waitlists for new drivers, which fix the size of the competing pool.
variables.values_or_range: Pause since 2018; EV exemption windows lifted licensed FHVs from 95,396 (Feb 2023) to 107,636 (Feb 2024); Uber froze sign-ups in Apr 2023 (waitlist).
variables.impact_evidence: TLC licence pause report Feb 2026; Smart Cities Dive; Bloomberg via Yahoo [S]; legal basis verified: Admin Code 19-550 (L.L. 2018/147) has the TLC review FHV licence numbers at least once a year and lets it vary them for wheelchair-accessible and low- or zero-emission vehicles [P*, added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Scenario parameter for pool size; fleet growth by the agent limited to accessible or EV cars per scenario.

variables.name: Platform log-on lockouts
variables.description: Uber and Lyft block drivers from logging on, or log them off, when demand is low, to keep utilisation high under the TLC pay formula.
variables.values_or_range: Depends on rule vintage. Before Aug 2025: on/off, triggered when utilisation is below ~50-58%; widespread in 2024 [uncertain: the 'from May 2024' start date was not re-checked]; Aug 2024 deal: Uber to phase out by Labor Day, Lyft to keep utilisation at least 50%; later replaced by waitlists; mid-shift lockouts reported. From 1 Aug 2025: a platform must give 72 h notice before restricting a driver on a calendar day and must keep a driver who logs on available for at least 16 h (restarting after 8 h offline); exceptions for licensing, rule breaches, misconduct and excessive cancels or non-acceptance; $500 per violation [corrected by fact-check: P*, 35 RCNY 59D-22(c)].
variables.impact_evidence: NYC Comptroller letter; City Limits; Bloomberg via Yahoo [S]; 35 RCNY 59D-22(c) [P*]; high for 2024 to Jul 2025 replays, lower under the Aug 2025 access rule [fact-check note].
variables.how_to_model: Gatekeeper by rule vintage: for pre-Aug-2025 dates, refuse log-on (or log off mid-shift) when forecast utilisation in the zone and hour is below the threshold, with a probability set by driver priority; from Aug 2025, allow only whole-day restrictions announced 72 h ahead and no lockout within 16 h of logging on; show a 'busy times' hint.

variables.name: Cruising cap (scenario toggle)
variables.description: TLC rule, struck down in 2019, to cap empty app-car time in Manhattan south of 96th St.
variables.values_or_range: Planned 36% (Feb 2020) then 31% (Aug 2020); annulled 23 Dec 2019; a later Council report proposed 11 cents per empty minute.
variables.impact_evidence: NY1 on the ruling; NYC Council report [S]; caps, dates and hours verified: 36% from 1 Feb 2020 and 31% from 1 Aug 2020, weekdays 6 am-11 pm and weekends 8 am-11 pm, in the zone south of and excluding 96th St, WAVs exempt, $350 per 100 excess hours; the annulled text still appears in the RCNY compilation [P*, 35 RCNY 59D-21, added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Off by default; a policy scenario that charges platforms for empty time, leading to more lockouts and rebalancing.

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Robotaxi background fleet
variables.description: Number of driverless cars competing in the scenario city.
variables.values_or_range: NYC 2026: none carrying passengers (test permit Aug 2025 for 8 cars with safety drivers, expired 31 Mar 2026; state law allows testing only); scenarios 0-10% of supply; Waymo US ~3,000 cars in early 2026 [S] [uncertain: the 3,800 upper figure from the May 2026 recall was not re-checked].
variables.impact_evidence: TechCrunch; West Side Spirit; fleet count from a May 2026 NHTSA recall [S]; NYC facts (Aug 2025 approval, 8 cars, specialist behind the wheel, Manhattan south of 112th St and Downtown Brooklyn, permits expired 31 Mar 2026, Hochul's Feb 2026 proposal withdrawn, ~3,000 US cars) match Vital City's Waymo map methodology on GitHub [S, re-checked by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Scenario parameter; robotaxi bots never log off and charge at depots.

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Robotaxi trips per car per day
variables.description: Trips per robotaxi per day, a realism ceiling for the robotaxi agent.
variables.values_or_range: About 19-24 trips per car per day (about 500k rides/week across 3,000-3,800 cars, Mar 2026) [corrected by fact-check: arithmetic range; 2025 figures of 450k+ rides/week on ~2,500 cars give ~26, S, GitHub company profile].
variables.impact_evidence: Waymo 500k paid rides/week (Mar 2026) [S]; division [design].
variables.data_source: Waymo statements; CPUC quarterly AV reports [U]
variables.how_to_model: Validation target for robotaxi runs.

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Robotaxi operating limits
variables.description: Robotaxi supply drops outside the operating area (geofence, freeways, heavy rain or snow, flooded roads) and while charging.
variables.values_or_range: Geofence 0-100% of city; weather pauses; 1-3 h charging per day [U].
variables.impact_evidence: Waymo fleet-wide software recall in May 2026 after flooded-road and construction-zone incidents [S].
variables.how_to_model: Zone mask, weather thresholds and charging schedule (R08).

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Robotaxis on a human platform
variables.description: When a platform mixes robotaxis and human drivers, which riders get which, and at what price.
variables.values_or_range: Uber-Waymo in Austin and Atlanta: UberX, Green, Comfort and Comfort Electric requests can go to a Waymo at the same price, with no tip prompt; ~100 robotaxis in Austin (2025) and ~200 by 2026 [corrected by fact-check: these are analyst estimates, not Waymo disclosures, per Vital City's methodology on GitHub [S]].
variables.impact_evidence: Uber investor release (2024); Reuters via StreetInsider [S].
variables.how_to_model: Matcher includes robotaxis for eligible products inside the geofence, with a preference weight and a rider opt-out rate [U].

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Number of competing model fleets
variables.description: How many LLM agents, each running 1 or N cars, compete in the same market.
variables.values_or_range: 1 (solo against bots) up to 5 models x N cars.
variables.impact_evidence: Multi-agent rankings differ from solo ones in Vending-Bench Arena (team dossier D07) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Harness setting with seat rotation and mirrored runs (R12).

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Agent fleet share of total supply
variables.description: The agent's cars as a share of all supply where they work, which decides whether they take the market as given or move it.
variables.values_or_range: 1 car ~0.007% of NYC app supply; N=100 ~0.7%; N=1,000 ~7% [design, using ~15k cars online].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; added supply cuts utilisation (Hall et al.) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Either shrink background supply by the fleet size (displacement) or keep it fixed (additive); report both.

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Own-fleet cannibalisation
variables.description: Extra cars of the same fleet take trips from each other, so revenue per added car falls as N grows.
variables.values_or_range: Marginal revenue per car falls with N; better dispatch could serve NYC taxi demand with ~30% fewer cars (Vazifeh et al. 2018).
variables.impact_evidence: Vazifeh et al., Nature 557 (2018) [S]; a Manhattan HVFHV replay saw utilisation per car fall from 57% (1,500 cars) to 28% (6,000) (fleetsim, via R11) [S, added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Measure the marginal revenue curve by running N and N + dN cars; report fleet efficiency.

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Intra-fleet dispatch rule
variables.description: Whether the platform matches each fleet car on its own (nearest wins) or lets the fleet operator pick which of its cars takes a request.
variables.values_or_range: Independent | operator assigns | operator assigns with veto.
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; Uber dispatches the Waymo fleet on its platform [S].
variables.how_to_model: Matcher flag; operator-assign adds an internal batching step for the fleet.

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Rival visibility
variables.description: What the agent can see about other cars: nothing, a busy or surge heat map, airport queue counts, or live rival positions.
variables.values_or_range: None | heat map (as in driver apps) | queue counts | full positions (unrealistic).
variables.impact_evidence: Uber app shows queue position and drivers ahead at JFK [S]; driver apps do not show rivals' cars [U].
variables.how_to_model: Observation levels in the API; realistic default = surge or busy heat map plus own queue position.

variables.sub_box: H. Robotaxis and competing model fleets
variables.name: Coordination channel between rival fleets
variables.description: Whether competing agents can message each other, with a risk of zone-splitting collusion.
variables.values_or_range: None | public | private.
variables.impact_evidence: LLM agents formed cartels when given email in Vending-Bench Arena (team dossier D07) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Harness toggle; log messages and detect zone partitioning.

variables.name: Background supply generation mode
variables.description: How the simulator creates competitor cars: replay historical trips as ghost drivers, simulate rule-based bots, or a hybrid.
variables.values_or_range: Replay | agent-based bots | hybrid (replayed demand, bot supply).
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; public app trip data has no driver or vehicle ID, so driver-level replay is impossible [S, columns re-read on GitHub by fact-check]; the TLC may collect driver and vehicle licence numbers per trip (Admin Code 19-550(d)) but does not publish them [P*].
variables.how_to_model: Default hybrid: demand resampled from trips; supply from a calibrated bot population.

variables.name: Displacement rule for replayed trips
variables.description: When the agent serves a request that a background driver served in history, what happens to that driver.
variables.values_or_range: Remove the trip from the background driver (it idles) | ignore (additive) | full re-simulation.
variables.impact_evidence: [design].
variables.how_to_model: Background bots re-plan after losing a trip, so each request is served once.

variables.name: Supply elasticity setting
variables.description: Whether background supply is fixed or reacts to surge, events, agent behaviour and earnings.
variables.values_or_range: Fixed | short-run elastic | short- and long-run elastic.
variables.impact_evidence: Chen & Sheldon; Hall et al. [S].
variables.how_to_model: Toggle; report scores under both to separate skill from equilibrium effects.

variables.name: Supply calibration targets
variables.description: Public statistics the background supply must reproduce.
variables.values_or_range: TLC monthly: unique drivers, unique vehicles, vehicles per day, hours per day per vehicle and per driver, trips per day, minutes per trip; HVFHV: on-scene minus request by zone and hour (Uber rows only; Lyft leaves on_scene_datetime empty) [corrected by fact-check], driver_pay per trip-hour (no driver ID, so not per online hour); FHV base report: trips and unique vehicles per base; Schaller empty share and idle gaps.
variables.impact_evidence: TLC monthly report columns [S, read in GitHub import code; re-read by fact-check: trips_per_day, farebox_per_day, unique_drivers, unique_vehicles, vehicles_per_day, avg days and hours per vehicle and per driver, avg_minutes_per_trip, trips_per_day_shared]; HVFHV columns [S].
variables.data_source: TLC monthly CSV; HVFHV records; FHV Base Aggregate Report
variables.how_to_model: Fit log-on curves and the archetype mix by simulated method of moments; hold out months for validation.

variables.name: Driver-level behaviour data
variables.description: Datasets with persistent driver IDs, used to fit shift lengths, stopping rules and airport choices.
variables.values_or_range: 2010-2013 NYC yellow trips with hashed medallion and licence IDs (FOIL); Chicago TNP Drivers monthly (trips per driver, MULTIPLE_TNPS).
variables.impact_evidence: Chris Whong used the 2013 FOIL data for airport waits [S]; Chicago dataset documentation [S].
variables.how_to_model: Fit hazard models offline; carry the parameters to 2025 with a drift adjustment.

variables.name: Taxi metered rate of fare
variables.description: The yellow and green taxi meter charges an initial unit plus one unit per fifth of a mile when moving at 12 mph or more, or per 60 seconds when slower or stopped.
variables.values_or_range: $3.00 initial + $0.70 per unit = $3.50/mile above 12 mph, $0.70/min (=$42/h) below 12 mph; unchanged since 18 Dec 2022 and still in force Aug 2026
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a) and 82-26(a), rules current through 13 Aug 2026 (re-read in fact-check)
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via nyc_code_archive (verbatim export, current to 13 Aug 2026) https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; validate on yellow/green fare_amount in NYC TLC trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
variables.how_to_model: Meter integrates the per-second speed trace from the travel-time engine: distance units above 12 mph, time units below (cross-link R10-043)

variables.name: Final-unit pre-assessment (round-up)
variables.description: The meter charges the full unit that is currently accruing, so every metered fare is rounded up to the next $0.70.
variables.values_or_range: +$0.00 to +$0.70 per trip, about +$0.35 on average [design calc]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(1)(i)-(v): initial unit $3.00, each additional unit $0.70, current unit pre-assessed
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; calibrate on yellow fare_amount vs trip_distance and duration
variables.how_to_model: Fare = $3.00 + 0.70 x floor(accrued units) [corrected by fact-check: the $3.00 prices the initial unit (first 1/5 mi or 60 s) and $0.70 each additional unit, so the earlier $3.00 + 0.70 x ceil(units) charges one unit too many] [uncertain: which convention meters implement; calibrate on yellow fare_amount]

variables.name: Weekday rush-hour surcharge
variables.description: Flat surcharge on taxi trips that start in the weekday afternoon peak, except on legal holidays.
variables.values_or_range: $2.50 for trips starting Mon-Fri after 16:00 and before 20:00, not on legal holidays; $5.00 on JFK-Manhattan flat-fare trips
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(2)(i) and (b)(1)(i); about 12% on a $20 meter fare [design calc]
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; yellow 'extra' field; holiday calendar from R02
variables.how_to_model: Add by trip start timestamp and holiday flag; driver keeps it (part of fare)

variables.name: Overnight surcharge
variables.description: Flat surcharge on taxi trips that start at night.
variables.values_or_range: $1.00 for trips starting after 20:00 and before 06:00 (not on JFK flat-fare trips [S])
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(2)(ii); [S] JFK flat-fare page lists no overnight charge (code comment citing TLC fare page)
variables.how_to_model: Add by trip start time; driver keeps it

variables.name: MTA State surcharge on taxi trips
variables.description: State tax added to taxi trips that start in NYC and end in NYC or one of seven nearby counties; the driver collects it and the owner or e-hail app remits it.
variables.values_or_range: $0.50 per trip; applies to destinations in NYC, Dutchess, Nassau, Orange, Putnam, Rockland, Suffolk, Westchester
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(3) and 80-17(g) list the counties; [P*] 35 RCNY 51-03 defines the MTA Tax as the 50-cent tax under NYS Tax Law Art. 29-A (amount upgraded from [S] by fact-check)
variables.how_to_model: Add to rider total; exclude from driver revenue

variables.name: Taxi improvement surcharge
variables.description: Per-trip surcharge that the driver remits through the medallion (or green licence) owner to the City's Taxicab Improvement Fund, which pays for accessible taxis.
variables.values_or_range: $1.00 per taxi trip and per green hail trip (levied since 1 Jan 2015; $0.30 before Dec 2022 [U])
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(1)(i) and (h), 80-17(h)-(i), 51-03 (deposited into the Taxicab Improvement Fund) [corrected by fact-check: fund money, not owner revenue]
variables.how_to_model: Add to rider total; exclude from driver and owner revenue; optional WAV-taxi driver payments from the fund

variables.name: NYS congestion surcharge (Manhattan south of 96th St)
variables.description: State per-trip surcharge on taxi and for-hire trips that begin, end or pass through Manhattan south of 96th Street.
variables.values_or_range: Taxi $2.50; FHV/app $2.75; shared ride $0.75; since Feb 2019
variables.impact_evidence: [S] TLC dictionary congestion_surcharge field; capstone and HVFHV analyses cite $2.50 / $2.75 / $0.75 and the 96th St boundary; raises rider price so it feeds demand (R05-020)
variables.how_to_model: Polygon test on the realised route (begin, end or pass-through); add to rider price; pass-through, not driver revenue

variables.name: Congestion Relief Zone per-trip toll
variables.description: MTA congestion-pricing charge on taxi and FHV trips that begin, end or occur in Manhattan at or below 60th Street (FDR Drive and West Side Highway excluded).
variables.values_or_range: Taxi $0.75, FHV/app $1.50 per trip from 5 Jan 2025 (private cars pay $9 once per day at peak, 05:00-21:00 weekdays and 09:00-21:00 weekends, 75% less overnight [S]); step-ups [uncertain: about $1.00 / $2.00 per trip in 2028-2030 and $1.25 / $2.50 from 2031, proportional to the $12 / $15 car-toll phases; not confirmed]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] TLC yellow and HVFHS dictionaries (18 Mar 2025): cbd_congestion_fee 'starting Jan. 5, 2025'; [S] amounts and zone in a congestion-pricing working paper; Uber trips fell up to 6% while Lyft offset the fee (Zhang 2026, via the paper) [S]
variables.data_source: NYC TLC trip records (cbd_congestion_fee); MTA CRZ page https://mta.info/agency/bridges-and-tunnels/congestion-relief-zone (not fetched)
variables.how_to_model: Zone flag on route; add to rider price; open question for empty robotaxis entering the zone (R07-064)

variables.name: Airport access fee on taxi pickups
variables.description: Fee added to yellow taxi trips that pick up at JFK or LaGuardia, passed through to the airport operator.
variables.values_or_range: $1.25 (older dictionary), then $1.75 in 2023-2025 records; one 2026 code source says the current TLC rate card shows $2.00 [S, unverified]; may change [uncertain: 2026 amount unresolved; rate card and 2026 trip files unreachable during fact-check]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] yellow dictionary (Mar 2025): 'For pick up only at LaGuardia and John F. Kennedy Airports'; [S] amounts from 2025 trip-data notebooks and a 2026 fare config
variables.how_to_model: Add on pickups in zones 132 (JFK) and 138 (LGA); pass-through

variables.name: LaGuardia surcharge
variables.description: Flat surcharge on yellow taxi trips to and from LaGuardia (green taxis: trips to LaGuardia).
variables.values_or_range: $5.00 per trip; recorded with fare extras and treated as driver revenue [U] (listed with rush and night surcharges in 58-26(a)(2); owners may not take surcharges above the lease, 58-21(c)(5))
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(a)(2)(iii) and 82-26(a)(2)(iii); makes LGA runs about $5 more valuable than an equal metered trip
variables.how_to_model: Add when origin or destination is zone 138 (yellow) or destination is 138 (green)

variables.name: JFK-Manhattan flat fare
variables.description: Fixed taxi fare between JFK and any Manhattan address in either direction; trips from JFK to other boroughs stay metered.
variables.values_or_range: $70.00 + $5 weekday 16:00-20:00 + MTA tax, improvement, congestion, CBD and airport fees and tolls [uncertain: whether the airport access fee applies on RatecodeID 2 trips]; multi-stop: flat to first stop then meter
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(b); [S] 2025 HVFHV: average base fare $73.18 for JFK pickups and $59.72 for LGA [corrected by fact-check: '$60-73' mixed the two], LGA/JFK the top revenue zones; driver bears the traffic risk on a fixed fare
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; RatecodeID = 2 in yellow records
variables.how_to_model: If (JFK, Manhattan zone) pair, replace meter with $70; keep surcharges; time cost from R10-010

variables.name: Newark Airport taxi trips
variables.description: Taxi trips to Newark use the meter plus a surcharge, and the passenger pays tolls both ways; drivers may refuse EWR after 8 hours of operation in a 24-hour period.
variables.values_or_range: Meter + $20.00 Newark surcharge + tolls out and back; NYC taxis may not solicit or cruise for fares at Newark Airport (80-19(a)(4)(i), upgraded from [U] by fact-check; prearranged EWR pickups not checked), so model an empty return
variables.how_to_model: Add $20 and double tolls; force an empty return leg; allow refusal flag after 8 h

variables.name: Out-of-city taxi fares
variables.description: Rules for taxi trips leaving NYC: Westchester and Nassau use double meter beyond the city line; other places use a flat dollar fare agreed before departure.
variables.values_or_range: Westchester/Nassau: in-city meter + 2x meter outside + tolls both ways; other counties: negotiated flat (RatecodeID 5); service to Westchester/Nassau is mandatory
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-26(c), 80-17(f), 80-20(a)(1); rare trips but single fares of $100+ [U]
variables.how_to_model: Split route at city boundary; double outside units; negotiated fare drawn from historical RatecodeID 5 distribution

variables.name: Flex Fare (taxi e-hail upfront price)
variables.description: TLC-approved e-hail apps can offer yellow and green taxi riders a binding upfront fare instead of the meter, using a filed rate schedule.
variables.values_or_range: Optional per e-hail trip; recorded as payment_type 0; driver sees pickup, drop-off and quote before accepting; WAV requests may not cost more; apps include Curb, Arro and Uber's taxi integration [S]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 78-15(b), 78-21(a)(3), 80-17(a)(1), 51-03; [P*] yellow dictionary payment_type 0 = Flex Fare trip; shifts traffic risk to the driver
variables.how_to_model: E-hail offers carry a fixed quote from an app pricing model (like R07-019); accepted Flex trips ignore the meter

variables.sub_box: B. Taxi money flows and lease costs
variables.name: Taxi revenue split by fare component
variables.description: Which parts of a taxi fare the driver keeps and which pass to the owner, the state, the MTA, the City fund or the airport.
variables.values_or_range: Driver keeps meter fare, rush/night/LGA extras and tips; MTA tax, congestion surcharge, CBD fee and airport fee are pass-through; improvement surcharge goes via the owner to the City's Taxicab Improvement Fund [corrected by fact-check]; owner may collect the MTA tax from the driver (58-21(c)(5)(vii)); tolls reimburse the E-ZPass holder
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-17(g)-(i), 58-21(c)(5), 51-03; scoring on rider totals would overstate driver revenue by roughly $5-7 per Manhattan trip [design calc]
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; yellow/green itemised fare fields
variables.how_to_model: Ledger with one row per fare component and a recipient (driver, owner, state, MTA, City fund, airport)

variables.sub_box: B. Taxi money flows and lease costs
variables.name: Taxi lease caps
variables.description: Maximum amount a medallion owner may charge a driver to lease a cab and medallion per shift or week.
variables.values_or_range: Per 12-h shift: $105 day; night $115 (Sun-Tue), $120 (Wed), $129 (Thu-Sat); week $630 day / $737 night; hybrid/diesel +$3 per shift; owner-drivers pay none; medallion-only weekly $952 ($994 hybrid); medallion + conditional vehicle purchase $952/$994 + $275 per week [added by fact-check]; shift leases include maintenance
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-21(c)(1)-(4); section last amended eff. 2 May 2025 [corrected by fact-check: not a change in the cap amounts, which are long-standing (2012 [U])]; $105-129 per 12 h is about $9-11 per hour of fixed cost
variables.how_to_model: Persona choice (owner-driver, daily lessee, weekly lessee, medallion-only lessee); fixed cost charged at shift or week start; cross-link R08 and R09-003

variables.sub_box: B. Taxi money flows and lease costs
variables.name: Lease add-on charges
variables.description: Extra charges an owner may add to a taxi lease: gasoline, card processing and late return.
variables.values_or_range: Gas surcharge if the owner supplies fuel: banded on the trailing 6-month EIA NYC gasoline index, $16-31 per shift ($96-186/week) for ordinary cabs and $13-28 ($78-168) for hybrid/diesel, effective 31 Jul and 31 Dec [corrected by fact-check: $21/$126 was only the 2012 value]; card fee $7/shift or $49/week; late return up to $25/h, capped at one shift
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; EIA NYC gasoline prices https://www.eia.gov/petroleum/gasdiesel/
variables.how_to_model: Optional persona options; gas surcharge looked up from the index band on the replay date; late fee accrues per hour after shift end (cross-link R09-019)

variables.sub_box: B. Taxi money flows and lease costs
variables.name: Taxi toll pass-through rules
variables.description: Passengers pay the actual E-ZPass toll; on some bridges the passenger pays no toll one way and double the other way to cover the driver's return.
variables.values_or_range: Actual E-ZPass amount; none on Cross Bay, Marine Parkway and Verrazzano trips toward Brooklyn/Queens; 2x in the opposite direction; out-of-city: tolls both ways
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; tolls_amount field; toll rates in R10-021
variables.how_to_model: Toll table by crossing and direction with passenger multiplier 0, 1 or 2; driver pays unreimbursed tolls

variables.sub_box: C. App rider fares, surge and taxes
variables.name: App rider fare formula (upfront price)
variables.description: The price an app rider is quoted before booking, built from a base charge, per-mile and per-minute rates, a booking fee and a minimum fare.
variables.values_or_range: NYC 2025 average base_passenger_fare $27.66 (Uber), $25.09 (Lyft) [uncertain: average trip length not in the source; '~5-mile trips' unconfirmed]; mean fare per mile $7.81 / $7.14; short trips (<=3 mi) avg $14.46, long (10+ mi) $68.17
variables.impact_evidence: [S] FerrisSearch analysis of 243.6M 2025 HVFHV trips; rate cards are filed with TLC (35 RCNY 59D-17(a)) but not published [P*]
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (base_passenger_fare, trip_miles, trip_time) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
variables.how_to_model: Fit fare = a + b*miles + c*minutes + zone x hour effects, times surge (R07-020), on HVFHV records

variables.sub_box: C. App rider fares, surge and taxes
variables.name: Surge (dynamic pricing)
variables.description: Price multiplier or add-on that rises when local requests outrun available drivers; drivers see a surge map and an added amount per trip.
variables.values_or_range: Rider side 1.0-2.0x typical, rare spikes above 3x [U]; driver side +$1 to +$10 per trip [U]; NYC receipts must itemise any price multiplier
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-20(d)(6) receipts itemise the multiplier; [S] Cohen et al. 2016 elasticity about -0.5 near 1.2x (via R05-020)
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (fare residuals by zone-time); no public surge feed
variables.how_to_model: Surge = f(open requests / idle supply in zone over last 5-15 min), capped and smoothed; feeds rider conversion (R05) and driver offers

variables.sub_box: C. App rider fares, surge and taxes
variables.name: Ride product price levels
variables.description: Rider price and driver pay multipliers for app products such as standard, Comfort, XL, Black, WAV and Share.
variables.values_or_range: Comfort ~1.2-1.3x, XL ~1.5x, Black ~2-2.5x, Share up to 20% off [U]; WAV must not cost more than standard
variables.impact_evidence: [U] platform rate cards; [P*] 35 RCNY 78-15(b)(1)(ii) (no WAV premium on Flex); [P*] CNYCA: premium services average 40-60% higher fares; product mix from R05-024
variables.data_source: none found (HVFHV data flags only shared and WAV)
variables.how_to_model: Product multiplier table; vehicle eligibility from R08; driver opt-ins in R09-066

variables.sub_box: C. App rider fares, surge and taxes
variables.name: Fare estimate and quote rules
variables.description: Limits on how far an app's final charge may exceed the estimate it gave the rider.
variables.values_or_range: Estimate ranges at most 150% high-to-low; charge at most 120% of the estimate (or of the top of the range) unless the rider changes the trip; livery bases must give binding quotes
variables.how_to_model: Cap final charge at 1.2 x quote unless a destination change event occurs

variables.sub_box: C. App rider fares, surge and taxes
variables.name: Rider-side taxes and fees on app trips
variables.description: Taxes and fees added on top of the app base fare that the rider pays but the driver does not receive.
variables.values_or_range: Sales tax ~8.875% (2025 avg $2.32 on $27.66); Black Car Fund ~2.5% (avg $0.69); airport fee $2.50 per LGA/JFK/EWR pickup or drop-off; congestion $2.75; CBD $1.50; tolls
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] HVFHS dictionary (Mar 2025) fields and $2.50 airport fee; [S] 2025 fee averages (FerrisSearch); [S] 8.875% and 2.5-3% rates from GitHub analyses
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (sales_tax, bcf, airport_fee, congestion_surcharge, cbd_congestion_fee)
variables.how_to_model: Add to rider price before the conversion model; exclude from driver pay

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: Platform take rate (driver share of fare)
variables.description: The share of the rider's base fare that the platform pays the driver for a trip.
variables.values_or_range: NYC 2025 mean driver_pay / base fare 79% for both Uber and Lyft; 71-77% on Uber airport corridors (Lyft 83-84%); above 100% on some shared or WAV trips (shared unmatched 103%, Lyft WAV 204%); ~100% in 2019 vs ~80% in 2025 [S]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] FerrisSearch analysis of 243.6M 2025 HVFHV trips; [S] student analysis of HVFHV 2019-2025
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (driver_pay vs base_passenger_fare)
variables.how_to_model: Driver pay = max(NYC floor from R07-025/026, platform offer); offer = share(distance, zone, time) x fare + noise, fitted on HVFHV

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: NYC minimum pay: per-mile component
variables.description: TLC floor on what Uber or Lyft must pay per passenger mile in the city: an expense factor divided by an applied utilization rate.
variables.values_or_range: From 1 Aug 2025: $0.850/mi (WAV $1.061) / 68.5% = ~$1.24/mi (WAV ~$1.55); before: $0.789 / 58% = ~$1.36/mi (Mar 2024); 2019 factor $0.631; CPI-adjusted each 1 March [uncertain: Mar-Jul 2025 factor probably ~$0.820 (~$1.41/mi) [derived]; whether $0.850 is itself CPI-indexed from 1 Mar 2026, and the rates the TLC posted, could not be read]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-22(a)(1),(b) (amended eff. 1 Aug and 22 Sep 2025); [P*] CNYCA Feb 2025 expense model (proposed $0.871 non-WAV, $1.061 WAV; factor history); [S] 58% utilization in 2024 (Bloomberg via blog)
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; TLC driver pay page https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/driver-pay.page (blocked; URL not verified)
variables.how_to_model: Floor_miles = factor_mile / 0.685 x in-city passenger miles; use the rate in force on the replay date (R07-065)

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: NYC minimum pay: per-minute component
variables.description: TLC floor on what Uber or Lyft must pay per passenger minute in the city, also scaled up by a utilization rate.
variables.values_or_range: Base $0.287/min (2019) indexed to $0.338 by Mar 2024; / 53.3% from Aug 2025 = ~$0.63-0.69/min in 2025-26 [derived]; before Aug 2025 ~$0.58/min (58%, Mar 2024; ~$0.61 after the Mar 2025 CPI step [derived]); example 5 mi + 20 min trip floor ~ $19 [uncertain: the Aug 2025 rule was reported as a ~5% pay raise [S], which these derived rates (~+1% on that trip) do not reproduce; check posted rates]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-22(a)(2),(b); [P*] CNYCA factor table (Exhibit 2); [S] 58% utilization for 2024 (Bloomberg via blog)
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; TLC driver pay page (CPI-adjusted rates; blocked here)
variables.how_to_model: Floor_minutes = factor_min / 0.533 x in-city passenger minutes; slow traffic raises floor pay per trip (cross-link R10)

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: Out-of-city pay rates
variables.description: Higher per-mile and per-minute floor for the part of a trip that runs outside NYC, to cover the empty return.
variables.values_or_range: $1.700/mi (WAV $2.122) and $0.574/min outside the city, not divided by utilization; applies to the outside part of trips that start in NYC and end outside it
variables.how_to_model: Split the route at the city boundary; apply out-of-city rates to the outside part

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: Annual CPI indexation of pay factors
variables.description: Each 1 March the TLC raises the per-mile and per-minute factors by the NY-NJ-PA CPI-W change; it also resets them by rule from time to time.
variables.values_or_range: Time factor +1.4% (2020), +5.5% (2022), +6.5% (Feb 2023), +3.5% (Mar 2024); distance factor +1.4%, +5.2%, +6.1%, then a distance-only reset of +6.7% to $0.762 on 13 Mar 2023 (transport CPI) and +3.5% to $0.789 (Mar 2024) [added by fact-check]; no step in 2021 (Covid); 2024 CPI-W 3.9%; changes every year
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-22(a)(4); [P*] CNYCA Exhibit 2 (factor history)
variables.data_source: TLC driver pay page; BLS CPI-W NY-NJ-PA (bls.gov blocked here)
variables.how_to_model: Rate table keyed by effective date; select by replay date

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: Hourly pay compliance option
variables.description: A platform may instead pay drivers per hour of accepting dispatches, as long as each hour pays at least the per-mile and per-minute floor for that hour's passenger miles and minutes.
variables.values_or_range: On/off (per platform)
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-22(a)(5); NYC Admin Code 19-549(b)
variables.how_to_model: Alternative pay mode: hourly wage w, topped up to the floor sum per hour

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: Driver app access rules (lockouts)
variables.description: Limits on when Uber or Lyft may block a driver from logging on, introduced after platforms used lockouts to keep utilization high.
variables.values_or_range: Since 1 Aug 2025: 72 h notice before restricting a day; once online, access kept >=16 h (restarts after 8 h offline); exceptions for licensing, rule breaches, misconduct, excessive cancels or non-acceptance; $500 per violation. Before: lockouts nearly every hour (2024). From 28 Jul 2026, restrictions of 72 h+ in a row or 168 h+ per year count as deactivation under the just-cause law, and economic cuts follow reverse seniority (R07-045) [added by fact-check]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-22(c) and penalty table; [P*] NYC Admin Code 20-1281, 20-1284; [S] Bloomberg Oct 2024 and NYT Jun 2025 via blog summary
variables.how_to_model: Scenario toggle: 2024 regime (random or priority lockouts when supply is high) vs 2025 regime (notice + 16-h access) vs 2026 regime (adds deactivation limits); cross-link R09-042

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: Vehicle utilization standards and platform penalties
variables.description: City law lets the TLC set utilization standards for app vehicles and fine platforms per trip when they miss them; platforms may not pass the fine to drivers.
variables.values_or_range: Penalty $0.01-$0.10 per trip dispatched in the non-compliant 24 h for a first violation, $0.50-0.80 for a second within 24 months, $1-5 for later ones [added by fact-check]; $500-1,000 if deducted from driver pay; may vary by area, time, WAV and EV status
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] NYC Admin Code 19-550(b),(c),(e),(f)
variables.how_to_model: Fleet-level constraint: penalty per trip when fleet utilization in a period is below the standard

variables.sub_box: D. Platform take and the NYC driver pay floor
variables.name: Manhattan-core cruising cap
variables.description: Rule that the share of time available app vehicles spend empty in the congestion zone must stay under a cap, measured per platform.
variables.values_or_range: <=31% of available time cruising south of 96th St (36% from Feb 2020, 31% from Aug 2020), 06:00-23:00 weekdays and 08:00-23:00 weekends; WAVs exempt; fine $350 per 100 h over per month, suspension or revocation if more than 10% over; still printed in the rules but reported annulled by a state court in Dec 2019 [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-21 and penalty table; [U] court annulment; [corrected by fact-check: impact downgraded from medium because the rule is reportedly annulled and off by default; medium only when the toggle is on]
variables.how_to_model: Off by default; when on, the fleet manager tracks zone cruising share per month and pays the fine or holds cars outside the zone

variables.name: Quests (trip-count bonuses)
variables.description: Platform bonus for completing a set number of trips in a time window, often in tiers.
variables.values_or_range: e.g. $30 for 15 trips on a weekday, $100 for 40 trips over a weekend [design]; NYC amounts not public
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Uber and Lyft run quests; progress tracked in R09-025; can make a marginal trip worth far more than its fare
variables.how_to_model: Offer objects (window, thresholds, payout) issued per driver; pay on threshold crossing

variables.name: Streaks, consecutive-trip and zone boosts
variables.description: Small add-ons for taking trips back to back or starting trips in a boosted zone or time.
variables.values_or_range: $1-$5 per trip or a multiplier on surge zones [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] platform driver apps
variables.how_to_model: Per-trip add-on if conditions hold (consecutive acceptances, zone, time)

variables.name: Cancellation and no-show fees
variables.description: Fee a rider pays for cancelling late or not showing up, mostly passed to the driver; taxi e-hail apps may charge them only if listed in a filed fee schedule.
variables.values_or_range: Free window ~2 min after match; no-show after ~5 min wait; rider fee ~$5-10 in NYC [U]; driver share 75-100% [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 78-15(c)-(d) (e-hail fee schedules); [U] app amounts; frequencies from R05-022 and R05-037
variables.applies_to: human app driver, robotaxi, taxi e-hail
variables.data_source: none found (TLC records contain no cancelled trips)
variables.how_to_model: On rider cancel after free window or no-show timer, credit the driver the fee and free the car

variables.name: Wait-time (late rider) fee
variables.description: Per-minute charge when the rider keeps the driver waiting past a grace period at pickup.
variables.values_or_range: Grace ~2 min, then ~$0.30-0.60/min [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [U] platform help pages; lateness distribution in R05-038
variables.how_to_model: Accrue fee per minute after grace; pass to driver

variables.name: Tip pass-through rules
variables.description: Rules that all tips go to the driver and that riders can tip in-app; drivers may not ask for tips.
variables.values_or_range: 100% pass-through for apps, e-hail and taxi card tips; robotaxi: no tipping [U]; app tips ~4-5% of fare revenue, ~18% of rides tipped, ~20% among tippers (2025) [S]; yellow tip_amount records card tips only
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-17(b), 59B-23(h), 78-15(a), 80-17(a)(6); [P*] yellow dictionary (cash tips not included); [S] FerrisSearch 2025
variables.how_to_model: Tip amount from R05-047/048 goes 100% to the driver; zero for robotaxi

variables.name: Toll reimbursement on app trips
variables.description: Platforms must pass the full toll paid on a dispatched trip back to the driver; tolls on empty legs are the driver's cost.
variables.values_or_range: 100% of on-trip tolls; driver_pay excludes tolls and tips; empty-return tolls unreimbursed [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-17(c); [S] HVFHS dictionary: driver_pay 'not including tolls or tips'
variables.how_to_model: Credit on-trip tolls; charge deadhead tolls to the driver (toll table in R10-021)

variables.name: WAV trip pay premium
variables.description: Extra pay for trips done in wheelchair-accessible vehicles, from the higher floor factor and platform bonuses.
variables.values_or_range: Floor factor $1.061 vs $0.850 per mile; 2025 Lyft WAV driver pay ~204% of fare (flat ~$15/ride), Uber ~101%; taxis in the accessible programme must accept dispatches
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-22(a)(1), 53-08; [S] FerrisSearch 2025 WAV analysis (~699K WAV trips); matters for a WAV persona, low overall
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (wav_request_flag, wav_match_flag, driver_pay)
variables.how_to_model: WAV vehicle flag raises floor and adds a flat bonus per platform; WAV demand from R05-031

variables.name: Shared-ride pay treatment
variables.description: How drivers are paid when a rider books a discounted shared ride.
variables.values_or_range: Uber 2025: shared matched avg fare $21.04 (payout 94%), unmatched $16.34 (payout 103%) vs $28.02 standard (78%); drivers paid as normal trips [S]; drivers may not force sharing
variables.impact_evidence: [S] FerrisSearch 2025; [P*] 35 RCNY 80-19(c)(3) ($100 fine)
variables.data_source: NYC TLC HVFHV trip records (shared_request_flag, shared_match_flag)
variables.how_to_model: Rider gets discount; driver pay computed as a normal trip on actual miles and minutes

variables.sub_box: F. Offer information and account standing
variables.name: Information shown before accepting
variables.description: What the rules and apps let a driver see about a trip before committing to it.
variables.values_or_range: App: pickup, ETA, and in most US markets destination and upfront pay [U]; taxi e-hail: pickup, drop-off and fare estimate or binding Flex quote only, rider name only after accepting; taxi street hail: asking the destination before the rider is seated is a violation (except Flex Fare and returning-home cases); robotaxi dispatcher: everything
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 78-21(a)(3) (e-hail disclosure), 80-20(a)(4); [U] app practice in NYC
variables.how_to_model: Observation schema per driver type; duplicate of R05-036 (R07 owns the rule text)

variables.sub_box: F. Offer information and account standing
variables.name: Taxi refusal ban and penalties
variables.description: Taxi and green drivers must take riders to any destination in NYC, Westchester, Nassau or Newark and must not drop an accepted e-hail.
variables.values_or_range: Mandatory penalties: $350 pleaded / $500 after hearing first; $700 / $1,000 + up to 30-day suspension second within 24 months; $750 / $1,000 + revocation third within 36 months [upgraded to P* by fact-check]; allowed refusals: off-duty logged, >8 h operated for EWR/Westchester/Nassau, disorderly rider, unsecured animal, among others
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-20(a)-(b), 80-02(e) (refusal rows share the overcharge penalty cell); [S] fine amounts also via R09-032 (NBC/amNY)
variables.how_to_model: Taxi agent cannot decline after a hail; declining an accepted e-hail triggers a fine with detection probability p; cross-link R09-032

variables.sub_box: F. Offer information and account standing
variables.name: Acceptance-rate consequences
variables.description: What happens to an app driver who declines many offers: lost airport queue place, lower tier, and in NYC a lawful access restriction for excessive non-acceptance.
variables.values_or_range: Tier thresholds ~85-90% acceptance [S]; airport FIFO place lost after several declines [S]; declines reportedly unpenalised under upfront fares [S]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-22(c)(3) exception; [S] Uber JFK page and Gridwise via R09-040
variables.how_to_model: Rolling acceptance counter (state in R09-040) maps to queue loss, tier and lockout risk

variables.sub_box: F. Offer information and account standing
variables.name: Driver cancellation-rate consequences
variables.description: Penalties for cancelling a trip after accepting it.
variables.values_or_range: Uber Pro cap ~4% [S]; repeated cancels lose airport queue place [S]; excessive cancellation allows immediate NYC access restriction [P*]; taxi cancelling an accepted e-hail counts as a refusal [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Cancellation counter with thresholds triggering queue loss, tier loss or temporary access block

variables.sub_box: F. Offer information and account standing
variables.name: Rating and deactivation thresholds
variables.description: Rules under which a platform removes a driver: low average rating or compliance failures, now limited in NYC by a just-cause law.
variables.values_or_range: Rating floor ~4.6/5 commonly cited [U]; 99% of Uber NYC deactivations are compliance-related (licence, hour caps) [S]; [corrected by fact-check: NYC Admin Code 20-1281 to 20-1290 (L.L. 52 of 2026, eff. 28 Jul 2026) bars deactivation after a 30-day probation except for just cause, bona fide economic reason or legal requirement; needs written progressive discipline and 14 days' notice (none for egregious misconduct, account sharing or repeated fraud); restrictions of 72 h+ in a row or 168 h+ per year count as deactivation; economic layoffs need 120 days' notice, reverse seniority]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] NYC Council hearing Sept 2024 via R09-043; [P*] NYC Admin Code 20-1532 (delivery workers) and 20-1281 to 20-1290 (HVFHV drivers, L.L. 2026/052)
variables.data_source: NYC Admin Code via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive (rule); rating thresholds none found
variables.how_to_model: Terminal event if rating (R09-039) stays below floor or hour caps are breached repeatedly; for replay dates from 28 Jul 2026, require warnings and 14-day notice before a non-misconduct deactivation

variables.sub_box: F. Offer information and account standing
variables.name: TLC points (persistent violator programme)
variables.description: Licence suspension or revocation when a driver collects too many TLC and DMV points.
variables.values_or_range: 6-9 points in 15 months: suspension up to 30 days; 10+: revocation; e.g. phone use 3-4 points, reckless driving 4 points; course can remove 3 points (TLC points at most once per 5 years)
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-27, 80-14 penalty tables
variables.how_to_model: Points ledger from violations; suspension removes the driver for N days

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: TLC passenger-time cap and fines
variables.description: NYC limit on how long a taxi or for-hire driver may carry passengers per day and week.
variables.values_or_range: <=10 h passenger time in any 24 h (resets after 8 consecutive hours with no passengers); <=60 h per Mon-Sun week; time between trips not counted; a last trip begun under the limit is a defence; fines $50/$75 up to 1 h over, $100/$150 for 1-2 h, $150/$200 for 2-3 h, $200/$300 for 3-4 h, $300/$400 beyond; 5-15 day suspension after 3+ violations of 4 h+ in a month
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-14(f) and penalty table (amended eff. 6 Mar 2025)
variables.how_to_model: Rolling counters; block new trips or fine per extra hour; duplicate of R09-005 (R07 adds the fine schedule)

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: Street-hail legality by vehicle type and zone
variables.description: Which vehicles may pick up riders who wave from the street, and where.
variables.values_or_range: Yellow: anywhere, but no cruising for fares at JFK/LGA/EWR or within 100 ft of a taxi stand; airport pickups only via stands and feed lines [corrected by fact-check]; green: only in the Hail Zone (not Manhattan south of E 96th/W 110th St, not airports), fines $500 + suspension, $750 + suspension, revocation; FHV/app: never (fines $200-350, in the exclusionary zone $500/$750/revocation); robotaxi: app only
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-19(a)-(c), 82-13 and penalty tables, 59B-23(d), 51-03 (zone definitions)
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; TLC taxi zone shapefile
variables.how_to_model: Hail encounters (R05-042) only offered to vehicle types and zones where legal; illegal pickups fined with detection probability

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: Taxi solicitation and stand rules
variables.description: Where taxis may cruise for fares and how taxi stand queues work.
variables.values_or_range: No cruising for fares at JFK, LGA, EWR, within 100 ft of a stand, or on Lincoln Center private streets; join the back of a stand line; first two cabs stay in the seat; relief use <=1 h; fines $50-150
