variables.how_to_model: Stand objects with FIFO queues; cruising pickups disabled near stands and at airports

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: Off-duty 'returning home' pickup exception
variables.description: A logged-off taxi may still take a rider whose destination is directly on its route home or to the garage, and may ask the destination first.
variables.values_or_range: Allowed only if logged off, trip record marked 'Returning to garage/home', and destination on route; green: only inside the Hail Zone; fine $75/$100 if misused
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-19(a)(5),(b)(6), 80-20(a)(4)(i); the legal form of the team's 'take me home' idea for taxis
variables.how_to_model: Action go_home_offduty: hails accepted only if destination reduces distance to home; cross-link R09-020, R05-060

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: Airport pickup rules
variables.description: How each vehicle type may pick up at NYC airports.
variables.values_or_range: Taxi: holding lot and feed line, separate short-haul and long-haul tickets at some terminals (no swapping); app: may not accept a dispatch while parked at JFK/LGA pickup areas ($250 fine), so waits in staging lots; app airport fee $2.50; NYC taxis may not solicit at EWR
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-19(a)(4), (e)-(f); [P*] HVFHS dictionary airport_fee; queue dynamics in R09-057 and R05-063
variables.how_to_model: Per-airport queue objects by vehicle type; short-haul ticket gives priority re-entry [design]

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: Shortest-route rule and overcharge penalties
variables.description: Drivers must take the shortest reasonable route unless the rider asks otherwise; overcharging is heavily fined.
variables.values_or_range: Shortest-route violation $100/$150 (80-16(a)) [added by fact-check]; overcharge: $350/$500 first, $700/$1,000 + up to 30 days second within 24 months, revocation third within 36 months; overcharge of $10+ means revocation; note NYC app floor pay uses actual miles and minutes
variables.how_to_model: Detours beyond x% over the shortest route raise complaint and fine probability; blocks the long-hauling exploit

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: Phone and app use while moving
variables.description: TLC drivers may use an electronic device only while lawfully standing or parked; taxi e-hail apps may allow single-touch accept, cancel or arrived buttons while moving [corrected by fact-check: no matching exception for Uber/Lyft driver apps was found].
variables.values_or_range: Fine $250/$350 + suspension (deferred if course done) + 3-4 points
variables.how_to_model: Restrict complex agent actions (e.g. browsing offers) to stopped states; single-tap accept in motion only for taxi e-hail

variables.sub_box: G. Hours, hailing, airports and conduct
variables.name: Taxi payment acceptance rules
variables.description: Taxi drivers must accept cash and cards without mark-up and be able to make change.
variables.values_or_range: Card and cash mandatory; no card surcharge to riders (fines $200/$300/$500); change for $20; non-payers: log fare and go to police
variables.how_to_model: Payment type from R05-050; small time cost for cash; dispute path for non-payment (R05-057)

variables.sub_box: H. Licensing, insurance and market entry
variables.name: TLC licensing and compliance costs
variables.description: Fees and courses a driver must pay for to get and keep a TLC licence and a licensed vehicle.
variables.values_or_range: Driver licence $84/yr ($252 per 3 yrs); one-time 24-h course $250 + exam $49, fingerprints $90.25, WAV training $100, DMV E-class $107.50; drug test $34/yr; vehicle licence $550 per 2 yrs; owner total ~$1,382/yr = ~$0.043/mile
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 80-07; [P*] CNYCA Feb 2025, Appendix Exhibit 4
variables.how_to_model: Fixed annual cost amortised per hour or mile in the cost ledger (cross-link R08)

variables.sub_box: H. Licensing, insurance and market entry
variables.name: Insurance requirements and premiums
variables.description: Minimum insurance for TLC vehicles and AV test vehicles, and what drivers actually pay.
variables.values_or_range: TLC minimum: $100k PIP per person, $100k/$300k bodily injury, $10k property, 24/7 cover; median FHV premium $4,548/yr (gas) and $4,750 (EV) = ~$0.14/mile; AV testing: $5M auto, $3M personal liability, $2M property
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-13(d), 59A-12(c); [P*] CNYCA driver survey 2024; [P*] 34 RCNY 4-17(d)(10)
variables.how_to_model: Annual premium as fixed cost per vehicle; AV fleet uses the higher minimum (cost values in R08)

variables.sub_box: H. Licensing, insurance and market entry
variables.name: FHV licence cap and Green Rides mandate
variables.description: Limits on new for-hire vehicle licences and a required rising share of app trips done by zero-emission or wheelchair-accessible vehicles.
variables.values_or_range: New FHV licences frozen since Aug 2018 except EVs and WAVs; ZEV/WAV trip share 5% (2024), 15% (2025), 25% (2026), 40% (2027), 60% (2028), 80% (2029), 100% (2030); $50 per 1,000 trips short plus a corrective plan; actual 19.7% in Aug 2024; target changes every year
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59D-13(c) and penalty table; [P*] CNYCA (licence pause, GRI adopted Oct 2023, Aug 2024 share)
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive; TLC vehicle licence lists on NYC Open Data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Platforms may prioritise EV/WAV dispatch to meet the quota [design]; fleet may only add EV or WAV units in NYC

variables.sub_box: H. Licensing, insurance and market entry
variables.name: Operator licence fees for a fleet
variables.description: Fixed fees a company running its own fleet or app would pay in NYC.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHS licence $190,000/yr; TLC vehicle licence $550 per car per 2 yrs; NYC AV test permit $5,000/yr
variables.how_to_model: Fixed fleet overhead per day in the fleet profit ledger

variables.sub_box: I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
variables.name: Robotaxi legal status by jurisdiction
variables.description: Whether paid driverless rides are allowed in the simulated city, which decides if the robotaxi track is real or counterfactual.
variables.values_or_range: NYC: testing only with a trained safety driver (8 Waymo cars, Manhattan south of 112th St and Downtown Brooklyn); state permits expired 31 Mar 2026; Feb 2026 state proposal (excluding NYC) withdrawn; NY law requires a hand on the wheel. Permissive: 28 states per Vital City, including AZ, CA, FL, GA, TN, TX where Waymo operates (11 Waymo cities, ~3,000 cars, May 2026) [corrected by fact-check]; ambiguous: WA (Seattle human-driver rule), IL. Effectively barred: NY, MA, NJ
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Vital City Waymo map methodology (6 May 2026) citing THE CITY, CNBC, TechCrunch; [P*] 34 RCNY 4-17
variables.data_source: Vital City waymo-map https://github.com/vitalcity-nyc/waymo-map; NCSL AV legislation tracker [U]
variables.how_to_model: Scenario flag: NYC counterfactual (use R07-064 mapping) or a permissive city rule pack (R07-067); if a safety driver is required, add wage and hour rules (R09-051)

variables.sub_box: I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
variables.name: Operating design domain (where and when a robotaxi may drive)
variables.description: The approved service polygon, hours, road types and conditions for a robotaxi; requests outside it cannot be served.
variables.values_or_range: NYC permit: only DOT-approved areas, dates and hours; Waymo Nashville launch 60 sq mi; airports and freeways added city by city [U]; pauses in severe weather [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 34 RCNY 4-17(f)(3)-(4); [S] Vital City (Nashville area); freeway access in R10-023
variables.data_source: Waymo service-area maps [U]; path-avmap av-map-data boundaries https://github.com/path-avmap/av-map-data
variables.how_to_model: Polygon + time windows + weather thresholds; out-of-ODD requests rejected or handed to human drivers

variables.sub_box: I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
variables.name: Robotaxi fare structure
variables.description: How a Waymo-like service prices rides: base charge, per mile, per minute, with dynamic adjustment.
variables.values_or_range: SF ~$9.52 + $1.66/mi + $0.30/min (avg ride ~$20.43); LA ~$5.37 + $2.50/mi + $0.32/min; premium ~31% over Uber and ~41% over Lyft (Apr 2025: $20.43 vs $15.58 vs $14.44), narrowing to ~12.7% over Uber and ~27.3% over Lyft (late 2025) [corrected by fact-check]; $29.99/month subscription [S]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] industry notes citing Obi data via TechCrunch (Jun 2025, Jan 2026) and Waymo pricing help page
variables.data_source: Waymo trip pricing https://support.google.com/waymo/answer/9059184; Obi price reports [S]
variables.how_to_model: Rate card plus dynamic multiplier; rider uptake via AV premium in R05-027

variables.sub_box: I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
variables.name: Robotaxi network partner revenue split
variables.description: Share kept by Uber or Lyft when robotaxis are booked through their apps.
variables.values_or_range: Undisclosed [U]; design default 20-30% of fare [design]; Austin (Mar 2025) and Atlanta (Jun 2025) via Uber, Nashville (7 Apr 2026) via Lyft [corrected by fact-check: dates]
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Vital City operating-city table; [U] contract terms
variables.how_to_model: Fleet revenue = fare x (1 - partner share) for partner-dispatched trips

variables.sub_box: I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
variables.name: Robotaxi incident reporting and enforcement
variables.description: Duties after crashes and rule breaches that can take robotaxis off the road.
variables.values_or_range: NYC permit: crash notice within 4 h, periodic data (miles, takeovers, shift lengths, NHTSA SGO reports), stop within 24 h of suspension; NHTSA Standing General Order crash reports; California AB 1777 police notices to AV companies and emergency geofencing [uncertain: signed 2024, operative 1 Jul 2026 per background knowledge; not checked]
variables.how_to_model: Incident event removes the vehicle for a review period; emergency geofences block zones temporarily

variables.sub_box: I. Robotaxi regulation and operating domain
variables.name: NYC robotaxi fee mapping (counterfactual)
variables.description: Design choice of which NYC rule set a hypothetical robotaxi follows, since no commercial rule exists.
variables.values_or_range: Option A (FHV-like): upfront fare, $2.75 congestion, $1.50 CBD, $2.50 airport fee, no hails, no pay floor; Option B (taxi-like): meter, hails, medallion needed; plus whether empty robotaxis pay the $9 daily CRZ car toll (peak; 75% less overnight [S])
variables.impact_evidence: [design] no NYC commercial pathway exists (R07-059); choice shifts fees by several dollars per trip
variables.how_to_model: Rule-pack switch read by pricing and fee modules

variables.name: Rule-set vintage matched to the replay date
variables.description: The fares, fees, pay floors and caps used must match the date of the demand being replayed, or be a declared counterfactual.
variables.values_or_range: Key dates: taxi fare 18 Dec 2022; HVFHV distance-factor reset 13 Mar 2023; CBD toll 5 Jan 2025; HVFHV floor and access rules 1 Aug 2025; CPI step each 1 March; Green Rides step each 1 Jan; HVFHV wrongful-deactivation law 28 Jul 2026; CRZ step-up 2028 [U] [corrected by fact-check: 'lease caps 2 May 2025' removed; that date is a later amendment to 58-21, not a change in the cap amounts]
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] amendment histories in the rules archive; mismatch can bias revenue by 5-15% [design guess]; cross-link R10-064
variables.how_to_model: Versioned rule tables with effective dates; harness asserts data date and rule date agree

variables.name: Profit accounting definition
variables.description: Exactly which money counts in the score: driver pay, tips, bonuses, minus pass-throughs, lease, vehicle costs, fees, and optionally tax.
variables.values_or_range: Pre-tax by default; optional self-employment tax 15.3% and IRS mileage rate $0.70/mi (2025; 2026 rate not checked) [design]; pass-throughs always excluded
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] CNYCA cites IRS 2025 rate $0.70/mi; [design] rankings can change when costs are included
variables.how_to_model: Single ledger with component tags; score views: gross, net of costs, after tax

variables.name: City rule pack (generalisation beyond NYC)
variables.description: Swappable bundle of fare, fee, pay-floor and hailing rules so the same engine can run other cities.
variables.values_or_range: NYC default; stubs for e.g. Seattle and Minnesota per-mile/per-minute floors, California Prop 22 engaged-time guarantee, Chicago ground-transport tax [U]; Seattle local rule requiring a human driver in AVs [S]
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; values for other cities not verified this session [U]; [S] Vital City (Seattle AV rule)
variables.how_to_model: Config files per city with the same schema as the NYC tables

variables.name: Powertrain type
variables.description: Whether the car runs on gasoline, is a hybrid or plug-in hybrid, or is battery-electric, which sets energy cost per mile, refuelling downtime and licence eligibility.
variables.values_or_range: Gas (e.g. Camry 2.5L LE/SE, EPA 28 city / 39 highway mpg [P*]); hybrid (Camry Hybrid LE 51/53 mpg [P*], RAV4 Hybrid 41/38 [P*], Sienna hybrid about 36 [U]); plug-in hybrid; battery EV (Model 3 2019 trims 0.25-0.29 kWh/mi [P*], Model Y about 0.28 [U], Ioniq 5 about 0.30 [U], Niro EV 0.30 [P*], Jaguar I-PACE 0.44 [corrected by fact-check: EPA 44.3 kWh/100 mi, not about 0.40]). Energy cost per mile at $3.40/gal and $0.30-0.60/kWh: hybrid about $0.07-0.08, gas sedan about $0.11, large SUV about $0.17, EV $0.10 (home) to $0.15-0.18 (DC fast); I-PACE-class robotaxi about $0.22-0.26 on public DC fast or $0.07-0.12 at a depot [corrected by fact-check].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] calculation from the listed ratings and prices: about a 2-3x spread in energy cost per mile across powertrains, plus very different refuel and charge downtime; EPA ratings for model years 2019-2020 confirmed in the EPA vehicles file via a GitHub copy (rfordatascience/tidytuesday big_epa_cars.csv) [P*]; post-2020 models [U].
variables.data_source: EPA fuel economy data https://www.fueleconomy.gov/feg/download.shtml (2019-2020 values checked via GitHub copy [P*]); NYC Open Data 'For Hire Vehicles (FHV) - Active' and 'Medallion Vehicles - Authorized' lists https://opendata.cityofnewyork.us [U] [uncertain: believed to hold VIN, vehicle year, WAV flag and a vehicle-type code but not make or model; decode VINs with NHTSA vPIC https://vpic.nhtsa.dot.gov/api/]. TLC trip records carry no vehicle or fuel field [P*].
variables.how_to_model: Vehicle spec table (powertrain, consumption curve, tank or battery size, refuel or charge behaviour, maintenance rates); each car is assigned one spec.

variables.name: Service class and product eligibility
variables.description: Which ride products the car qualifies for (standard, Comfort, XL, Black, Black SUV, wheelchair-accessible, Green or Comfort Electric), which sets the fare tier it earns and the pool it competes in.
variables.values_or_range: Standard sedan; Comfort (newer, roomier car); XL (6 or more rider seats); Black (luxury sedan, black-car base); Black SUV; WAV; Green / Comfort Electric (EV or hybrid). Premium tiers need newer model years [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] premium tiers pay roughly 1.5-2.5x standard per mile but need $60-100k vehicles; [P*] HVFHV records have no product field, only shared and WAV flags (schema in toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data; confirmed by the R06 and R09 fact-checks).
variables.applies_to: human app driver, fleet (taxi and robotaxi each have one class)
variables.data_source: Uber and Lyft vehicle requirement pages [U]; no public NYC class mix (see R06-007).
variables.how_to_model: Class flag on each car filters eligible offers (R06 matcher) and selects the fare table (R07); a higher class raises capex, insurance and fuel use.

variables.name: Rider seat capacity
variables.description: How many riders the car may carry, which decides whether it can take larger groups.
variables.values_or_range: Sedan 4 riders; XL minivan or SUV 6; NYC yellow taxi 4, or 5 in a five-passenger cab, plus one child under 7 on an adult's lap; no vehicle may exceed its DMV-registered seating (35 RCNY 80-15(e)) [P*]; Waymo I-PACE 4 [U]; Zoox 4 [U]; Tesla Cybercab 2 [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Yellow taxi trips 2023 with a recorded passenger count (36.2M of the 37.2M with a fare; 1.6% record 0) [corrected by fact-check: denominator]: 75.2% carried 1 passenger, 15.2% 2, 3.8% 3, 2.1% 4, 1.3% 5 and 0.9% 6, so about 2.2% of parties need more than four seats (medium for an XL car, which earns on these).
variables.data_source: TLC yellow trip records passenger_count https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page (HVFHV records have no party size); 35 RCNY 80-15 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*].
variables.how_to_model: Draw party size from the yellow passenger_count distribution by zone and hour; offers with party size above the seat count go only to XL cars.

variables.name: Luggage space
variables.description: Trunk volume, which limits airport and long-distance trips with several bags.
variables.values_or_range: Sedan trunk about 15 cu ft (2-3 large bags); SUV or minivan 30+ cu ft; rider bags 0-4 per airport trip [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [P] JFK and LGA trips are 3.75% of HVFHV drop-offs and 3.54% of pickups (Jan 2023; re-matched to the script output), and only a fraction overflow a sedan trunk [design].
variables.data_source: none found (no luggage field in TLC data)
variables.how_to_model: Airport trips carry a bag count; if it exceeds the trunk, the rider rebooks an XL or cancels (R05).

variables.name: Wheelchair-accessible vehicle (WAV)
variables.description: Whether the car has a ramp or lift, which costs more to buy and run but earns WAV incentives and serves WAV and Access-A-Ride trips.
variables.values_or_range: WAV minivan conversion about $55-80k vs about $30-35k for a hybrid sedan [U]; Taxi Improvement Fund for WAV taxis: one-time hack-up payment of at least $20,000 plus $10,000 in quarterly operating payments over 4 years, and $10 to the driver per accessible-dispatch trip, funded by the $1.00 Taxicab Improvement Surcharge (35 RCNY 58-50(i), 51-03) [P*]; medallion-only weekly lease of a required accessible taxi carries a $77/week driver credit (58-21(c)(3)(ii)) [P*]; HVFHV minimum pay per mile $1.061 for WAV trips vs $0.850, about 25% more (59D-22(a)(1)) [P*]; since 18 Oct 2024 every newly hacked-up yellow taxi must be an accessible model (67-06(a)) [P*]; ramp loading adds about 2-5 min dwell [design]. HVFHV Jan 2023: WAV requested on 0.15% (Uber) and 0.14% (Lyft) of trips, but 6.4% and 7.1% of trips were served by a WAV [P].
variables.impact_evidence: [P] HVFHV Jan 2023 wav_request_flag vs wav_match_flag: WAVs mostly carry ordinary riders, so the extra capex must be recovered through incentives, the higher WAV pay floor and WAV-only offers; WAV trips also count toward the Green Rides quota (59D-13(c)) [P*].
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (default for new yellow cabs), fleet
variables.data_source: TLC HVFHV trip records (wav_request_flag, wav_match_flag; access_a_ride_flag is blank or 'N' in Jan 2023, so unusable) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; 35 RCNY 58-50, 59D-22, 67-06 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]; NYC Open Data FHV active list WAV flag [U].
variables.how_to_model: WAV flag raises capex, fuel use and dwell; enables WAV-only offers (R06-030), per-trip incentives and the higher WAV pay floor (R07); TIF payments for taxi owners.

variables.name: Vehicle age, odometer and condition
variables.description: Model year and accumulated miles of the car, which drive maintenance and breakdown rates, product eligibility and, for taxis only, the TLC retirement date (FHVs have no TLC age limit) [corrected by fact-check].
variables.values_or_range: Model year 0-7+ years old; odometer 0-300k+ miles; full-time NYC app use about 30-45k miles a year [design: about 700 miles per 50-hour week]; double-shifted yellow cabs run more [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] maintenance and breakdown rates rise with mileage and premium tiers use model-year cut-offs; mileage from our cost stack [design].
variables.data_source: NYC Open Data FHV active and medallion vehicle lists (vehicle year) [U] [uncertain: field names not re-read; NYC Open Data blocked]
variables.how_to_model: State updated per mile and per day; feeds breakdown hazard (R08-054), maintenance (R08-045), eligibility (R08-002) and taxi retirement (R08-040).

variables.sub_box: Energy use per mile and per hour
variables.name: Energy use per mile by speed (drive cycle)
variables.description: Fuel or electricity used per mile as a function of average speed and stop-and-go, so a Manhattan crawl costs a gas car much more per mile than an expressway run.
variables.values_or_range: Gas sedan about 18-25 mpg below 10 mph vs 30-39 mpg at 25-45 mph [U]; EPA city vs highway: 2.5L Camry 28 vs 39 mpg, Camry Hybrid 51 vs 53, I-PACE 42.2 vs 46.8 kWh/100 mi (EVs use less in the city) [P*]; hybrid about 40-50 mpg in city traffic [U]; EV 0.22-0.35 kWh/mi (0.44 for I-PACE), nearly flat in city traffic [U]; EPA's 'New York City Cycle' test averages about 7 mph [U]. HVFHV same-borough on-trip speeds Jan 2023: Manhattan 10.8 mph, Brooklyn 11.2, Bronx 13.5, Queens 15.9, Staten Island 17.0 [P].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] energy is only about 3-6% of gross per online hour for a hybrid or EV, but per-mile cost for a non-hybrid roughly doubles in crawl traffic [U]; on-trip speeds [P] re-matched to the script output; EPA city/highway split [P*].
variables.data_source: EPA ratings https://www.fueleconomy.gov [U] (2019-2020 via GitHub copy [P*]); NREL FASTSim or EPA MOVES speed-consumption curves [U]; TLC trip speeds https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page [P].
variables.how_to_model: Per-link consumption = f(powertrain, link speed from R10) with a stop-and-go penalty, e.g. c(v) = a/v + b + c*v^2 fitted per powertrain; the agent sees the gauge and trip cost estimates, not the curve.

variables.sub_box: Energy use per mile and per hour
variables.name: Idling and waiting energy
variables.description: Fuel or electricity burned while the car waits with the engine or climate system on (airport lots, staging spots, traffic).
variables.values_or_range: Gas car about 0.2-0.5 gal/h depending on engine size and AC (about $0.70-1.70/h at $3.40/gal) [U]; large SUV up to about 0.8 gal/h [U]; a hybrid's engine cycles on for heat or AC; EV about 0.3 kW baseline plus HVAC 0.5-6 kW [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] fueleconomy.gov and Argonne idling guidance (a quarter to half a gallon per hour); matters per trip when airport queues run 1-3 h (R06-041).
variables.how_to_model: Energy draw per stationary minute by powertrain and HVAC state; the anti-idling rule (R10-034) can force engine-off waits in gas cars, EVs exempt; idling while parked can also draw a $100 ticket (19 RCNY 39-05(r)) [P*].

variables.sub_box: Energy use per mile and per hour
variables.name: Climate control load (AC and heat)
variables.description: Extra energy for air conditioning or heating, set by outside temperature, which matters most for EVs in winter.
variables.values_or_range: AC cuts a conventional car's mpg about 5-25% in very hot weather [U]; EV resistive heater 3-6 kW, heat pump 1-2 kW [U]; close to zero on mild days.
variables.impact_evidence: [U] AAA 2019 EV temperature test and fueleconomy.gov AC guidance (medium for EVs in winter, low otherwise).
variables.data_source: NOAA NCEI hourly temperature, Central Park https://www.ncei.noaa.gov [U]
variables.how_to_model: HVAC kW = g(temperature from R04) applied for every minute in service or waiting; also a small rider-comfort term for ratings.

variables.sub_box: Energy use per mile and per hour
variables.name: Cold- and hot-weather EV range and charging loss
variables.description: EV range and DC fast-charging speed fall in cold weather (and somewhat in heat), forcing more and longer charging stops.
variables.values_or_range: Range down about 20-41% at about 20°F with heating, about 17% at 95°F with AC [U]; fast-charge power reduced until the pack warms (preconditioning helps) [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] AAA 2019 study (-41% at 20°F with HVAC, -17% at 95°F); Recurrent fleet data (about 20-30% winter loss); not re-read in this session.
variables.data_source: NOAA temperature [U]; AAA and Recurrent reports [U]
variables.how_to_model: Temperature factors multiply consumption and divide charge power by hour of day.

variables.sub_box: Energy use per mile and per hour
variables.name: Driving style and eco-driving
variables.description: How hard the driver accelerates and brakes, which changes fuel use and wear on the same route.
variables.values_or_range: Aggressive driving lowers mileage about 10-40% in stop-and-go traffic [U]; smooth baseline; robotaxi uses a smooth profile [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] fueleconomy.gov driving guidance; pairs with the speed factor in R09-029.
variables.how_to_model: Persona multiplier on consumption and on brake and tyre wear, tied to the R09-029 speed factor.

variables.sub_box: Energy use per mile and per hour
variables.name: Gas refuelling stop
variables.description: Time and detour to refuel a gas or hybrid car, which happens rarely but costs unpaid minutes.
variables.values_or_range: Tank 13-18 gal; urban range about 350-650 mi (hybrids at the top) [U]; stop 5-10 min plus 0-15 min detour, few stations in Manhattan (R01-064); about one stop per 1-2 shifts [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] at about 700 mi a week a hybrid refuels about twice a week; station scarcity [U] via R01-064.
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (gas and hybrid cars)
variables.data_source: OpenStreetMap amenity=fuel https://www.openstreetmap.org ; AFDC for alternative fuels https://afdc.energy.gov/stations
variables.how_to_model: Fuel-level state; the refuel action (R09-059) routes to a station POI, dwells 5-10 min, pays gallons x local price.

variables.name: Gasoline retail price (NYC)
variables.description: Pump price per gallon of regular gasoline in New York City on the replayed date.
variables.values_or_range: Roughly $3.10-3.70/gal in 2024-2026, peak about $5.00 in June 2022 [U]; weekly series.
variables.impact_evidence: [design] a $1/gal swing moves a 45-mpg hybrid's cost by about $0.02/mi (about $16 a week at 700 mi) and a 20-mpg SUV's by $0.05/mi; price levels [U] (eia.gov blocked here). [fact-check: the TLC indexes its optional taxi gas surcharge ($13-31 a shift) to a 6-month average of the EIA New York City gasoline price (35 RCNY 58-21(c)(6)) [P*], confirming the EIA NYC series as the regulator's reference; borderline medium, about 1-2% of gross per $1/gal for a hybrid.]
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (gas and hybrid)
variables.data_source: EIA weekly retail gasoline, New York City (series EMM_EPMR_PTE_Y35NY_DPG) https://www.eia.gov/dnav/pet/hist/LeafHandler.ashx?n=PET&s=EMM_EPMR_PTE_Y35NY_DPG&f=W [series ID U]
variables.how_to_model: Daily price interpolated from the EIA weekly series for the scenario date, plus station markups (R08-014).

variables.name: Station-level price spread and fuel detours
variables.description: Prices differ between stations (Manhattan dearer, outer boroughs and New Jersey cheaper), so a driver may detour to save.
variables.values_or_range: Spread about $0.20-0.80/gal within the metro area; New Jersey often cheaper because of lower fuel tax [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background; station-level price data is proprietary (no public series).
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (gas and hybrid)
variables.data_source: none found public (GasBuddy is proprietary); station locations from OpenStreetMap.
variables.how_to_model: Station markup = borough or state offset + noise; the agent trades detour minutes against savings.

variables.name: Fuel price shocks and supply disruptions
variables.description: Sudden fuel price jumps or shortages that raise costs or limit refuelling.
variables.values_or_range: 2022 spike to about $5/gal [U]; November 2012 post-Sandy odd-even gas rationing in NYC with long station queues [U] [uncertain: the 2012 order is recalled as exempting taxis, livery and other commercial vehicles, so the plate rule may not have bound TLC cars even though the queues did].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background (EIA price history; 2012 rationing order); high impact inside such a scenario.
variables.how_to_model: Scenario event scaling price and adding station queue time or odd-even plate rules (with TLC exemption flag) (link R03 disruptions).

variables.name: Home electricity price
variables.description: Residential electricity price paid for overnight home charging.
variables.values_or_range: Con Edison residential all-in about $0.25-0.38/kWh, higher in summer; time-of-use overnight rates lower [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] at $0.30/kWh with 12% losses an EV costs about $0.10/mi, vs $0.15-0.18/mi on public fast chargers; tariff levels [U]. Medium only for drivers with home charging (R08-029).
variables.applies_to: human app driver (EV with home charging)
variables.data_source: EIA Electric Power Monthly (NY residential average) https://www.eia.gov/electricity/monthly/ [U]; Con Edison tariffs https://www.coned.com [U]
variables.how_to_model: Price per kWh by hour (flat or time-of-use) applied to home sessions.

variables.name: Public DC fast-charging price
variables.description: Price per kWh (or per minute) at public fast chargers, the main EV energy cost for NYC drivers without home charging.
variables.values_or_range: About $0.40-0.65/kWh across Tesla Supercharger, EVgo, Electrify America and Revel sites in NYC; some per-minute pricing; member plans 10-25% off [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] at $0.50/kWh and 0.30 kWh/mi an EV pays about $0.15/mi, about double a 45-mpg hybrid at $3.40/gal ($0.076/mi), so EV energy savings in NYC depend on where the driver charges; prices [U].
variables.applies_to: human app driver (EV), robotaxi (if no depot), fleet
variables.data_source: AFDC station locator and API (network, connector, pricing text) https://afdc.energy.gov/stations [U]; network price pages [U]
variables.how_to_model: Price per kWh by network and hour; session cost = kWh to battery / efficiency x price + session fees.

variables.name: Public Level 2 and curbside charging price
variables.description: Price for slower public charging at the curb or in garages, often charged per hour.
variables.values_or_range: NYC DOT curbside Level 2 pilot about $2.50/h daytime and about $1/h overnight [U]; garage Level 2 often bundled with a parking fee [U]; 6-11 kW.
variables.impact_evidence: [U] NYC DOT curbside charging pilot (2021) background; useful only for long breaks or overnight.
variables.data_source: AFDC Level 2 sites https://afdc.energy.gov/stations; NYC DOT electric vehicle pages https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/motorist/electric-vehicles.shtml [U]
variables.how_to_model: Hourly price plus occupied parking time; charge power from R08-024.

variables.name: Time-of-day energy pricing and idle fees
variables.description: Charging prices that change by hour (off-peak discounts) and penalties for staying plugged in after charging ends.
variables.values_or_range: Off-peak fast-charging discounts of about 20-50% overnight at some networks; idle or overstay fees about $0.40-1.00/min when a site is busy; Con Edison time-of-use super-off-peak overnight [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] network pricing policies (e.g. Tesla time-of-use and idle fees), not re-read here.
variables.how_to_model: Price table by hour; idle fee accrues per minute if the car stays after the session ends.

variables.name: Depot electricity tariff and demand charges
variables.description: Commercial electricity price for a fleet depot, including monthly charges on peak kW that punish many cars fast-charging at once.
variables.values_or_range: Energy about $0.12-0.25/kWh plus demand charges about $15-50 per kW-month on commercial tariffs [U]; NY utility EV fleet programmes reduce demand charges [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] 20 chargers x 150 kW peaking together = 3 MW, i.e. roughly $45k-150k a month in demand charges at those rates; tariff levels [U].
variables.data_source: Con Edison commercial tariffs https://www.coned.com [U]; NY PSC / NYSERDA EV programmes [U]
variables.how_to_model: Depot bill = kWh x energy price + monthly peak kW x demand rate; the fleet agent can stagger charging to cut the peak.

variables.name: Platform fuel and charging discounts, EV per-trip incentives
variables.description: Discounts and bonuses that platforms or programmes give on fuel, charging or EV trips.
variables.values_or_range: Fuel cash back of a few cents per gallon or 1-6% via driver rewards tiers [U]; charging discounts at partner networks [U]; per-trip EV bonus about $1 on some EV products, and EV ride-product premiums for riders [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Uber Pro and Lyft rewards pages (not re-read).
variables.data_source: Uber Pro and Lyft driver rewards pages [U]
variables.how_to_model: Multiplier on fuel and charging cost plus an add-on per eligible trip (pay rules in R07).

variables.name: Battery capacity and usable range
variables.description: Usable battery energy and the range it gives, which decides how often an EV must stop during a shift.
variables.values_or_range: Model 3 about 57-75 kWh (EPA 220-310 mi for 2019-2020 trims [P*], about 270-360 mi for 2021-2024 [U]) [corrected by fact-check]; Model Y about 60-79 kWh (about 260-330 mi) [U]; Ioniq 5 about 77 kWh (about 260-300 mi) [U]; Niro EV about 65 kWh (EPA 239 mi 2019-2020 [P*], about 253 mi 2023+ [U]); Jaguar I-PACE (Waymo) 90 kWh [U], EPA 234 mi [P*]; real NYC range about 70-85% of EPA after HVAC, winter and buffers [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] a full-time driver covers about 120-200 mi a shift, so a 220-mi real range forces a mid-shift fast charge on most days; high mainly at fleet level; capacities [U], EPA ranges [P*].
variables.data_source: fueleconomy.gov and manufacturer specs [U]; EPA vehicles file GitHub copy (2019-2020) [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Battery kWh and usable window (e.g. 5-95%); drain from R08-007, R08-008, R08-009 and R08-010.

variables.name: Fuel level or state of charge
variables.description: How much fuel or charge is left right now, a running state that forces a stop when low.
variables.values_or_range: 0-100%; driver reserve buffers 10-20% [design]; fast charging usually to 70-80% [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] running empty strands the car (tow plus lost hours), while high charge targets waste time in the slow taper (R08-024).
variables.how_to_model: Decrement per mile and per idle minute; warnings at thresholds; forced stop and tow at zero.

variables.name: Charging power curve and taper
variables.description: How fast a car charges at each state of charge on each charger type: fast when low, slowing sharply above about 80%.
variables.values_or_range: Level 2 6-11 kW (about 20-35 mi of range per hour); DC fast chargers 50-350 kW with car-limited peaks of about 75-250 kW; 10-80% in about 18-45 min depending on the car; 80-100% can take as long as 10-80% [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] manufacturer and test data (e.g. Ioniq 5 10-80% about 18 min, Niro EV about 45 min); [design] each 30 min of charging costs about $17 of gross at about $34 per online hour.
variables.data_source: Manufacturer curves and public charging-curve tests [U]
variables.how_to_model: Piecewise power-vs-SOC curve per model, capped by charger kW and temperature (R08-010); integrate over time.

variables.name: Charger queue and occupancy
variables.description: Waiting time before a charger is free, which depends on site size, time of day and how many other EVs want it.
variables.values_or_range: 0-60+ min; peaks around shift changes and late evening [design]; sites of 4-40 stalls [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] NYC ride-hail drivers report queues at popular fast-charging hubs; no public occupancy history found.
variables.data_source: none found for occupancy history (AFDC gives stall counts, not use) https://afdc.energy.gov/stations
variables.how_to_model: M/M/c queue per site with hourly arrivals from the background EV share (R06) plus the agent's own fleet; optional live counts if the scenario gives a charging app.

variables.name: Charger reliability
variables.description: Chance that a public charger is broken, slower than rated, or fails to start.
variables.values_or_range: About 10-20% of public charging visits end without a charge in US surveys; derated output common [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] J.D. Power EVX public charging studies 2023-2024 (roughly one visit in five without a charge).
variables.data_source: none public for NYC (survey summaries only) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Per-session failure draw; a failure costs the detour and sends the car to another site.

variables.name: Charging session overhead
variables.description: Unpaid minutes around a charge: finding the stall, parking, plugging in, paying and walking.
variables.values_or_range: 3-10 min per session [design]; parking fees at some garage sites [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]
variables.how_to_model: Fixed dwell added to each session (robotaxi depots may automate it).

variables.name: Connector standard and network access
variables.description: Which chargers the car can use: Tesla (NACS) vs CCS, adapters, and fleet-only or member-only hubs.
variables.values_or_range: Teslas: all Superchargers plus CCS with an adapter; other makes: CCS sites plus some Superchargers with adapters [U]; fleet-only hubs [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] 2023-2025 shift of US makers to NACS.
variables.how_to_model: Compatibility mask between each car and each charger site.

variables.name: Home or overnight charging access
variables.description: Whether the driver can charge cheaply overnight at home, which sets the starting charge and the energy price.
variables.values_or_range: Yes: starts the shift at 80-100%, about $0.10/mi; No: all public charging at about $0.13-0.18/mi plus downtime. Most NYC drivers live in apartments without a private spot [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] cost stack: without home charging EV energy cost rises about 50% and 2-4 h a week go to charging stops.
variables.data_source: none found (no survey of NYC driver home charging)
variables.how_to_model: Persona flag; if yes, charge resets overnight at the home tariff (R08-016).

variables.name: Trip energy feasibility
variables.description: Whether the car has enough range to finish an offered trip and reach a charger afterwards, which can force a decline.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV Jan 2023: 0.61% of trips over 30 mi, 0.11% over 50 mi, 0.009% over 100 mi; 4.5% end outside NYC or at Newark, where return pickups are almost nil [P].
variables.impact_evidence: [P] long trips are rare, so this binds mainly when the charge is already low; shares re-matched to the script output.
variables.how_to_model: Before acceptance compare trip plus return-to-charger energy with charge minus buffer; destination may be hidden (R06-025).

variables.name: Charging efficiency losses
variables.description: Energy lost between the grid and the battery, which the driver still pays for.
variables.values_or_range: About 10-15% on Level 2 and 5-10% on DC fast; more in cold weather [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background.
variables.how_to_model: kWh billed = kWh into battery / efficiency.

variables.name: Battery degradation
variables.description: Gradual loss of battery capacity with age, mileage and fast charging.
variables.values_or_range: About 1.5-2.5% a year on average, more with heavy fast charging; high-mileage ride-hail EVs keep about 85-90% after 150-200k mi [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Geotab battery-health analyses and Recurrent data; low within a run, medium for multi-year fleet economics.
variables.how_to_model: Capacity factor from age and cumulative fast-charge share; fixed per scenario unless runs span months.

variables.name: Weekly rental or lease of a TLC-plated car
variables.description: Weekly rent paid by drivers who do not own their car, often the biggest single cost for NYC app drivers.
variables.values_or_range: About $350-650 a week by model (hybrid sedan lower, Tesla or XL higher), sometimes including insurance and maintenance [U]; lease-to-own deals similar [U]. FHV rents are unregulated; for scale, the TLC caps a weekly taxi lease of medallion plus vehicle (maintenance included) at $630 day / $737 night, +$21 for hybrids (35 RCNY 58-21(c)) [P*].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] $450 a week over 50 online hours = $9/h, about a quarter of gross per online hour (about $34 = Uber Jan 2023 driver pay of $57.1 per engaged hour [P] x about 59% time with a passenger [S, R10]); price levels [U].
variables.applies_to: human app driver, fleet (if it rents)
variables.data_source: none public (rental company price lists only) [U]; taxi lease caps 35 RCNY 58-21 [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Fixed weekly cost allocated per hour according to the accounting basis (R08-067); flags for bundled insurance and maintenance.

variables.name: Purchase price, financing and incentives
variables.description: What it costs to buy the car (price, sales tax, loan interest, rebates), which sets depreciation and financing cost.
variables.values_or_range: Camry Hybrid about $30-35k; Model Y about $45-50k; WAV minivan about $55-80k; Black SUV about $80-100k [U]; NYC sales tax 8.875% [U]; loan APR about 7-20% [U]; federal $7,500 EV credit ended for purchases after 30 Sep 2025 [U]; NY Drive Clean rebate up to about $2,000 [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] $35k at 10% APR over 5 years is about $172 a week in payments (about $3.4/h at 50 h a week); prices [U].
variables.applies_to: human app driver (owner), taxi owner, fleet
variables.data_source: Manufacturer prices [U]; NYSERDA Drive Clean Rebate https://www.nyserda.ny.gov/All-Programs/Drive-Clean-Rebate [U]
variables.how_to_model: Capex plus loan schedule converted to cost per week; depreciation via R08-035.

variables.name: Depreciation per mile and per year
variables.description: Loss of resale value from age and mileage, a real but deferred cost of each mile driven.
variables.values_or_range: About $0.10-0.25/mi for a $30-50k car driven 35-45k mi a year to a 6-7 year retirement [design]; EV used prices were volatile in 2023-2025 [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] a $35k car falling to about $5k over 250k mi is about $0.12/mi; [U] used-car price indices.
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi, fleet (robotaxi capex in R08-061)
variables.how_to_model: Per-mile charge in the cost ledger plus a per-day age component.

variables.name: Commercial (TLC) insurance premium
variables.description: Annual cost of the commercial liability policy that every TLC-licensed vehicle must carry at all times.
variables.values_or_range: About $5,000-12,000+ a year for an FHV, higher for new drivers or after claims [U]; TLC minimums [P*]: $100,000 per person no-fault basic economic loss, $100,000/$300,000 bodily injury, $10,000 property damage for FHVs under 8 seats (35 RCNY 59A-12(c)(1)) and taxis (58-13(d)(1)); cover must run 24/7 (59A-12(c)(5)); taxis run more than one shift a day need double-shift cover (58-13(d)(2)); 8-15 seat FHVs $1.5M combined; the NYC FHV market is dominated by one insurer (American Transit) [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] $8,000 a year = about $154 a week = about $3/h at 50 h a week, about 9% of gross per online hour; premium levels [U]; coverage minimums verified [P*].
variables.data_source: TLC insurance requirements https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/vehicles/insurance.page [U]; 35 RCNY 58-13, 59A-12 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]; NY Department of Financial Services [U]
variables.how_to_model: Fixed weekly cost, scaled by driver experience and claim history (R08-037).

variables.name: Insurance deductible and claim surcharge
variables.description: Out-of-pocket cost per claim and the premium rise after an at-fault crash.
variables.values_or_range: Deductible $500-2,500 [design, as in R09-008]; at-fault surcharge about +10-40% for about 3 years [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background.
variables.data_source: NY Department of Financial Services consumer guides [U]
variables.how_to_model: On a crash (R08-056) charge the deductible and raise the future premium.

variables.name: TLC licence, registration and inspection fees
variables.description: Government fees to keep the driver and car licensed (TLC driver licence, vehicle licence, DMV registration, inspections, drug test).
variables.values_or_range: [corrected by fact-check from rule text, P*] TLC driver licence $84 a year on a 3-year term, i.e. $252 (35 RCNY 80-07, 80-06); FHV vehicle licence $275 a year on a 2-year term, i.e. $550 (59A-07(a), 59A-06); Commercial Motor Vehicle Tax $800 per 2-year FHV licence period if not paid to DMV (59A-07(g)); TLC inspection fee $75 for FHVs (59A-04(e)(7)) and $90 for taxis (58-07(d)); taxicab licence $550 a year (58-07(a)); DMV registration about $100-300 [U]; together about $15-20 a week for an FHV owner-driver [design] (was $5-15).
variables.impact_evidence: [design] about $0.3-0.4 per online hour; fee values now [P*].
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi, fleet (robotaxi licensing in NYC undefined)
variables.data_source: TLC licensing pages https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/drivers/get-a-tlc-drivers-license.page [U]; 35 RCNY 80-07, 59A-07, 59A-04, 58-07 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Fixed annual costs prorated per week.

variables.name: Inspection frequency and downtime
variables.description: How often the car must be inspected, and the hours lost each time.
variables.values_or_range: [corrected by fact-check, P*] Taxis every four months at the TLC facility (35 RCNY 58-29(b)); FHVs also three times a year, at least once every four months (59A-26(a)(1)) (was 'about once a year'); only new-licence and renewal FHV inspections must be at the TLC Safety and Emissions facility (Woodside, Queens [U]), the others at any DMV-registered station (59A-04(e)-(f)); late taxi inspection means summary suspension; about 1-4 h each with travel and waiting [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] frequency from rule text; three visits of 1-4 h a year are under 0.5% of online time.
variables.data_source: TLC inspection pages https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc [U]; 35 RCNY 58-29, 59A-26, 59A-04 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Scheduled off-duty block on a set date in multi-week runs (three a year).

variables.name: Vehicle age limits and retirement
variables.description: Maximum vehicle age allowed under TLC rules, which caps service life and the resale value at retirement.
variables.values_or_range: [corrected by fact-check, P*] Taxis retire at the first scheduled inspection after 84 months (7 years) from hack-up, less the vehicle's age if hacked up used (35 RCNY 67-18(a)-(b)); one-time hardship extension up to 6 months (67-18(d)); an accessible taxi may stay in service past the date while it passes inspection (67-18(c)); since 18 Oct 2024 only Accessible Taxicab Models may be hacked up, new (under 500 miles, two latest model years) or converted (67-06), and Alternative Fuel Medallions need a hybrid or CNG model (67-05(b)). FHVs and green cars have no TLC scheduled retirement (59A-28(d) repealed; 82-61 reserved); platform model-year limits apply [U]. (Was 'roughly 5-8 model years for taxis and FHVs'.)
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] rule text; medium for multi-year fleet planning.
variables.applies_to: taxi (TLC rule), human app driver (platform limits only), fleet
variables.how_to_model: Retirement date from hack-up date (taxis) or platform model-year cut-off (FHVs) sets the depreciation horizon (R08-035) and forces replacement in fleet runs.

variables.name: Licence rules for adding vehicles (EV and WAV)
variables.description: Rules on which new vehicles may be licensed and what share of trips must be zero-emission or accessible, which constrain fleet growth and vehicle choice.
variables.values_or_range: FHV licence pause since 2018 with EV exemption windows (licensed FHVs 95,396 in Feb 2023 to 107,636 in Feb 2024) (R06-053 [S]); issuance reviewed every six months from Feb 2023, WAV licences always issued, EV-only licences (individual, or up to 25 per applicant) released at TLC discretion (35 RCNY 59A-06(a)) [P*] [uncertain: whether any EV-only licences were released in 2026; 'only WAV licences in 2026' rests on a snippet]; Green Rides [P*]: each high-volume service must dispatch at least 5% (2024), 15% (2025), 25% (2026), 40% (2027), 60% (2028), 80% (2029) and 100% (2030) of trips to zero-emission or accessible vehicles, fine $50 per 1,000 trips short (59D-13(c)).
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Green Rides schedule and licensing rules from rule text; licence counts [S] via R06-053. High for fleet composition.
variables.data_source: TLC licence pause report https://www.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/license-pause-report-2026-02.pdf [S]; 35 RCNY 59A-06, 59D-13 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Fleet expansion only allows licence-eligible types; scenario year sets the required ZEV-or-WAV trip share (25% in 2026).

variables.name: Taxi medallion and shift-lease costs
variables.description: What a yellow-cab driver pays to use a medallion and cab for a shift or week, or an owner-driver pays on medallion debt.
variables.values_or_range: [corrected by fact-check, 35 RCNY 58-21 as amended May 2025, P*] Shift caps for cab plus medallion: $105 any day shift; $115 Sun-Tue, $120 Wed, $129 Thu-Sat night shifts; weekly caps $630 (day) and $737 (night) (was $667-800); hybrids +$3 a shift or +$21 a week ($108-132; $648/$755); leases include maintenance, weekly leases include collision cover; medallion-only weekly cap $952 ($994 hybrid); medallion plus lease-to-own vehicle $952-994 + $275 a week, vehicle payments capped at $42,900; driver pays fuel unless the owner supplies it for a surcharge of $13-31 a shift indexed to the EIA NYC gasoline price; card processing $7 a shift or $49 a week; late return up to $25/h. Medallion Relief Program guaranty: principal up to $170,000 at a fixed 7.3% or less over 10-25 years, payment up to $1,235 a month (58-51(e)) [P*]; medallion values about $100-200k [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] a $115 shift lease over 12 h is about $9.6/h before fuel, a $737 night week over 60 h about $12/h; caps [P*].
variables.data_source: TLC taxicab leasing resolution https://www.nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/taxicab_leasing_resolution.pdf [S]; 35 RCNY 58-21, 58-51 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]; TLC medallion transfer data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Fixed cost per shift or week for the lessee persona (optional gas-included lease); the owner-driver persona pays a weekly loan instead (MRP-capped).

variables.name: Taxi equipment and card-processing fees
variables.description: Costs for the taxi technology system (meter, screen, card reader), roof light and partition, and fees fleets charge drivers on card payments.
variables.values_or_range: [corrected by fact-check, P*] Card processing is a flat $7 per daily shift or $49 per week (35 RCNY 58-21(c)(5)(xi)), not about 5% of card fares, and no other card pass-along is allowed (58-26(g)); medallion-only and lease-to-own caps already include card fees (58-21(c)(3)(iv), (c)(4)(v)); the $1.00 Taxicab Improvement Surcharge is deducted from card receipts but is a rider surcharge paid to the WAV fund (58-16(f), 58-21(f)); technology-system charges only as set by TLC rule (58-21(c)(5)(viii)), size [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] $49 a week is about 1-1.5% of a taxi driver's gross; card share can be computed from payment_type in TLC records [P] (fare-side rules in R07).
variables.data_source: TLC yellow trip records payment_type https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page; 35 RCNY 58-21, 58-26 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Flat card-processing charge per shift or week (not a percentage) plus any TLC-set technology fee.

variables.name: Vehicle-borne advertising income
variables.description: Small extra income from roof-top or in-car screen advertising that offsets vehicle costs.
variables.values_or_range: About $0-300 a month where programmes exist [U]. [corrected by fact-check, P*] Only taxis may carry rooftop ads in NYC, on a TLC-authorised fixture with a $50 a year permit (35 RCNY 67-16, 58-07(g)), and the income goes to the medallion owner, not usually the lessee [U]; FHVs, including Uber and Lyft cars, may not carry rooftop ads, and interior ads need a TLC-licensed interior advertising provider (59A-29(e)); robotaxis outside TLC licensing unregulated here [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background; [P*] advertising rules.
variables.applies_to: taxi (medallion owner), robotaxi; human app driver interior ads only
variables.data_source: none found for income; 35 RCNY 67-16, 59A-29 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Fixed monthly credit, or credit per online hour in ad zones; taxi-owner and robotaxi personas only (FHV rooftop ads banned).

variables.name: Routine maintenance per mile
variables.description: Scheduled servicing (oil and filters, fluids, small repairs), charged per mile.
variables.values_or_range: Gas and hybrid about $0.03-0.06/mi; EV about $0.02-0.04/mi (no oil); oil change every 5-10k mi at about $50-100 [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] maintenance plus tyres at about $0.06/mi is about $0.84/h (about 2.5% of gross); [U] AAA maintenance estimates.
variables.how_to_model: Per-mile accrual, with service events every N miles that take the car off the road for 1-2 h (taxi lessees: owner pays, 35 RCNY 58-21(b)).

variables.name: Tyre wear and replacement
variables.description: Cost of tyres worn by city driving, potholes and heavy EVs.
variables.values_or_range: Set of four about $600-1,200; life about 30-60k mi; EVs wear about 10-30% faster [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background.
variables.data_source: none found (AAA bundles tyres with maintenance) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Per-mile accrual, faster for EVs and aggressive personas (R08-011).

variables.name: Brake wear
variables.description: Cost of brake pads and rotors, high in stop-and-go traffic for gas cars and much lower with regenerative braking.
variables.values_or_range: Gas-car pads about 20-40k mi in NYC traffic; hybrids and EVs often 2-3x longer; pads and rotors about $300-700 per axle [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background.
variables.how_to_model: Per-mile accrual scaled by stops per mile (from R10 speeds) and powertrain.

variables.name: Car wash and interior cleaning (human-driven)
variables.description: Routine washing and cleaning to keep the car presentable for ratings and TLC rules.
variables.values_or_range: $15-40 per wash, or about $30-60 a month for unlimited plans; every 1-7 days, more often in winter salt season [U]; 20-40 min per visit [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background; cleanliness feeds ratings (R09-039) and mess events (R09-046, robotaxi cleaning in R09-047).
variables.how_to_model: Cleanliness state decays per trip and with weather; a wash action costs money and time.

variables.name: Simplified all-in per-mile cost (calibration)
variables.description: One cost per mile that bundles energy, maintenance, tyres and depreciation, for simple modes and as a sanity check.
variables.values_or_range: IRS business standard mileage rate 70 cents/mi for 2025 [U] [uncertain: the 2026 rate is recalled as 72.5 cents/mi; irs.gov blocked, not re-read]; AAA average new-car total about $0.75-0.85/mi at 15k mi a year [U]; our NYC full-time stack about $0.61/mi (owner, hybrid) to $0.81/mi (renter), fixed costs included [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] cost stack for 700 mi per 50-hour week (see dossier; arithmetic re-checked); IRS and AAA values [U].
variables.data_source: IRS standard mileage rates https://www.irs.gov/tax-professionals/standard-mileage-rates [U]; AAA Your Driving Costs [U]
variables.how_to_model: 'Simple cost mode' uses one per-mile and one per-hour rate; detailed mode uses the itemised variables.

variables.sub_box: Tolls, parking and fines paid by the driver
variables.name: Driver-paid tolls (loaded vs empty legs)
variables.description: Tolls are passed to the rider on paid trips, including the return toll on trips that leave the city; the driver pays only tolls on empty repositioning legs not tied to a trip (e.g. a tolled crossing to an airport queue or home). [corrected by fact-check: was 'paid by the driver on empty legs such as returning from New Jersey, Newark or Staten Island'.]
variables.values_or_range: Rule [P*]: on trips beyond NYC the rider pays 'all necessary tolls to and from the destination' (35 RCNY 58-26(f)(2) taxis, 59A-23(b)(2) FHVs); apps must pass to the driver any toll paid on a dispatched trip (59D-17(c)); taxi riders pay double going into and nothing coming out of the one-way-tolled Verrazzano, Cross Bay and Marine Parkway crossings (58-26(f)(1)). Data [P]: yellow 2023: 8.2% of trips had tolls (mean $7.34, about 3.0% of fares); HVFHV Jan 2023: Uber 10.8% (mean $10.11), Lyft 16.7% (mean $5.31), about 4.3-5.0% of base fares; 100% of app drop-offs at Newark carry a toll (median $21) and 56-62% of other out-of-city drop-offs (median $20), although westbound Hudson crossings are free; yellow 2023: 98% of Newark drop-offs (median $17.75). MTA E-ZPass car toll at major crossings $6.55 until 5 Aug 2023 and $6.94 from 6 Aug 2023 [P], about 6% higher from Jan 2026 (R01-020 [S]); Hudson crossings $14.79-16.79 inbound only in 2026 (R01-021 [S]), $12.75/$14.75 in 2023 records [P]. 3.9% of HVFHV trips end outside NYC and 0.6% at Newark, with almost no pickups there [P].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*][P] corrected by fact-check (was medium): the return toll is rider-paid by rule and in the data, so the driver keeps only the return time and energy (deadhead, R01-059 and R10) plus tolls on voluntary empty repositioning, which can mostly be routed around; likely well under 1% of gross [design].
variables.data_source: TLC trip records (tolls, tolls_amount) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page [P] (fc_tolls.py); 35 RCNY 58-26, 59A-23, 59D-17 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]; MTA tolls https://www.mta.info/fares-tolls/tolls ; PANYNJ https://www.panynj.gov/bridges-tunnels
variables.how_to_model: Toll on crossing edges by direction (R01); charged to the rider when loaded, plus the return toll on out-of-city trips; charged to the driver only for empty repositioning crossings not tied to a trip.

variables.sub_box: Tolls, parking and fines paid by the driver
variables.name: Toll payment method
variables.description: Whether the car pays by E-ZPass or by plate and mail, and the admin fees rental fleets add.
variables.values_or_range: [corrected by fact-check, P*] Every taxi and FHV owner must hold an MTA E-ZPass account and tag, and drivers may not operate for hire without one and must use it at all MTA crossings (35 RCNY 58-27, 59A-24, 59D-18, 80-15(d)); toll-by-mail (about 1.4-1.5x E-ZPass, PANYNJ about $23 vs $16.79, R01-021 [S]) applies to TLC cars only on tag failure, otherwise to non-TLC cars such as a robotaxi; taxi owners holding the tag may require a replenishment deposit of up to $10 a shift, capped at $100 (58-27(d)(2)); rental-fleet admin fee per toll $0-25 [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] E-ZPass mandate; [S] via R01-021; [U] rental fees.
variables.data_source: MTA and PANYNJ toll schedules (as R08-050); 35 RCNY 58-27, 59A-24, 80-15 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Toll multiplier and fixed fee by payment type; default E-ZPass for TLC personas.

variables.sub_box: Tolls, parking and fines paid by the driver
variables.name: Parking costs (overnight and during the shift)
variables.description: What it costs to keep the car overnight and to park during breaks or waits.
variables.values_or_range: Overnight: free street parking with alternate-side moves, or a garage at about $200-600 a month in the outer boroughs and $500-1,000+ in Manhattan [U]; short-term Manhattan garage about $20-50 for 1-2 h [U]; relief stands free for up to 1 h (R01-031; 34 RCNY 4-08, re-read by the R10 fact-check [P*]); airport FHV lots free [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background; relief-stand limit [P*].
variables.data_source: none public for prices; relief stands on NYC Open Data https://catalog.data.gov/dataset/taxi-and-for-hire-vehicle-fhv-relief-stands (R01-031)
variables.how_to_model: Per-night or per-hour parking price by zone; break actions choose paid or free spots.

variables.sub_box: Tolls, parking and fines paid by the driver
variables.name: Ticket and fine ledger
variables.description: Money lost to parking, standing and camera tickets and TLC summonses, whichever domain models the triggering event.
variables.values_or_range: [verified with detail, P*] 19 RCNY 39-05 base fines: no stopping or no standing $100; no parking $30 and meters $20, both $50 in Manhattan south of 96th St; street cleaning $50; idling $100; plus a state mandatory surcharge [U], so about $35-115 as posted; bus-lane and bus-route cameras $50, $100, $150, $200, then $250 within 12 months (39-18, 39-24); speed and red-light cameras $50 (39-21, 39-17 via the R10 fact-check); DEP anti-idling $350-2,000 (R10 fact-check); TLC fines in 35 RCNY about $25-1,000 plus suspensions; taxi owners may deduct parking and red-light camera tickets from the driver's deposit (58-21(e)(2)); rental fleets add admin fees [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] fine schedules; events come from R09-014, R10-030 to R10-032 and R10-034.
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (robotaxi: owner liability)
variables.data_source: NYC Open Data 'Open Parking and Camera Violations' https://data.cityofnewyork.us/City-Government/Open-Parking-and-Camera-Violations/nc67-uf89 [U]; 19 RCNY 39-05, 39-18, 39-24 via jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Each violation event posts a fine to the ledger; camera tickets go to the registered owner and are passed on with a fee.

variables.name: Mechanical breakdown hazard
variables.description: Chance per mile that the car breaks down and must be towed or repaired, rising with age and mileage.
variables.values_or_range: About 1 per 20-60k mi for older high-mileage cars [design]; NYC tow about $100-300 [U]; repair $200-3,000; downtime 0.5-5 days.
variables.impact_evidence: [design] no public per-mile breakdown rate for NYC TLC vehicles found.
variables.how_to_model: Poisson hazard per mile x age factor; on an event end the shift, charge tow and repair, set downtime (R08-058).

variables.name: Flat tyres and minor roadside events
variables.description: Small mishaps such as flats, dead 12 V batteries or warning lights that cost an hour or two.
variables.values_or_range: About 1 per 15-40k mi, more in pothole season (Feb-Apr) [design]; 0.5-2 h downtime; $20-200 [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]
variables.how_to_model: Poisson event per mile with a seasonal factor; downtime and a small cost.

variables.name: Collision cost and downtime (human-driven)
variables.description: What a crash costs the driver beyond the event: deductible, repairs, a replacement car, days off the road and higher premiums.
variables.values_or_range: Downtime 3-30 days; deductible $500-2,500; replacement rental about $50-100 a day if one is available [U]; base crash rate per mile by zone and hour from NYC collision data [design]; taxi weekly leases include collision cover, and an optional damage plan for lease-to-own drivers is capped at $50 a week with a $250 deductible (35 RCNY 58-21(c)(1)(vi), (c)(4)(v)G) [P*].
variables.impact_evidence: [S] via R09-008: injury-crash rate +23.8% above 12 h a day; corrected by fact-check (was medium): the R09 fact-check puts expected crash cost at about $0.2-1 per hour, a few per cent of gross or less; high only inside a run where a crash happens.
variables.data_source: NYC Open Data Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes (vehicle type includes taxi) https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Public-Safety/Motor-Vehicle-Collisions-Crashes/h9gi-nx95 [U]
variables.how_to_model: The crash hazard (R09-008) triggers this package of cost and downtime.

variables.name: Robotaxi (ADS) crash and incident rate
variables.description: How often a driverless car is in a crash or incident that stops it, and what it costs.
variables.values_or_range: Large reductions vs human benchmarks reported by Waymo (e.g. Swiss Re 2024: about 88% fewer property-damage and 92% fewer bodily-injury claims over 25.3M miles) [U]; even minor contacts stop the car for inspection [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Swiss Re and Waymo 2024 study; corrected by fact-check (was medium): claim rates about 90% below human drivers make the expected crash cost per robotaxi hour smaller than the human case (R08-056, low); severe-incident costs sit in R08-060 and R08-066. ADS crashes are listed publicly under NHTSA's Standing General Order.
variables.data_source: NHTSA Standing General Order crash data https://www.nhtsa.gov/laws-regulations/standing-general-order-crash-reporting ; Waymo Safety Impact https://waymo.com/safety/impact/ ; California DMV AV collision reports [U]
variables.how_to_model: Hazard per mile below the human base; each event takes the car out for inspection and repair; rare severe events trigger R08-060.

variables.name: Repair downtime and spare vehicles
variables.description: Days a car is off the road after a breakdown or crash, and whether a spare or rental replaces it.
variables.values_or_range: Human driver earns nothing unless a TLC-plated replacement is found [U]; taxi weekly leases must be pro-rated when the car is unavailable through no fault of the lessee (35 RCNY 58-21(c)(1)(v)) [P*]; fleet spare ratio 0-15% [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] a 10-day repair at about $34 per online hour x 50 h a week is about $2,400 of lost gross; medium mainly via the fleet spare-ratio decision.
variables.how_to_model: Car state 'in repair' with a countdown; the fleet agent can keep spare cars (R08-069).

variables.name: Theft and vandalism
variables.description: Losses from theft of parts or attacks on the car.
variables.values_or_range: Catalytic-converter theft targeted hybrids during 2020-2023 [U]; robotaxi vandalism, e.g. Waymo cars set on fire in San Francisco (Feb 2024) and Los Angeles (June 2025) [U]; $1-3k (converter) up to total loss.
variables.impact_evidence: [U] background.
variables.data_source: NYPD complaint data on NYC Open Data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Rare event hazard by zone and event (R03 protests); repair cost and downtime.

variables.name: Recalls and fleet-wide grounding
variables.description: Software or hardware recalls, or regulator suspensions, that take many cars out of service at once.
variables.values_or_range: Waymo fleet-wide software recall in May 2026 after flooded-road and construction-zone incidents (R06-058 [S]) [uncertain: details not re-read by this or the R06 fact-check; check the NHTSA recall record]; Cruise driverless permit suspended in Oct 2023 [U]; hours to months.
variables.impact_evidence: [S] via R06-058; [U] Cruise 2023. Rare, but high impact when it happens.
variables.applies_to: robotaxi, fleet (model recalls also hit human-driven cars)
variables.how_to_model: Scenario event: a share of the fleet is offline for a duration; optional software-update downtime.

variables.name: Robotaxi vehicle capex and amortisation
variables.description: Cost of a driverless car (base vehicle, sensors, compute) spread over its service life.
variables.values_or_range: Current Waymo-type car about $100-200k all-in [U]; next-generation platforms (Zeekr, Ioniq 5) aimed lower [U]; Tesla Cybercab target under $30k [U]; amortised over about 300k mi: $0.10-0.67/mi [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] $150k over 300k mi = $0.50/mi, vs about $0.12-0.15/mi depreciation for a human driver's hybrid; capex levels [U].
variables.data_source: none public (company statements and analyst estimates) [U]
variables.how_to_model: Per-mile and per-day amortisation in the fleet ledger.

variables.name: Sensor cleaning, calibration and replacement
variables.description: Keeping cameras and lidar clean and calibrated, including weather-driven cleaning and repairs after minor damage.
variables.values_or_range: Onboard washer and air jets; depot cleaning each visit; recalibration after windshield or sensor replacement; 0-60 min per depot visit [design]; worse in snow, salt and rain [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] AV sensor-cleaning design background; no public per-car cost.
variables.how_to_model: Sensor-dirt state grows with precipitation and road salt (R04); above a threshold the car returns to the depot.

variables.name: Fleet operations overhead per vehicle
variables.description: Non-driving labour per car: depot staff who charge, clean and inspect, field teams who recover stuck cars, and fleet managers.
variables.values_or_range: Depots of about 70 staff serving hundreds of cars (R09-045 [S]); 24/7 three-shift depots (R09-044 [S]); about $10-25 per vehicle-day [design]; remote assistance costed in R09-049.
variables.impact_evidence: [S] via R09-044 and R09-045; per-car cost [design].
variables.how_to_model: Fixed cost per car-day plus a per-incident field-recovery cost and delay.

variables.name: Depot real estate cost
variables.description: Rent for depot and parking space for each robotaxi in an expensive city.
variables.values_or_range: NYC industrial rent about $20-40 per sq ft a year [U]; about 300-400 sq ft per car with aisles and chargers [design], so about $6k-16k per car a year.
variables.impact_evidence: [design] calculation; rent levels [U].
variables.how_to_model: Fixed cost per car slot; depot location trades rent against deadhead (R10-057).

variables.name: HD mapping and map upkeep
variables.description: Cost and time to map a new service area and keep it current, which limits where robotaxis may operate.
variables.values_or_range: One-time mapping cost per km2 plus ongoing updates; lead time weeks to months; no published figures [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] no public cost data.
variables.how_to_model: Geofence-expansion action with cost and delay (geofence in R01-008).

variables.name: Robotaxi insurance and liability
variables.description: Liability cover for a driverless fleet, often self-insured, priced per mile or per car.
variables.values_or_range: About $0.03-0.15/mi [design]; fewer claims than human drivers (R08-057) but a heavy tail of severe events and legal exposure [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Swiss Re and Waymo claims study; no public robotaxi premium found.
variables.how_to_model: Per-mile charge plus a rare catastrophic-event tail.

variables.sub_box: Cost accounting, information and vehicle choice
variables.name: Cost accounting basis for profit
variables.description: Which costs count in the profit score: only marginal costs (energy, wear, tolls, fines) or also fixed costs (rental, insurance, licences, capex) per hour.
variables.values_or_range: Marginal only; marginal plus time-based fixed costs; full economic cost including depreciation and financing [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] in our cost stack, fixed costs are about $4.6/h for an owner and $9.5/h for a renter vs marginal costs of about $2-4/h for a hybrid (energy and wear, plus depreciation for owners), so the basis moves profit per hour by about 14-28% of gross and changes incentives (fixed costs reward longer shifts); arithmetic re-checked.
variables.how_to_model: Ledger tags each cost as marginal or fixed; scoring sums by the chosen basis; report all three.

variables.sub_box: Cost accounting, information and vehicle choice
variables.name: Cost and vehicle-state information shown to the agent
variables.description: Which cost and vehicle data the agent can see: fuel or charge level, live fuel and charging prices, charger queues, maintenance warnings, cost per mile.
variables.values_or_range: Minimal (gauge only); standard (gauge, prices, cost per mile); full (plus charger occupancy and breakdown risk) [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] mirrors the team's with/without event-information ablation.
variables.how_to_model: Observation filter on the vehicle-state API.

variables.sub_box: Cost accounting, information and vehicle choice
variables.name: Vehicle choice and fleet mix
variables.description: At fleet level, which vehicles to buy or rent (EV vs hybrid, WAV, XL, premium) and how many spares, within licence rules and budget.
variables.values_or_range: Mix of vehicle specs; capex budget; licence-eligible types (R08-041); Green Rides ZEV-or-WAV trip share (25% in 2026, 100% by 2030, 35 RCNY 59D-13(c)) [P*]; taxi hack-ups accessible-only since Oct 2024 (67-06(a)) [P*]; spare ratio [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design] energy cost spread about $0.07-0.26/mi (corrected by fact-check from $0.08-0.18, using EPA's 0.44 kWh/mi for an I-PACE-class car and depot vs public DC fast prices) plus capex from about $30k to $200k per car.
variables.data_source: EPA specs [U] (2019-2020 via GitHub copy [P*]); TLC licence rules (R08-041) [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Procurement action at scenario start (or monthly) choosing specs; costs flow to the ledger (fleet decisions in R11).

variables.sub_box: Cost accounting, information and vehicle choice
variables.name: Emissions and carbon accounting (optional)
variables.description: Optional score term for CO2 from fuel and electricity, to test green goals or Green Rides compliance.
variables.values_or_range: Gasoline about 8.9 kg CO2 per gallon [P*: EPA tailpipe CO2 x combined mpg gives a median 8,880 g/gal across 2,960 gasoline models from 2015 on]; NYC grid about 0.25-0.35 kg CO2 per kWh [U] [uncertain: EPA eGRID's NYC/Westchester subregion (NYCW) is recalled at about 0.40 kg/kWh because in-city generation is mostly gas, while the NY state average is nearer 0.2-0.25; read eGRID before use]; carbon price $0-200 per tonne [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] EPA emission factors; gasoline factor [P*].
variables.data_source: EPA GHG Emission Factors Hub https://www.epa.gov/climateleadership/ghg-emission-factors-hub [U]; EPA eGRID https://www.epa.gov/egrid [U]
variables.how_to_model: Emissions per mile by powertrain; optional penalty in the score.

variables.sub_box: A. Shift structure and working time
variables.name: Shift start time and place
variables.description: When and where the driver goes online for the day.
variables.values_or_range: App driver: any time 00:00-23:59, usually from the home zone; taxi lessee: fixed by lease (day shift about 05:00, night shift about 17:00).
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Chen, Chevalier, Rossi & Oehlsen 2019 (JPE 127(6)): drivers' reservation wages vary hour by hour, and forced inflexible schedules would cut their hours by more than two-thirds [uncertain: not re-checkable; the paper's headline is that drivers earn more than twice the surplus they would under less flexible arrangements]; NYC 2011 GPS study (DNAinfo, TLC figures): active cabs fall about 20% at the 4-5 pm shift change.
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi (constrained by lease), fleet (per car)
variables.data_source: TLC 2009-2013 trip data with hashed hack licence (2013 FOIL release; archived TLC trips at ICPSR 37254, https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/web/ICPSR/studies/37254 [uncertain: whether ICPSR keeps the hashed IDs]; alternative [U]: Donovan & Work, NYC Taxi Trip Data 2010-2013, Illinois Data Bank, https://doi.org/10.13012/J8PN93H8, with anonymised medallion and hack-licence IDs); Chicago Taxi Trips with a stable Taxi ID (https://data.cityofchicago.org, wrvz-psew). Current TLC public files carry no driver ID (yellow, HVFHV [P*]; green [P]).
variables.how_to_model: Action go_online(time, zone); the taxi persona is restricted to its lease window; the start zone defaults to home.

variables.sub_box: A. Shift structure and working time
variables.name: Shift end and total hours (daily, weekly)
variables.description: How long the driver works each day and how many days each week.
variables.values_or_range: App: 1-12 h/day within caps; NYC full-time about 40-60 h/week; taxi lease shift 12 h ([P*] 35 RCNY 58-21(i)(1)(ii); owners may offer pro-rated shorter shifts, 58-21(c)(1)(vii)); 4-7 days/week.
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Parrott (presentation drawing on the 2018 TLC earnings study): 60-65% of NYC app drivers are full-time with driving as their only job; Hall & Krueger 2015 draft [corrected by fact-check: about half (51%) of US Uber drivers drove 1-15 h/week in late 2014, pooled across markets, with NYC drivers working longer; not 'most outside NYC' (U)].
variables.applies_to: human app driver, taxi, fleet (per car)
variables.data_source: TLC Data Hub driver fare and earnings (added Jan 2023 [uncertain: date not checked], via nyc.gov/tlc); TLC 2009-2013 FOIL trips; Chicago taxi IDs.
variables.how_to_model: Agent calls go_offline; harness tracks daily and weekly hours and reports profit per hour and per day.

variables.sub_box: A. Shift structure and working time
variables.name: Taxi lease shift window and handover
variables.description: Drivers who lease a yellow cab work a fixed 12-hour shift and must hand the cab back at a set time.
variables.values_or_range: Two 12 h shifts per cab; handover usually 16:00-17:00; 35 RCNY 58-21(i)(1)(ii) requires 12 consecutive hours ([P*]; the pilot waiver is [S]); late-return charge at most $25 per hour, capped at one shift's lease (35 RCNY 58-21(c)(5)(iv)) [corrected by fact-check: was 'per hour [U]'].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 58-21 (verbatim, nyc_code_archive); [S] 2011 city GPS study and TLC counts (6,688 to 5,452 cabs between 4 and 5 pm); TLC pilot press release 2015 on moving shift change outside 4-8 pm.
variables.data_source: 35 RCNY 58-21 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]; TLC taxicab leasing resolution (nyc.gov/assets/tlc/downloads/pdf/taxicab_leasing_resolution.pdf) [S]; 2009-2013 FOIL trips for shift timing.
variables.how_to_model: Taxi persona gets a hard shift end and a garage location; late return costs up to $25/h, capped at one shift's lease. The same handover also creates a supply dip in the competitor model (R06).

variables.sub_box: A. Shift structure and working time
variables.name: Driver work profile (persona type)
variables.description: The type of driver, which sets default availability, hours, costs and constraints.
variables.values_or_range: Full-time app driver (only job); part-time app driver (other job); taxi lessee day or night; owner-driver; robotaxi (no driver).
variables.impact_evidence: [S] Parrott (presentation drawing on the 2018 TLC study): 60-65% of NYC drivers full-time; Uber 2014 survey (Hall & Krueger): 52% part-time and 75% of part-timers have other jobs [uncertain: survey figures not re-checkable this session].
