variables.values_or_range: median ~1-2 min [U] [corrected by fact-check: Uber trips in Jan 2023 (13.6M) show pickup minus on-scene median 0.8 min (47 s), mean 1.0 min, P75 1.8 min; 17% of trips sit at 2.0-2.2 min and only 3.8% exceed 2.1 min, so the field looks censored at the 2-minute wait clock (P*)]; Uber/Lyft wait fees start 2 min after arrival (5 min for premium) [S] [uncertain for Lyft: not re-read]; Waymo waits up to 5 min (4 min at Phoenix airport) then charges a no-show fee; luggage or mobility aids add ~30-120 s (bus analogue: 15-19 s ordinary vs 28-137 s encumbered)
variables.impact_evidence: Platform wait-fee policies and Waymo help page [S]; HVFHV records carry on_scene and pickup timestamps [P*]; on_scene_datetime is filled for 100% of Uber (HV0003) but 0.14% of Lyft (HV0005) trips in Jan 2023, despite the dictionary's 'accessible vehicles only' label [P*]
variables.data_source: TLC HVFHV trip records (pickup_datetime minus on_scene_datetime where populated: Uber only)
variables.how_to_model: Lognormal dwell by zone type (airport, station, residential), hour and luggage flag, calibrated on HVFHV on-scene to pickup gaps.

variables.name: Drop-off dwell and payment time
variables.description: Time from arrival at the destination until the vehicle can leave, including payment (taxi), unloading and door closing.
variables.values_or_range: app trips 15-45 s [design]; taxi card or cash payment +30-90 s [design]; airport curb with luggage 1-3 min [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] no public NYC measurement found
variables.data_source: none found (TLC trip end is the drop-off time, not the departure time)
variables.how_to_model: Add a dwell draw after each drop-off before the vehicle becomes available.

variables.name: Curb availability and stopping search
variables.description: Extra time to find a legal or safe spot to stop at busy curbs (no-standing zones, bus lanes, bike lanes, double-parked trucks).
variables.values_or_range: 0-3 min in Midtown and FiDi peaks; ~0 in residential outer boroughs [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] Manhattan has few loading docks so curbs are saturated [S on freight]; 34 RCNY 4-11(c): taxis and FHVs may stop briefly to pick up or drop off where standing is banned, must be within 12 in of the curb, and may double-park only if no curb space is free within 100 ft; never in bike lanes, crosswalks or no-stopping zones [P*]
variables.data_source: NYC DOT parking regulation signs dataset [U]; OSM
variables.how_to_model: Zone-hour 'curb friction' delay added to each pickup and drop-off, higher on bus-route blocks.

variables.name: Double parking and delivery lane blockage
variables.description: Background lane capacity lost to double-parked delivery and service vehicles, peaking midday.
variables.values_or_range: corridor capacity -6 to -12% (Manhattan parcel-delivery simulation); a travel lane blocked ~25% of the day on Church Ave, Brooklyn; delivery stops ~21 min, two-thirds double-parked [S]; 34 RCNY 4-08 lets commercial vehicles double-park up to 20 min while loading when no curb space is free on the block [P*]
variables.impact_evidence: BTS/ROSAP Manhattan delivery study [S]; NYC DOT Church Ave analysis [S]
variables.data_source: none direct; captured in TLC-calibrated speeds
variables.how_to_model: Implicit in calibrated midday speeds; optional explicit blockage events on curb-lane edges.

variables.name: Rider pin accuracy and meeting friction
variables.description: Delay or failed pickups because the rider's GPS pin, the vehicle's position or the agreed side of the street is wrong.
variables.values_or_range: GNSS error can reach 50 m or more in urban canyons; shadow matching roughly doubled accuracy [uncertain: not re-read]; 0.5-3 min extra or a cancellation [design]
variables.impact_evidence: Uber Engineering 'Rethinking GPS' and GPS World coverage [S]
variables.data_source: none public for NYC error rates
variables.how_to_model: Draw pin error (sigma 10-20 m outer boroughs, 30-60 m Midtown/FiDi [design]); if past half a block or on the opposite side, add search time or a cancellation chance.

variables.name: Hotspot curb queues
variables.description: Queues of pickup vehicles at concentrated pickup points (stations, venues, airports) that grow with the number of cars converging, including the agent's own fleet.
variables.values_or_range: 2-10 min approach and queue at Penn Station, Port Authority and venues at peaks [design]; airport lots can be longer (R06)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] no public queue-time data found within the search budget
variables.how_to_model: M/M/c queue at designated pickup nodes with service rate from curb length; fleet vehicles join the same queue.

variables.name: Airport pickup access path
variables.description: Extra driving and waiting to reach designated airport pickup areas (FHV lots, taxi holds) rather than the terminal curb.
variables.values_or_range: +3-15 min [U]; Waymo at Phoenix airport limits terminal wait to 4 min
variables.impact_evidence: [U] JFK and LGA send FHV pickups to designated areas; Waymo PHX airport rules [S]
variables.how_to_model: Airport nodes with a mandatory staging-lot detour and service-type-specific access rules.

variables.name: Routing objective
variables.description: What the route planner minimises: fastest time, shortest distance, toll-free, highway-free or a risk-adjusted time.
variables.values_or_range: fastest / shortest / avoid tolls / avoid highways / P90 time
variables.impact_evidence: OSRM car profile supports routability, duration and distance weights [P]
variables.how_to_model: Expose k alternative routes with time, distance and toll and let the agent choose, or fix a policy per prompt variant.

variables.name: Time-versus-distance pay crossover speed
variables.description: The speed below which a trip earns by time rather than distance, which ties traffic speed directly to revenue.
variables.values_or_range: yellow and green taxi meter: 70 cents per 1/5 mile at 12 mph or more, or per 60 s below 12 mph (35 RCNY 58-26(a)) [P*] [corrected by fact-check: the threshold is 'at 12 mph or more', not 'above']; HVFHV driver pay has per-mile and per-minute parts (R07)
variables.impact_evidence: 35 RCNY 58-26 via nyc_code_archive [P*]; TLC taxi fare page [S]
variables.how_to_model: Meter integrates per-segment speed along the realised route, so the engine must emit a sub-trip speed trace, not only total time.

variables.name: Navigation ETA error shown to agent
variables.description: Difference between the ETA the agent is shown and the realised travel time.
variables.values_or_range: multiplicative error with MAE ~10-25% [design]; optimistic bias in peaks [design]
variables.impact_evidence: Uber builds ETAs as routing-engine segment sums plus an ML residual correction (DeepETA, judged by MAE), implying raw router ETAs are biased [S]
variables.data_source: derived from the R10-008 noise model
variables.how_to_model: Shown ETA = expected time x (1 + bias + noise); realised time drawn separately from the true distribution.

variables.name: Traffic information level
variables.description: How much traffic information the agent receives: none, typical map times, live speeds, or live speeds plus incidents and closures.
variables.values_or_range: L0 none / L1 typical times / L2 live speeds / L3 live + incidents + gridlock alerts
variables.impact_evidence: [design] mirrors the team's with/without public event information test
variables.how_to_model: Harness flag selecting which traffic layers enter the observation.

variables.name: Dynamic re-routing
variables.description: Whether routes are recomputed en route when conditions change, by a navigation autopilot or by the agent.
variables.values_or_range: none / autopilot every N min / agent-controlled
variables.impact_evidence: [design]
variables.how_to_model: Re-plan the remaining path at each traffic update tick.

variables.name: Vehicle localisation and missed turns
variables.description: Navigation errors such as missed turns in urban canyons where the driver's own GPS drifts.
variables.values_or_range: missed-turn probability 1-5% per Midtown trip for humans [design]; near zero for a robotaxi with lidar and HD-map localisation [U]
variables.impact_evidence: Uber: GNSS errors of 50 m or more in dense cities [S]
variables.how_to_model: Small probability of a 1-4 min loop detour on Midtown and FiDi trips.

variables.name: Driver route knowledge
variables.description: A human driver's local knowledge of shortcuts and traffic patterns compared with app routes.
variables.values_or_range: 0-5% time saved for experienced taxi drivers [design]
variables.how_to_model: Experience factor on chosen-route time; in multi-day runs it can be learnt memory (cross-link R09, R12).

variables.name: Map staleness
variables.description: Mismatch between the map the agent sees and the true network (recent turn bans, closures, new bus lanes).
variables.values_or_range: 0-2% of edges stale [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] robustness test
variables.how_to_model: Agent map built from an older OSM snapshot, simulator from a newer one.

variables.name: Pickup deadhead (en route to rider)
variables.description: Time and distance driven empty from accepting a request to reaching the rider.
variables.values_or_range: NYC HVFHV average wait 4.4-6.6 min by borough (2018-Jan 2026) [S; consistent with a Jan 2023 check: mean request-to-pickup 4.3 min Manhattan, 4.7 Brooklyn, 4.8 Bronx, 5.0 Queens, 5.5 Staten Island, 4.6 citywide; Uber request-to-on-scene (pure en-route time) mean 3.0-4.3 min, median 2.4-3.7 min by borough, P*]; ~10% of ride-hail VMT is driving to pickups (six US metros); SF pickup ETAs late 2025: Waymo 5.74 min, Uber 3.15, Lyft 5.14
variables.impact_evidence: TLC license pause report Feb 2026 [S]; TLC HVFHV Jan 2023 [P*]; Fehr & Peers 2019 [S]; Obi via Axios [S]
variables.data_source: TLC HVFHV trip records (request_datetime, on_scene_datetime, pickup_datetime; on_scene filled for Uber only)
variables.how_to_model: Same travel-time engine from vehicle position to pickup; logged per trip for utilisation metrics.

variables.name: Cruising and idle share
variables.description: Share of time or miles without a passenger while waiting for the next request.
variables.values_or_range: ~41% of HVFHV time without a passenger in Manhattan below 96th St (2019); TLC cap adopted Aug 2019 (35 RCNY 59D-21: 36% from Feb 2020, 31% from Aug 2020, weekdays 6 AM-11 PM and weekends 8 AM-11 PM in the Congestion Zone; en-route time to pickups counts as cruising; WAVs exempt) [P*], still printed in the rules but annulled by a state court in Dec 2019 and not enforced [U]; ~33% of ride-hail VMT waiting or cruising (six US metros)
variables.impact_evidence: 35 RCNY 59D-21 [P*]; TLC 2019 cruising rule documents [S]; Fehr & Peers 2019 [S]
variables.data_source: TLC reports; HVFHV records lack a vehicle ID so gaps between trips cannot be rebuilt [P*: no vehicle or driver ID in the HVFHV schema]
variables.how_to_model: Emerges from the simulation; report it as a metric and use the 41% figure as a sanity check for baseline policies.

variables.name: Hail-search cruising speed (taxi)
variables.description: Speed and pattern at which a taxi cruises empty looking for street hails, trading hail encounters against fuel and time.
variables.values_or_range: 5-15 mph [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] NYC street-hail supply and demand studies exist (arXiv 1909.12861) [S]; 34 RCNY 4-11(b) bars vehicles other than taxis from cruising for passengers [P*]
variables.data_source: TLC yellow and green trip records (pickup zones as hail density)
variables.how_to_model: Hail arrivals per edge-minute (R05) times time spent on each edge; slower cruising raises exposure per block.

variables.name: Repositioning travel cost
variables.description: Time and distance to move empty to a better zone, which the agent weighs against expected demand there.
variables.values_or_range: 5-40 min depending on distance and hour [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] repositioning is the core single-car and fleet decision and its cost is pure travel time
variables.how_to_model: Engine returns time and distance for any reposition order; optionally show the estimate before the agent commits.

variables.name: Waiting location: park, stand or circle
variables.description: Time to find a legal place to wait when stationary, and the choice between parking, using a stand, or circling.
variables.values_or_range: 113 taxi/FHV relief stands (70 in Manhattan) [S], park up to 1 h (34 RCNY 4-08) [P*]; taxi stands require the driver in the car [uncertain: 34 RCNY 4-11(a) says a taxi awaiting a fare may stand only at a taxi stand (or at a hydrant with the driver in the seat); no driver-presence rule for stands was found, P*]; street-parking search 0-10+ min in Manhattan [design]
variables.impact_evidence: NYC DOT relief-stand page and a council document citing DOT counts [S]; 34 RCNY 4-08, 4-11 [P*]
variables.data_source: NYC DOT Taxi and FHV Relief Stands https://www.nyc.gov/html/dot/html/motorist/taxirelief.shtml (Open Data list)
variables.how_to_model: Stand and parking capacity per zone; agent action 'wait at X'; if full, the car circles with fuel cost.

variables.name: Return-home deadhead at shift end
variables.description: Empty travel time from the last drop-off to the driver's home area, which the 'take me home' feature tries to reduce.
variables.values_or_range: 10-60 min [design], shorter late at night
variables.impact_evidence: [design] from the team's 'take me home' note
variables.how_to_model: Computed at shift end; destination-filtered trips toward home reduce it (cross-link R07, R09).

variables.name: Empty return from airports and outer areas
variables.description: Deadhead back toward demand after a drop-off at an airport or a low-demand area when no return trip is available.
variables.values_or_range: JFK to Midtown roughly 38-64 min by hour (occupied-trip benchmark) [corrected by fact-check: 2023 Midtown core to JFK weekday medians were 29-75 min by hour, LGA 21-44 min (P*)]
variables.impact_evidence: Schneider airport trip times [S]; TLC 2023 yellow trips [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Same engine; the agent chooses between the airport queue (R06) and deadheading back.

variables.name: Depot and charger deadhead
variables.description: Empty travel to depots, cleaning or chargers, which takes vehicles out of service.
variables.values_or_range: 5-30 min each way [design]; 1-3 trips a day for EVs [U]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] cross-link R08 charging
variables.how_to_model: Same engine to charger or depot nodes; charge time from R08.

variables.name: Empty-vehicle speed bias
variables.description: Empty and repositioning vehicles may move at different speeds than occupied trips, but trip data only observe occupied legs.
variables.values_or_range: empty speed 0.8-1.0 x occupied speed [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] TLC data record only paid trips, so deadhead speeds are unobserved
variables.how_to_model: Apply occupied-trip calibration to empty moves with an optional factor.

variables.name: Travel-time engine architecture
variables.description: How the simulator computes travel time from A to B: zone-to-zone lookup, road-graph routing with time-dependent speeds, or a hybrid.
variables.values_or_range: (a) 263-zone OD x hour table (lookup IDs 264-265 are Unknown and outside NYC) [P*]; (b) OSRM or Valhalla on OSM with speed profiles; (c) graph geometry for visuals plus OD-calibrated times
variables.impact_evidence: TLC trip files carry only taxi-zone IDs since July 2016, no coordinates [P*]
variables.data_source: TLC trip records; taxi zone shapefile; OpenStreetMap
variables.how_to_model: Recommend (c): Valhalla or OSRM path for geometry and the live map, edge times scaled so zone-pair x hour medians match TLC.

variables.name: Time resolution of speed profiles
variables.description: Bucket width for time-dependent speeds and how the chosen router supports it.
variables.values_or_range: Valhalla: 2016 five-minute speeds per edge per week (DCT-II compressed) plus free-flow (night) and constrained (7 AM-7 PM) speeds; OSRM: no native time dependence, reload a segment-speed CSV with osrm-customize (MLD) per bucket; options 5 / 15 / 60 min
variables.impact_evidence: Valhalla historical-traffic and speeds docs [P]; OSRM command-line docs [S], and docs/tools.md read on GitHub [P] (osrm-customize applies --segment-speed-file and --turn-penalty-file to an MLD graph; the release line is 26.x, package.json 26.10.0)
variables.how_to_model: Valhalla predicted traffic with depart_at times, or 168 hourly OSRM datasets switched by the simulation clock.

variables.name: Router default-speed bias
variables.description: Out-of-the-box router speeds assume free flow and badly underestimate dense-city travel times unless calibrated.
variables.values_or_range: OSRM car.lua: primary 65 km/h, secondary 55, tertiary 40, residential 25 on roads without a maxspeed tag; where OSM has maxspeed it uses 0.8 x maxspeed (25 mph gives ~32 km/h) and adds 2 s per signal; turn penalty up to 7.5 s, U-turn 20 s [P]; Valhalla uses the maxspeed tag directly as routing speed [P]; vs real Midtown ~7-9 km/h daytime, so a 2-5x underestimate [corrected by fact-check: about 3.5x on 25-mph-tagged streets and up to ~7x on untagged primaries, derived]
variables.impact_evidence: OSRM car.lua defaults [P] vs Midtown 4.8 mph [S] and TLC 2023 Midtown core 5.4-6.0 mph [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Never ship raw router ETAs; replace speeds with calibrated profiles and validate.

variables.name: Calibration target and acceptance error
variables.description: Which observed statistic the travel-time model must match and how closely.
variables.values_or_range: zone-pair x hour-of-week median and P90 of TLC durations; target MAPE 15-20% or better on a held-out month [design]; OD neighbour averaging beat route-based methods and map APIs on 173M 2013 NYC trips
variables.impact_evidence: Wang et al. 2016 SIGSPATIAL, arXiv 1512.08580 [S]
variables.data_source: TLC yellow, green and HVFHV trip records
variables.how_to_model: Hold out a month; report MAPE by distance band, hour and borough; fail the build above threshold.

variables.name: Trip-record cleaning rules
variables.description: Filters applied to TLC records before fitting speeds (bad timestamps, zero distance, impossible speeds).
variables.values_or_range: drop duration under 60 s or over 3 h, speed over 60 mph or under 1 mph, zero distance [design]; in 2023 yellow data these rules remove 1.15% (<60 s), 0.09% (>3 h), 2.02% (zero distance), 0.06% (>60 mph) and 0.18% (<1 mph) of trips [P*]
variables.impact_evidence: Published NYC travel-time studies drop trips under 10 s or over 24 h [S]
variables.how_to_model: Documented filter step in the data pipeline with counts removed per rule.

variables.name: Data-era alignment
variables.description: Matching the speed data year to the scenario year, since NYC speeds shifted with FHV growth, COVID and congestion pricing.
variables.values_or_range: 2010-2017 decline (9.1 to 7.1 mph south of 60th St); 2020-21 COVID anomaly [U]; Jan 2025 congestion-pricing step change
variables.impact_evidence: NYC DOT Mobility Reports [S]; NBER w33584 [S]
variables.how_to_model: Calibrate each scenario on the same months it replays, so demand and speeds come from one era.

variables.name: Time-dependent routing consistency (FIFO)
variables.description: Long trips cross speed buckets, so travel time must be integrated over time and a later departure must never arrive earlier.
variables.values_or_range: buckets 5-60 min; trips up to 90+ min
variables.impact_evidence: [design] standard requirement for time-dependent shortest paths
variables.how_to_model: Time-dependent Dijkstra evaluating each edge at its entry time, with smoothed bucket boundaries.

variables.name: Sub-trip position trace
variables.description: Second-by-second position along the route, needed for the live map and for meter time and distance accounting.
variables.values_or_range: tick 1-10 s of simulated time [design]
variables.impact_evidence: [design] team notes ask for a live map with moving cars and sped-up time
variables.how_to_model: Interpolate along the route polyline using edge-level times and emit positions to the visualiser.

variables.name: Common random numbers for traffic noise
variables.description: Identical random seeds for traffic noise across models, so profit differences reflect decisions rather than luck.
variables.values_or_range: fixed seed per scenario-day; 100 runs per model (team plan)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] the team plan of 5 models x 100 runs needs variance control
variables.how_to_model: Pre-generate day, zone and edge noise fields per seed; key trip noise by (seed, OD, departure bucket).

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Fleet size N
variables.description: Number of cars the model controls in a fleet run.
variables.values_or_range: 1 (single-car level), 5, 10, 25, 100, 500; stretch 1,000-5,000. Anchors: a Manhattan robotaxi sim needed ~3,000 cars to serve ~90% and ~5,000 to serve ~100% of ~150k Manhattan-internal weekday app requests (greedy dispatch); Waymo's whole US fleet is ~3,000-3,800 cars (R06-056) [uncertain: ~3,000 in early 2026 is Waymo's own figure (Vital City methodology, S); the 3,800 upper figure (Jalopnik, May 2026 recall) was not re-checked].
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim greedy sweep of 1,500-6,000 cars on June 2024 HVFHV trips: unserved demand 47.7% to 0%, utilisation 57% to 28% [S, GitHub README read directly].
variables.data_source: Harness setting; demand scale from NYC TLC HVFHV trip records https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-trip-record-data.page
variables.how_to_model: Harness parameter; run a ladder of N on the same seed and demand; report profit per fleet and per car.

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Active fleet by hour (dynamic fleet sizing)
variables.description: How many of the N cars the model keeps on duty each hour, while the rest wait at a depot, charge or rest.
variables.values_or_range: 0-N per hour; e.g. 100% at 7-10 am and 5-9 pm, 30-50% at 3-5 am [design].
variables.impact_evidence: FleetPy ships time-based and utilisation-based dynamic fleet sizing (target utilisation band, minimum active fleet; inactive cars go to the nearest depot and charge there) [P, code read on GitHub].
variables.data_source: Hourly demand curve from TLC trip records (R02); FleetPy reference code https://github.com/TUM-VT/FleetPy
variables.how_to_model: Action set_active(k, hour); deactivated cars drive to a depot; on-duty costs (remote assistance, wear, wages) accrue only while active.

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Vehicle class mix
variables.description: Share of the fleet in each vehicle type: battery EV, hybrid or gas, and standard, large (XL) or wheelchair-accessible (WAV).
variables.values_or_range: e.g. 100% EV; 80/20 EV/hybrid; XL 0-15%; WAV 0-25% [design]. The NYC for-hire fleet is mostly hybrid and gas with a growing EV share [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [verified by fact-check, P*, was U] Green Rides, 35 RCNY 59D-13(c): each HVFHS must dispatch at least 5% (2024), 15% (2025), 25% (2026), 40% (2027), 60% (2028), 80% (2029) and 100% (2030) of its trips to zero-emission or wheelchair-accessible vehicles, fine $50 per 1,000 trips short; per-type running costs are in R08.
variables.data_source: NYC Open Data 'For Hire Vehicles (FHV) - Active' https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Transportation/For-Hire-Vehicles-FHV-Active/8wbx-tsch [U]; 'Medallion Vehicles - Authorized' https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Transportation/Medallion-Vehicles-Authorized/rhe8-mgbb [U]
variables.how_to_model: Each car has a type with seats, product eligibility, range and cost; the mix is fixed per run or chosen at the start under a capital budget.

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Driver-type mix in the fleet
variables.description: Whether fleet cars are driverless or driven by employees, contractors or lessees, each with its own rules and costs.
variables.values_or_range: 100% robotaxi / 100% human / mixed, e.g. robotaxis inside a geofence plus human cars for airports and freeways.
variables.impact_evidence: Waymo freeway and airport limits (R06-058, R10-023) and Uber dispatching Waymo cars beside human drivers in Austin and Atlanta (R06-059) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Per-car flag selects a rule set: robotaxi (geofence, no breaks, remote assistance) or human (shifts, breaks, compliance R11-018).

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Starting positions
variables.description: Where the fleet's cars are when the run starts.
variables.values_or_range: all at one depot / spread over several depots / proportional to historical pickups at the start hour / random / all in one zone (stress test).
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; at about 1 empty mile per trip in Manhattan (fleetsim) a bad start costs each car a few empty trips; matters for the first 1-3 hours, little over several days.
variables.data_source: TLC trip records for the historical pickup distribution
variables.how_to_model: Harness option with a fixed seed; give every model the same start or report scores per start mode.

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Starting energy and condition
variables.description: Battery or fuel level, cleanliness and maintenance clock of each car at the start.
variables.values_or_range: all 100%; uniform 40-100%; 'morning after an overnight charge' 90-100% [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; energy binds within a single day: with no charging policy 4-12% of demand goes unserved (fleetsim) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Initial state vector per car drawn from the chosen profile with a fixed seed.

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Fleet growth between days
variables.description: Whether the model may add or retire cars between days, with a lead time and a capital or lease cost.
variables.values_or_range: fixed N (default) / plus or minus 10% per week, 1-7 day delivery, lease cost per car-day [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; rival supply re-equilibrates over about two months after pay changes (Hall et al., R06-012) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Off in v1; in multi-day campaigns, a daily 'order or return cars' action with cost and delay.

variables.sub_box: A. Fleet size, mix and starting state
variables.name: Regulatory cap on fleet size and licences
variables.description: Legal limits on how many cars, and which kinds, the fleet may run.
variables.values_or_range: NYC: new FHV licences paused since 2018 with exceptions (e.g. WAVs; only WAV licences in 2026) (R06-053); NYC AV test permit for 8 cars with safety drivers expired 31 Mar 2026 (R06-056); robotaxi cap 0 to unlimited as a scenario.
variables.impact_evidence: TLC licence pause (R06-053) and NYC AV permit (R06-056) [S]; legal basis: NYC Admin Code 19-550 lets the TLC regulate the number of FHV licences and vary it for wheelchair-accessible and low- or zero-emission vehicles [P*, added by fact-check]; 34 RCNY 4-17 allows AV testing in NYC only with a trained operator in the driver's seat, a $5,000 annual permit and at least $5M of auto insurance [P*, added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Harness cap on N and on the robotaxi share per scenario.

variables.name: Control architecture
variables.description: How the model is wired to the cars: one central fleet brain, one model instance per car, a hierarchy where the model sets targets and an algorithm executes, or a policy the model writes as code.
variables.values_or_range: centralised / decentralised per car / hierarchical (model every 5-15 min, algorithm every few seconds) / policy-as-code.
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; LLM-E-AMoD had ChatGPT and Gemini write MPC controllers for a 250-EV rebalancing and charging problem rather than decide each step [S, GitHub README, re-read by fact-check: a synthetic 20-node, 10 x 10 km MATLAB network, not NYC]; LLM4RD uses an LLM to design reward functions for multi-agent (MAPPO) EV ride-hailing scheduling, default 1,200 vehicles [S, README read directly by fact-check; was a GitHub listing].
variables.how_to_model: Harness modes over one simulator API; v1 hierarchical so that model cost scales with time, not with N.

variables.name: Dispatch authority and action set
variables.description: Who assigns requests to the fleet's cars, and so what the model may do: only reposition and accept, assign every request itself, or choose which own car takes a platform offer.
variables.values_or_range: platform-dispatched (Uber/Lyft fleet owner under an NYC base) / self-dispatched (robotaxi operator app, taxi e-hail) / platform offers, operator assigns (Uber-Waymo Austin model).
variables.impact_evidence: Uber matches riders to Waymo cars in Austin and Atlanta while a partner runs fleet operations (R06-059) [S]; the matcher-side flag is R06-063.
variables.how_to_model: Action schema per mode; in self-dispatch the model or its algorithm calls assign(request, car) inside the batch window (R11-011).

variables.name: Dispatch batching window
variables.description: How long requests are pooled before the fleet assigns them to cars.
variables.values_or_range: 0 s (greedy, first come) / 10-60 s / up to 300 s.
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim at 3,000 cars: a 30 s batch cut deadhead 8.2% and median wait 5.3% vs greedy; 300 s cut deadhead 14.8% but raised wait [S]; Uber batches over a few seconds (R06-020) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Matcher parameter; min-cost bipartite assignment per window; under platform dispatch it is a fixed rule.

variables.name: Strategic decision epoch
variables.description: How often the model is asked to re-plan repositioning, charging and the active fleet.
variables.values_or_range: every 1, 5, 15, 30 or 60 sim minutes, plus event triggers (surge, failure, let-out).
variables.impact_evidence: [corrected by fact-check: impact was high; no evidence supports high, and fleetsim found the strategic repositioning layer moved median wait only about 8% once a coded matcher dispatches, so the epoch mainly sets token cost (R11-014)]; offpeak repositions idle cars every 15 min [S]; gnn-rl-for-amod runs rebalancing on a coarse time step (json_tstep, default 3; the command-line flag is spelled --json_tsetp in main.py) [P, code]; [design] shorter epochs react faster but cost more tokens.
variables.how_to_model: Harness clock calls the model every k minutes and on flagged events; a default policy runs in between.

variables.name: Model latency against the simulated clock
variables.description: Whether the simulation pauses while the model thinks, or keeps running so that slow answers cost trips.
variables.values_or_range: paused (turn-based) / real time with 1-60 s latency mapped to sim time / scaled (1 s wall = k s sim).
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; a coded dispatcher answers in 0.81 ms inside a 30 s window (fleetsim) [S], so a 10-30 s model call is slow by comparison.
variables.how_to_model: Harness logs measured latency; in real-time mode the affected cars keep their old plan until the answer arrives.

variables.name: Compute and token budget per run
variables.description: Cap on model calls, tokens or dollars for one evaluation run, which limits how many cars can get individual attention.
variables.values_or_range: about $20 per run (team estimate); per-car control of 100 cars at one call per 5 min is 28,800 calls a day [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Team cost estimate of $10K for 5 models x 100 runs x $20 (meeting notes) and arithmetic [design].
variables.how_to_model: Harness meter; when the budget runs out, cars fall back to a default policy; report profit per dollar of compute.

variables.name: Own-fleet state visibility
variables.description: What the model knows about its own cars at each call.
variables.values_or_range: full telemetry (position, status, battery, ETA, cleanliness) for robotaxis / delayed or partial for human-driven cars / nothing in real time (classic taxi garage).
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; robotaxi fleets stream telemetry to remote operations (R09-048, R09-049) [S]; taxi garages see cars only at shift change [corrected by fact-check: NYC taxi technology systems must record each logged-on cab's position at least every 30 s (35 RCNY 66-03(h), P*), so the data exist; whether owners or garages can see it live was not confirmed].
variables.how_to_model: Observation builder with per-field delay and noise by driver type.

variables.name: Information sharing between own cars
variables.description: In decentralised mode, what one car's agent can see of the others.
variables.values_or_range: none / shared heat map / shared notes file / direct messages.
variables.impact_evidence: AMoDeus lists rebalancing policies 'without explicit communication' (Arsie et al. 2009) as their own class [P, README]; sharing between rival fleets is R06-065.
variables.how_to_model: Harness toggle; log messages; measure clustering (R11-028) with and without sharing.

variables.name: Demand forecast given to the fleet controller
variables.description: The demand outlook supplied to the model at each call.
variables.values_or_range: none / historical mean by zone and hour / noisy forecast / oracle (true future requests).
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim: an oracle forecast gave the same wait as the historical mean but ordered 20-30% more moves and empty miles [S].
variables.data_source: TLC trip records (historical zone-hour means); event calendars (R03)
variables.how_to_model: Forecast service with selectable quality; the event-information toggle is the with/without event awareness prompt test.

variables.name: Human driver compliance with fleet instructions
variables.description: Chance that a human driver follows the fleet's repositioning, charging or break instruction.
variables.values_or_range: robotaxi 100%; employee drivers 80-95%; contractors 20-60% [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] NYC app drivers are independent contractors who choose where to drive; [U] Revel ran an all-EV ride-hail fleet with employee drivers in NYC [uncertain: not re-checkable this session, including whether Revel still runs ride-hail in NYC].
variables.applies_to: human app driver fleet, taxi fleet
variables.how_to_model: Bernoulli draw per instruction and driver, lower late in the shift and for targets far from home (R09-015).

variables.name: Idle-car repositioning decision
variables.description: Where each idle fleet car goes after a drop-off: stay, cruise, or drive empty to a target zone.
variables.values_or_range: any of 263 taxi zones; 0-30 min of empty driving; per car or as a zone quota.
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim at 5,000 cars: forecast-driven repositioning cut median wait 8.0% and p90 wait 12.5% [S]; the single-car version is R09-052/053.
variables.data_source: TLC HVFHV request times by zone; TLC taxi zone shapefile
variables.how_to_model: Action reposition(car or k cars, zone); travel time from R10; cars can be matched en route.

variables.name: Rebalancing objective and target distribution
variables.description: What the fleet balances idle cars against (request counts, fare value or unmet demand) and over what horizon.
variables.values_or_range: proportional to requests / to fare value / to forecast shortfall; horizon 15-60 min.
variables.impact_evidence: gnn-rl-for-amod sets a desired distribution and then solves a min-cost rebalancing flow (reb_flow_solver) [P, code]; Pavone et al. 2012 fluid rebalancing is listed in AMoDeus [P, README].
variables.data_source: TLC trip records (fares by zone and hour)
variables.how_to_model: Model outputs a target share per zone; an LP turns targets into car moves.

variables.name: Repositioning reach cap
variables.description: Maximum empty-drive time the fleet allows for one repositioning move.
variables.values_or_range: 5-30 min; fleetsim used 20 min.
variables.impact_evidence: [corrected by fact-check: impact was low] fleetsim 20-minute reachability cap [S]; the README says the cap gated the whole policy: with a 10-min cap only 5.5% of zone pairs were reachable at midday and repositioning gave -1.2% wait for +6.6% empty miles, while 20 min gave -8.0% wait for +87% empty miles (empty-mile cost per 1% of wait rose from 5.5% to 10.9%) [S, re-read by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Constraint in the move LP or a validity check on each action.

variables.name: Empty miles from rebalancing
variables.description: Unpaid miles the fleet drives to pickups, repositioning and charging, which cost energy, wear and tolls.
variables.values_or_range: about 0.9-1.0 empty miles per trip without repositioning [corrected by fact-check: greedy pickup deadhead was 0.90-1.10 mi per trip across 1,500-6,000 cars and 0.85-0.87 with batching; 0.906 at 5,000 cars] and about 1.7 with it (Manhattan robotaxi sim); about one third of Manhattan cars empty at any moment (R06-002).
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim: repositioning raised empty miles per trip 87% (0.906 to 1.697), about 11% more empty miles per 1% of wait removed [S].
variables.data_source: TLC trip records (trip miles) for calibration
variables.how_to_model: Summed per car; cost per mile from R08; empty-mile share reported as a KPI.

variables.name: Idle staging capacity
variables.description: Number of legal places in a zone where idle fleet cars can wait without circling, double parking or paying a garage.
variables.values_or_range: 0-50 cars per zone [design]; garage cost per hour; robotaxis need a legal stop.
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; legal waiting spots (R01-032) and hotspot curb queues (R10-040).
variables.data_source: NYC parking regulations and licensed garages on NYC Open Data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Staging capacity per zone; extra idle cars must circle (miles) or use a paid lot.

variables.name: Airport allocation across the fleet
variables.description: How many fleet cars to commit to the JFK and LaGuardia queues at the same time.
variables.values_or_range: 0-20% of the fleet [design]; own cars ahead in a first-in-first-out queue lengthen each other's wait.
variables.impact_evidence: Airport queue waits of 1-3 h (R06-041) [S]; robotaxis may lack freeway access to airports (R10-023) [S].
variables.data_source: TLC trip records (zones 132 JFK, 138 LaGuardia); flight schedules (R05-062)
variables.how_to_model: Queue per airport with own cars counted; marginal value of the k-th car in the queue.

variables.name: Event pre-positioning
variables.description: How many fleet cars to stage near a venue before a let-out (Madison Square Garden, Barclays Center, Yankee Stadium, Citi Field, US Open).
variables.values_or_range: 0-50 cars; arrive 0-30 min before the end [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Event let-out convergence (R06-052) [S]; [U] Cruise robotaxis stalled near a 2023 San Francisco music festival when cellular links were congested [uncertain: news recollection (Outside Lands, Aug 2023), not re-checkable this session].
variables.data_source: NYC permitted event calendar on NYC Open Data; venue schedules (R03)
variables.how_to_model: Event demand pulse; staging limited by R11-023; overcommitment shows up as cannibalisation.

variables.name: Return to base with revenue
variables.description: Taking last trips that end near the depot or the driver's home before charging, cleaning or shift end: the fleet version of 'take me home'.
variables.values_or_range: destination radius 1-5 km; start 30-90 min before the planned return [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Destination filter mechanics (R06-028, R09-017) [S]; [design].
variables.how_to_model: A 'heading to base' flag biases matching toward trips that end near the base.

variables.name: Reference rebalancing baselines
variables.description: Non-LLM fleet policies run on the same scenarios to anchor model scores.
variables.values_or_range: no repositioning; greedy nearest dispatch; proportional LP (Pavone-style); model predictive control; a published RL policy.
variables.impact_evidence: AMoDeus ships about ten unit-capacity dispatch and rebalancing algorithms plus four ride-sharing ones (GPL-2.0, LICENSE.txt checked) [P, README]; FleetPy ships Alonso-Mora, Pavone and linear-hailing repositioning modules (MIT) [P, code: src/misc/init_modules.py re-read by fact-check]; FleetPy's optimisation modules use Gurobi, free only under an academic licence [P, README, added by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Port 2-3 baselines into the harness; report model profit as a % of the best baseline at the same N.

variables.name: Own-car clustering (herding)
variables.description: Fleet cars piling into the same hotspot because they react to the same signal, leaving gaps elsewhere.
variables.values_or_range: own idle cars per zone vs forecast requests; dispersion index from 0 (spread) to 1 (all in one zone).
variables.impact_evidence: [U] DiDi's multi-agent RL for fleet repositioning (Lin et al., KDD 2018) was built to stop agents chasing the same orders [uncertain: paper not re-read this session]; surge chasing herds human drivers (R06-011) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Compute a dispersion metric every epoch; show it on the map.

variables.name: Anti-clustering rule
variables.description: A cap or penalty on how many own idle cars may sit in one zone.
variables.values_or_range: none / soft penalty / hard cap per zone, e.g. at most 1.2 x forecast requests per 15 min [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design].
variables.how_to_model: Constraint in the move LP, or a harness guard that rejects moves above the cap.

variables.name: Fleet saturation curve (value of the N-th car)
variables.description: How revenue and utilisation per car fall as the fleet grows in a fixed market.
variables.values_or_range: Manhattan robotaxi sim: utilisation 57% at 1,500 cars, 50% at 3,000, 34% at 5,000, 28% at 6,000.
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim greedy sweep [S]; own-fleet cannibalisation (R06-062); Vazifeh et al. 2018: about 30% fewer cars could serve NYC taxi demand (R06-062) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Run N and N+dN on the same seed; report marginal profit per added car.

variables.name: Territory partition
variables.description: Whether cars are given home territories or float across the whole city.
variables.values_or_range: free-floating / k territories / one borough each.
variables.impact_evidence: [design].
variables.how_to_model: Optional home-zone constraint per car.

variables.name: Fleet ride pooling
variables.description: Combining riders from the fleet's own requests into one car.
variables.values_or_range: off / up to 2 / up to 4 riders.
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Alonso-Mora et al. 2017 (PNAS): about 3,000 four-seat cars could serve about 98% of NYC taxi demand [uncertain: paper not reachable this session]; the algorithm ships in AMoDeus ('High-Capacity Algorithm') and FleetPy (pooling/batch/AlonsoMora) [P, re-checked by fact-check].
variables.how_to_model: Insertion heuristic; off in v1.

variables.name: Earnings fairness across fleet drivers
variables.description: How evenly the fleet spreads good trips among its human drivers.
variables.values_or_range: Gini of driver daily pay 0.1-0.4 [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design].
variables.applies_to: human app driver fleet, taxi fleet
variables.how_to_model: Track pay per driver; optional attrition penalty when a driver's pay falls below a threshold.

variables.name: Charger-to-vehicle ratio
variables.description: Number of charging plugs the fleet can use per car.
variables.values_or_range: 1:15 (36 x 150 kW for 550 cars; offpeak's cars serve a 20% sample of Manhattan yellow-taxi demand [added by fact-check]), 1:23 (24 chargers), 1:42 (120 chargers for 5,000 cars); a Waymo SF depot had 19 dual chargers (R09-045).
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak: 24 chargers with smart scheduling served 96.1% of riders vs 93.4% with 72 chargers and a threshold rule [S]; fleetsim used 120 chargers at 10 sites [S].
variables.how_to_model: Charger nodes with plug count and power; cars queue when all plugs are busy.

variables.name: Charging schedule policy
variables.description: When fleet cars charge and to what level: fixed thresholds, top-ups in demand troughs, joint with dispatch, or overnight only.
variables.values_or_range: threshold 20 to 80%; 20 to 100%; trough top-ups; joint min-cost with dispatch.
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak: orchestrated charging served 3.4 points more riders at 15% lower energy cost than a 20-80% threshold [S]; fleetsim: no charging policy leaves 4-12% of demand unserved [S].
variables.how_to_model: Charging as a per-car action or a policy parameter set; charge time from charger power and taper (R08).

variables.name: Charger queue
variables.description: Waiting time for a free plug when many fleet cars arrive together.
variables.values_or_range: mean 2-27 min depending on policy (Manhattan sim).
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak mean charger queue: 2.3 min (queue-aware) to 26.6 min (charge to 100%) [S].
variables.how_to_model: First-in-first-out queue per site; queue length shown to the model.

variables.name: Charging site count and placement
variables.description: How many charging sites the fleet uses and where they are.
variables.values_or_range: 1-12 sites; mean drive to a charger 12.9 min (1 site) to 5.6 min (12 sites).
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak siting study: 6 p-median sites cut mean drive to 6.5 min and charger-trip distance about 25% vs the 6 busiest drop-off zones, while riders served changed by under 0.5 points [S].
variables.data_source: AFDC stations; NYC MapPLUTO zoning for candidate sites [U]
variables.how_to_model: Site list per scenario; optional p-median solver if the model chooses sites.

variables.name: Private depot vs public charging mix
variables.description: Share of charging done at the fleet's own depots versus public fast chargers shared with other EVs.
variables.values_or_range: private only / public only / mix; public price and occupancy vary by hour.
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak: two busy Palo Alto public sites had no free port 20-25% of weekday working hours [S]; [U] Revel built its own fast-charging hubs in NYC.
variables.how_to_model: Public chargers with hourly background occupancy and a posted price; private chargers carry a fixed cost.

variables.name: Fleet peak power, grid connection and demand charges
variables.description: The fleet's combined charging load, the depot's grid limit and the utility's charge on peak kW.
variables.values_or_range: about 3.1-3.6 MW peak for 550 cars (about 6 kW per car) [corrected by fact-check: 2.2-3.6 MW across offpeak's policies (2.19 MW when charging to 100%), with 36 x 150 kW = 5.4 MW installed]; demand charge in $/kW-month [U].
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak peak loads of 3.12-3.61 MW; demand charges not modelled there [S]; [U] Con Edison commercial tariffs bill peak demand.
variables.data_source: Con Edison tariffs https://www.coned.com/en/rates-tariffs [U]; NYISO prices https://www.nyiso.com/energy-market-operational-data [U]
variables.how_to_model: Depot kW cap; monthly peak charge prorated per day.

variables.name: Dispatch battery reserve
variables.description: Minimum charge a car must keep after a trip and the drive to a charger before it may accept a request.
variables.values_or_range: 5-20%, or 'enough for the trip plus the nearest charger' [design].
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak uses a 5% reserve and an energy-sufficiency check [S]; fleetsim's joint policy plugged in at 25-30% vs 10-20% for the naive rule [S].
variables.how_to_model: Feasibility filter in matching; a stranding event if a battery reaches 0.

variables.name: Share of fleet charging at peaks
variables.description: Fraction of the fleet plugged in during demand peaks, the visible cost of a poor charging plan.
variables.values_or_range: 0-20% at 5-8 pm [design]; robotaxis charge about 1-3 h a day (R06-058).
variables.impact_evidence: offpeak ablation: removing trough top-ups cut riders served from 96.2% [corrected by fact-check: the 6-seed ablation baseline is 96.2%; 96.1% is the 10-seed headline] to 95.1%, removing early unplugging for waiting riders to 95.8% [S].
variables.how_to_model: Hourly KPI; option to unplug early when riders are waiting.

variables.name: Fleet availability (uptime share)
variables.description: Share of fleet car-hours in service rather than charging, cleaning, in maintenance, in repair or parked.
variables.values_or_range: robotaxi about 75-90% (20-22 h a day per car, R09-044) [design] [corrected by fact-check: 20-22 h a day is 83-92%; 75% would be 18 h]; double-shift taxi 16-22 h a day [U]; single-shift human 8-12 h.
variables.impact_evidence: The Waymo-Lyft Nashville depot runs 24/7 in three shifts to charge, clean and maintain cars (R09-044) [S]; Waymo about 20 trips per car-day (R06-057) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Status machine per car; availability = in-service hours / total hours.

variables.name: Depot siting and cost
variables.description: Number and location of depots, and the cost of land, stalls and deadhead to demand.
variables.values_or_range: 1-6 depots; NYC industrial areas such as Long Island City, Maspeth, Woodside, Red Hook, Hunts Point [U]; stall cost about $300-1,000 a month [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] NYC yellow-cab garages cluster in western Queens [uncertain: recollection, not re-checkable this session]; depot geography in R01-063 and R09-045.
variables.how_to_model: Depot nodes with capacity and daily cost; depot-to-zone times from R10.

variables.name: Depot throughput
variables.description: How many cars per hour a depot can clean, inspect, charge and park.
variables.values_or_range: 2-10 cleaning bays; 10-30 min per clean (R09-047); about 70 staff per depot (R09-045).
variables.impact_evidence: Depots of about 70 staff each (R09-045) [S]; cleaning dwell (R09-047) [design].
variables.how_to_model: Multi-server queue per service at each depot.

variables.name: Preventive maintenance and inspection rotation
variables.description: Scheduled downtime per car for service, tyres, sensor calibration and regulatory inspection, and how the fleet staggers it.
variables.values_or_range: 2-6 h per 5,000-10,000 miles [design]; NYC taxis must be inspected every four months (35 RCNY 58-29(b)) and FHVs three times a year (35 RCNY 59A-26(a)) [verified by fact-check, P*, was U]; the TLC Safety and Emissions facility is in Woodside [U].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] TLC inspection schedule (35 RCNY 58-29, 59A-26); [design].
variables.how_to_model: Mileage and calendar counters; maintenance slots booked in low-demand hours.

variables.name: Unscheduled breakdown hazard and repair time
variables.description: Chance that a fleet car breaks down (flat tyre, fault, crash damage) and how long it is out.
variables.values_or_range: 0.5-3 failures per 10,000 vehicle-hours; out 1 h to 5 days [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; stuck-vehicle recovery for robotaxis (R09-050).
variables.data_source: NYPD Motor Vehicle Collisions https://data.cityofnewyork.us/Public-Safety/Motor-Vehicle-Collisions-Crashes/h9gi-nx95 [U] as a crash-rate proxy
variables.how_to_model: Hazard per mile and hour; repair-time draw; tow to depot.

variables.name: Spare vehicle ratio
variables.description: Share of the fleet held back to replace cars in repair or maintenance.
variables.values_or_range: 0-20% [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] US transit bus fleets use a 20% spare-ratio guideline (FTA) [uncertain: recalled FTA guidance for fleets of 50 or more buses; not re-checkable this session].
variables.how_to_model: Spares sit at the depot at low cost and are swapped in on failure.

variables.name: Mileage balancing and vehicle retirement
variables.description: Spreading miles evenly across cars and retiring cars at age or mileage limits.
variables.values_or_range: 50,000-100,000 miles a year for a 24/7 robotaxi [design]; TLC vehicle age limits [verified by fact-check, P*, was U: taxis must be retired at the first inspection 84 months after hack-up, and accessible cabs may stay on while they pass inspection (35 RCNY 67-18); the FHV retirement provision (35 RCNY 59A-28(d)) is repealed, so no TLC age cap for FHVs was found].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 67-18 and 59A-28; [design].
variables.how_to_model: Odometer per car; depreciation per mile (R08); multi-week runs only.

variables.sub_box: G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
variables.name: Labour and operating model
variables.description: Who drives the fleet's cars and how they are paid, which sets the fleet's cost per hour.
variables.values_or_range: robotaxi (remote assistance plus field staff) / employees on an hourly wage (NYC minimum about $16.50-17 an hour in 2025-26 [U] [uncertain: not re-checkable this session]) / contractors on TLC per-trip minimum pay (R07) / lessees paying a shift lease / outsourced fleet partner [corrected by fact-check: Waymo's fleet partners are Moove (Phoenix, Miami) and Avomo (Austin, Atlanta, Uber-dispatched rides) per industry notes on GitHub [S], and Lyft in Nashville (R09-044) [S]; Avis was not confirmed by any source read].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] NYC minimum wage schedule; Waymo's partner fleet operators [S]; TLC driver pay rules (R07).
variables.data_source: NY State minimum wage https://dol.ny.gov/minimum-wage-0 [U]; TLC driver pay rules (R07)
variables.how_to_model: Cost function per model: wage x paid hours, per-trip pay, or lease income.

variables.sub_box: G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
variables.name: Human fleet shift roster
variables.description: When each human-driven fleet car is on the road (shift starts, lengths, handovers), compared with a robotaxi running 24/7.
variables.values_or_range: 8-12 h shifts; staggered starts to cover 7-10 am and 5-9 pm peaks; double shift of two 12 h shifts per car [verified by fact-check, P*, was U].
variables.impact_evidence: NYC taxi day and night lease shifts of 12 consecutive hours (35 RCNY 58-21, via R09-003) [P*] with the 4-5 pm change (R02-044, R06-018) [S]; single-driver hours in R09-001/002.
variables.applies_to: human app driver fleet, taxi fleet
variables.data_source: TLC trip records (hourly demand curve, R02)
variables.how_to_model: Roster action per day; each handover at the depot costs deadhead and 10-30 min.

variables.sub_box: G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
variables.name: Double-shifting and lease or rental income
variables.description: For taxi and rental fleets, earning a fixed lease per shift while drivers keep the fares, and running each car for two shifts.
variables.values_or_range: taxi lease caps about $100-130 per 12 h shift [corrected by fact-check: $105-129 per 12 h shift for cab plus medallion ($108-132 for hybrids) and $630-737 a week, 35 RCNY 58-21(c), P*]; weekly TLC car rental about $400-600 [U] [uncertain: FHV rentals have no rate cap, only disclosure rules (Admin Code 19-553), and the range was not checked]; single vs double shift.
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] TLC lease caps (35 RCNY 58-21); lease shift structure in R02-045 and R09-003.
variables.applies_to: taxi fleet, human app driver (rental) fleet
variables.data_source: TLC rules (lease caps) https://www.nyc.gov/site/tlc/about/tlc-rules.page [U]; verbatim 35 RCNY 58-21 at https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive [P*]
variables.how_to_model: Alternative fleet business model: fleet profit = leases minus fixed costs, with drivers as R06 bots.

variables.sub_box: G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
variables.name: Remote-assistance pool sizing and queue
variables.description: How many remote agents the robotaxi fleet staffs, and how long cars wait for help when many ask at once.
variables.values_or_range: about 1 agent per 15-45 cars (Cruise about 1:15-20, Waymo about 1:43, R09-049); correlated surges at events and outages.
variables.impact_evidence: Waymo Senate testimony and reply to Sen. Markey; CNBC on Cruise (via R09-049) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Multi-server queue with c agents on shift; request rate per car from R09-048; cost = agents x wage.

variables.sub_box: G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
variables.name: Field and depot staff
variables.description: Cleaners, technicians, charger handlers and recovery drivers the fleet needs per car-day.
variables.values_or_range: about 70 staff per depot in three 24/7 shifts [S]; 0.1-0.3 staff per car [design].
variables.impact_evidence: WSMV on the Nashville depot (R09-044) and Jalopnik on depot staffing (R09-045) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Staff per depot x wage; recovery response time depends on field staff on shift.

variables.sub_box: G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
variables.name: Fleet fixed-cost stack per car-day
variables.description: Costs the fleet pays per car per day whether or not it drives: insurance, licences, financing or depreciation, depot stall, software and base fees.
variables.values_or_range: about $40-150 per car-day [design]; TLC commercial insurance is several thousand dollars a year per car [U]; fixed licence items include the TLC vehicle licence of $550 per car per 2 years and, for an own app, the HVFHS licence of $190,000 a year (R07-058) [P*, added by fact-check].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; per-vehicle cost items in R08.
variables.data_source: TLC licence fees [U]; insurance filings with NY DFS [U]
variables.how_to_model: Daily fixed charge per car on the fleet's books; idle and spare cars still pay it.

variables.sub_box: G. Operating model, staffing and fixed costs
variables.name: Base affiliation and licensing overhead
variables.description: In NYC every for-hire car must belong to a licensed base, which brings fees and reporting duties.
variables.values_or_range: own base ($500 a year base licence fee, 35 RCNY 59B-07) vs affiliation with an Uber or Lyft base; each FHV must affiliate with one base, and only one at a time (35 RCNY 59A-04(h)-(i)) [verified by fact-check, P*, was U]; other cities use TNC or AV permits instead.
variables.applies_to: human app driver fleet, robotaxi fleet (NYC-specific)
variables.data_source: NYC Open Data FHV Base Aggregate Report [U]
variables.how_to_model: Fixed fee and data-reporting duty per scenario.

variables.sub_box: H. Market impact and service obligations
variables.name: Fleet effect on surge and fares
variables.description: A large fleet fills shortages, so surge fires less and fares fall for everyone, the fleet included.
variables.values_or_range: negligible below 100 cars in NYC (under 1% of supply, R06-061); material at 5-10% or more of local supply.
variables.impact_evidence: Fleet share (R06-061) and Hall et al. re-equilibration (R06-012) [S]; [design].
variables.how_to_model: The surge engine (R07) counts fleet cars in local idle supply.

variables.sub_box: H. Market impact and service obligations
variables.name: Fleet effect on wait times and induced demand
variables.description: More fleet cars shorten pickup times, which draws more requests and fewer cancellations.
variables.values_or_range: Manhattan robotaxi sim: median wait 18.5 min with 1,500 cars to 7.2 min with 6,000; the real operator's median is about 3 min.
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim sweep [S]; induced demand (R05-068); increasing returns to scale in matching (Frechette et al. 2019, via R05) [S].
variables.data_source: HVFHV request_datetime and on_scene_datetime [corrected by fact-check: on_scene_datetime is filled for Uber trips and missing for Lyft trips (fleetsim EDA, S), so wait calibration rests on Uber rows]
variables.how_to_model: Rider ETA sensitivity (R05-021) plus a zone demand multiplier tied to recent service.

variables.sub_box: H. Market impact and service obligations
variables.name: Service coverage and equity obligations
variables.description: Rules or permit conditions that make the fleet serve all boroughs, night hours or minimum response times.
variables.values_or_range: none / outer-borough share of at least X% / maximum p90 wait / green-cab-style hail zone [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; green taxi hail zone (R01-006).
variables.how_to_model: Constraint with penalties in the score.

variables.sub_box: H. Market impact and service obligations
variables.name: Wheelchair-accessible service obligation
variables.description: NYC rules on accessible vehicles and response times, which fix part of the fleet mix and its positioning.
variables.values_or_range: HVFHV bases must answer most WAV requests within 10-15 min [corrected by fact-check: each FHV base must either send at least 25% of its trips to accessible vehicles (since July 2022) or join an approved accessible-vehicle dispatcher that serves at least 90% of WAV requests in under 10 min (35 RCNY 59B-17(c)(1)(v) and (f)(3)), and every HVFHS app must let riders request a WAV (59D-13(b)), P*]; yellow fleet goal of half accessible cabs [uncertain: the conversion schedule in 35 RCNY 58-50(a)-(d) now reads 'Reserved'; accessible cabs get at least $20,000 at hack-up plus $10,000 over 4 years from the Taxi Improvement Fund, and drivers $10 per accessible-dispatch trip (58-50(i)), P*].
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] 35 RCNY 59B-17, 59D-13 and 58-50; HVFHV wav_request_flag and wav_match_flag columns (R05-031) [S]; WAVs did about 9% of 2025 app trips (R06) [S].
variables.applies_to: human app driver fleet, taxi fleet
variables.how_to_model: WAV request stream; penalty if response targets are missed; WAV cars cost more (R08).

variables.name: Correlated fleet-wide outage
variables.description: One cause grounding many or all fleet cars at once: a software fault or recall, lost connectivity, a power blackout or a permit suspension.
variables.values_or_range: 0-2 events a year; lasting 1 h to weeks; 10-100% of the fleet [design].
variables.impact_evidence: Waymo fleet-wide software recall in May 2026 after flooded-road incidents (R06-058) [S]; [U] Cruise lost its California permit in Oct 2023 and halted its fleet; [U] Waymo cars stalled at dark signals in a Dec 2025 San Francisco blackout [uncertain: both are news recollections, not re-checkable this session].
variables.data_source: NHTSA recalls https://www.nhtsa.gov/recalls [U]; NHTSA Standing General Order crash reports [U]
variables.how_to_model: Rare scenario shock applied to all cars of one type; used in stress-test scenarios.

variables.name: Mid-trip failure handling
variables.description: What the fleet does when a car fails with a rider aboard: send another own car, refund, or leave the rider to rebook.
variables.values_or_range: rescue ETA 5-20 min; refund 0-100%; rating hit [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; stuck-vehicle recovery (R09-050).
variables.how_to_model: The event triggers a decision; a rescue trip gets priority; costs are logged.

variables.name: Crash and liability tail
variables.description: Rare severe crashes whose claims, deductibles and suspensions fall on the fleet.
variables.values_or_range: claim $10k to over $1M; probability per million miles by driver type [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Waymo reports fewer injury crashes per mile than human benchmarks; NHTSA SGO data [uncertain: not re-checkable this session].
variables.how_to_model: Per-mile crash draw with severity; deductible charged to profit; optional suspension.

variables.name: Vandalism and unrest pull-back
variables.description: Damage to fleet cars, or areas the fleet withdraws from, during protests or targeted vandalism.
variables.values_or_range: 0-5 cars damaged per event; area closed 1-72 h [design].
variables.impact_evidence: [U] several Waymo cars were set on fire during Los Angeles protests in June 2025 [uncertain: news recollection, not re-checkable this session].
variables.how_to_model: Event-linked damage hazard and a zone closure flag.

variables.name: Fleet profit variance and correlation
variables.description: Day-to-day spread of fleet profit and how correlated the cars' earnings are.
variables.values_or_range: daily profit coefficient of variation 5-30% [design]; high correlation for cars in the same zone or queue.
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; the team plans 100 runs per model.
variables.how_to_model: Report mean, standard deviation and CVaR over seeds, plus a diversification index.

variables.name: Fleet objective function
variables.description: What the fleet is scored on.
variables.values_or_range: total profit / profit per car / profit with a service floor (e.g. served at least 95%, p90 wait at most 10 min) / weighted profit and service.
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim: raising its fairness weight cut unserved requests from 9.66% to 8.17% but raised median wait from 9.0 to 16.9 min [S], so the best policy flips with the objective.
variables.how_to_model: Harness scoring function; robotaxi own-app mode includes a service floor, platform-driver mode scores profit only.

variables.name: Fleet KPI panel
variables.description: Standard fleet statistics reported beside profit.
variables.values_or_range: utilisation, trips per car-day, empty-mile share, riders served, wait p50 and p90, charging deadhead, availability, compute cost.
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim and offpeak report these [S]; Waymo about 20 trips per car-day (R06-057) [S].
variables.how_to_model: Harness logs per car per minute and summarises per run.

variables.name: Scale ladder and normalisation
variables.description: Running the same model at several fleet sizes and against baselines, to separate skill from scale.
variables.values_or_range: N in {1, 10, 100}; score = profit / best-baseline profit at the same N.
variables.impact_evidence: [design].
variables.how_to_model: Harness sweep; plot profit per car against N for each model.

variables.name: Simulator scale and runtime
variables.description: How fast the engine must run so that N-car fleets and 100 runs per model stay affordable.
variables.values_or_range: one day with 5,000 cars in about 3 s (greedy, Manhattan); model calls dominate run time.
variables.impact_evidence: fleetsim cut runtime from 37.3 s to 2.8 s per simulated day at 5,000 cars by using matrix indices [S].
variables.how_to_model: Vectorised zone-matrix engine with cached travel-time matrices.

variables.name: Fleet visual encoding
variables.description: How the live map shows fleet cars: colour by model, status, revenue ticker and own-car density against demand.
variables.values_or_range: 5 statuses (busy, idle, repositioning, charging, out of service); 1-5 model colours.
variables.impact_evidence: [design]; visualisation plan in the meeting notes.
variables.how_to_model: The event log feeds a map layer; time-lapse with day and night shading.

variables.name: Model under test
variables.description: The LLM or agent system whose decisions drive the car or fleet; the main independent variable of the benchmark.
variables.values_or_range: 5 frontier models for the headline board (e.g. Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, OpenAI and Google flagships) plus cheap development models; one model per run, or several per city in arena mode
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 2 end balances spread from about $9.2k to $15.5k across the top 7 of 66 entries, and about $7.5k-$15.5k across the top 10 (29 Sep 2026 capture, D01/D11) [corrected by fact-check: was 'across top models']; Vending-Bench 1: 'All models exhibit very high variance across their five runs' (verified in the paper text).
variables.how_to_model: One provider adapter per model behind an identical tool schema, observation and budget.

variables.name: Model snapshot and serving provider
variables.description: The exact model version string and the API or host that serves it, pinned and recorded for every run.
variables.values_or_range: Dated snapshot vs moving alias; first-party API vs third-party host vs self-hosted weights; quantisation level for open models
variables.impact_evidence: [S via team phase-1 dossier B, GitHub copy of the Vending-Bench 1 leaderboard] Kimi K2 Thinking averaged $1,296 net worth via Moonshot's own API vs $649 via a third-party API; on the leaderboard's minimum-net-worth metric the order flips ($418.54 third-party vs $354.00 Moonshot) [corrected by fact-check: source was misattributed to D11, and the flip was omitted].
variables.how_to_model: Run manifest records model id, provider, region, quantisation and date; leaderboard refuses unpinned aliases.

variables.name: Reasoning effort and sampling settings
variables.description: The thinking or effort level and sampling parameters used on every call.
variables.values_or_range: Effort low / medium / high / xhigh / max (Claude Opus 5.5 defaults to medium); temperature only where the API accepts it; max output 1k-16k tokens per call
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Claude API reference (cached 6 Oct 2026): effort levels, Opus 5.5 default 'medium', non-default sampling rejected on current Claude models (verified); [P* via team phase-1 notes, GitHub copy of Andon Labs posts] Opus 4.8 scored much higher at High than at Max effort on Vending-Bench 2, which Andon attributes to less context compaction [corrected by fact-check: benchmark version specified].
variables.how_to_model: Fixed per leaderboard track; an effort x model ablation on a subset of seeds.

variables.name: Context-management policy
variables.description: How much run history the model sees at each step, and how older history is trimmed, summarised or moved into memory.
variables.values_or_range: Sliding window of 10k / 30k / 60k tokens; server-side compaction (Claude default trigger 150k tokens, beta); memory tool on or off
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1: GPT-4o mini with a 60k-token memory did worse than with 30k, and collapse was not explained by the context filling up (Pearson r = 0.167 between days until sales stop and days until full memory) (verified in the paper text); compaction default 150k verified in the bundled Claude API reference.
variables.how_to_model: Harness-level policy fixed in the frozen track; token counts logged per step.

variables.name: Frozen harness vs bring-your-own agent
variables.description: Whether every model runs inside one fixed agent loop (measures the model) or teams may bring their own scaffold (measures the whole system and its cost).
variables.values_or_range: Frozen: fixed tools, prompts, context policy and budgets / BYO: any scaffold, reaching the simulator only through the same metered tool API
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D10] SWE-bench bash-only and Terminal-Bench's separate --agent and --model flags exist because scaffolds move scores enough to need separate tracks.
variables.how_to_model: Two leaderboard tracks; BYO tool calls metered by the tool server.

variables.name: Development model tier
variables.description: Cheap models used to build, debug and red-team the simulator and harness before paying for frontier runs.
variables.values_or_range: Claude Haiku 5.5 ($0.10 in / $0.50 out per MTok for prompts of 100K tokens or fewer; $0.50 / $2.50 above), Sonnet 5.5 ($2 / $10), open-weight Qwen models self-hosted or hosted; also usable as bot drivers
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Claude price table (cached 6 Oct 2026): Haiku 5.5 costs 1/40 of Opus 5.5 per token, but its tokenizer counts the same text as about 30% more tokens, so it is about 1/31 per unit of text [corrected by fact-check: long-prompt tier and tokenizer added]; the team's '80-90% of the intelligence at 1/100 of the cost' for Qwen is unverified [U].
variables.data_source: Claude pricing https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing; Qwen model cards (Hugging Face, not reachable here)
variables.how_to_model: Dev configuration profile; never mixed into headline results.

variables.name: Base system prompt and paraphrase set
variables.description: The fixed instructions that set the task, rules and tools, plus a few paraphrases to check that rankings do not hinge on wording.
variables.values_or_range: Minimal / standard / detailed-rules prompt; 2-3 meaning-preserving paraphrases per variant
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Sclar, Choi, Tsvetkov and Suhr 2023 (arXiv 2310.11324), FormatSpread repo: LLM results shift with meaning-preserving prompt formatting; the README gives no magnitude, and the size of the effect for long agentic runs is [U].
variables.how_to_model: Prompts versioned with the benchmark; headline uses the standard prompt; paraphrases run on a seed subset.

variables.name: Event-awareness prompt arm
variables.description: The team's planned A/B arm: the prompt either tells the model that public events (concerts, games, parades) move demand and gives it the event tool, or says nothing.
variables.values_or_range: Off / mention only / mention plus event-calendar tool
variables.impact_evidence: [design] team meeting plan; events create local demand surges and egress queues (cross-link R03); the effect is concentrated on event days (high there) and near zero otherwise.
variables.data_source: NYC Permitted Event Information https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/tvpp-9vvx ; venue schedules for ticketed events
variables.how_to_model: Crossed with the information level (R12-013) on the same seeds so the difference isolates the prompt.

variables.name: Objective statement and cost framing
variables.description: What the prompt says to maximise and which costs it makes salient.
variables.values_or_range: Net profit per online hour / total daily net profit / gross revenue; costs itemised in the prompt vs only in the ledger; optional constraint text such as 'be home by 02:00'
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1: setting the $2 daily fee to zero did not raise sales; without cost pressure GPT-4o mini 'appears to get stuck in loops' (verified in the paper text).
variables.how_to_model: One canonical objective for the headline (net profit per online hour after all costs); others as ablations.

variables.name: Strategy hints
variables.description: Whether the prompt includes driver know-how such as airport runs, the Manhattan core at rush hour, or avoiding drop-offs that strand the car.
variables.values_or_range: None / generic tips / NYC-specific playbook
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D10] Project Vend 2: 'Among the most impactful changes we made was forcing Claudius to follow procedures'; [S via R01] Haggag, McManus and Paci (2017, AEJ: Applied): neighbourhood experience raises NYC taxi drivers' productivity.
variables.how_to_model: Hints off for the headline so the benchmark measures the model's own strategy; hints as an ablation.

variables.name: Role framing
variables.description: Which operator the model plays, which fixes its rules, costs and allowed actions.
variables.values_or_range: Human app driver (Uber/Lyft, NYC HVFHV) / yellow or green taxi (street hail plus e-hail) / robotaxi operator (no driver; usually fleet level)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation, TLC Jan 2023 weekdays: HVFHV driver pay $54.04 per engaged hour vs yellow $109.84 gross per engaged hour (total_amount incl. surcharges, tolls and card tips only, not driver take-home; 'engaged' = passenger on board), so roles face different economics [corrected by fact-check: cash tips are not recorded in total_amount].
variables.how_to_model: Role selects a rule pack (fares, fees, hours rules, actions) from R07-R09; persona details are R09-004.

variables.name: Simulation disclosure
variables.description: Whether the model is told it is in a benchmark simulation or framed as doing a real job, which can change its conduct.
variables.values_or_range: Disclosed / neutral / framed as real
variables.impact_evidence: [P* via D01/D11] Andon Labs: Claude Fable 5 skipped paying a customer because 'customers are part of the simulation anyway'; effect on profit unmeasured [U].
variables.how_to_model: Framing twins on a seed subset; conduct metrics reported by framing.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: Information level ladder
variables.description: Which public information the agent can query, set as ordered levels so the value of each layer can be measured.
variables.values_or_range: L0 own state and offers only; L1 + map and historical aggregates; L2 + calendar and weather forecast; L3 + public event calendar; L4 + in-app market signals; Oracle = true future demand (upper bound only, never scored)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation, HVFHV Jan 2023 (re-verified against the script output): zone-hour pay per engaged hour from the six prior non-holiday weekdays correlates 0.84 with the day-11 values (5,528 zone-hours), so L1 already carries most of the learnable spatial signal; event layers matter mainly on event days [design].
variables.data_source: TLC trip records; NOAA/NWS; NYC Open Data events (see data sources)
variables.how_to_model: Each level is a set of enabled query tools; runs at several levels on the same seeds.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: Historical trip aggregates given
variables.description: Pre-computed public summaries of past trips that the agent can read, such as pickups and pay by zone and hour of week.
variables.values_or_range: None / last 10 days / same season last year / full history; fields: pickups, pay per engaged hour, median wait, drop-off mix by zone x hour of week
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation, HVFHV Jan 2023: the mean of the six prior non-holiday weekdays predicts Wed 11 Jan zone-hour pickups with WAPE 0.134 (top-10 zones per hour overlap 82%), close to the 0.120 reached by a plain mean of 19 other weekdays [corrected by fact-check: 0.120 is a reference level that uses days after the target, not a proven floor].
variables.how_to_model: Pipeline computes aggregates only from data dated before the scenario window and serves them through a query tool.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: Weather forecast as issued
variables.description: The forecast the agent sees must be the one published before the decision, never the weather that actually happened.
variables.values_or_range: None / text day-ahead forecast / hourly precipitation probability and temperature / perfect foresight (oracle only)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] serving observed weather as a 'forecast' leaks the future; [P] Open-Meteo data is CC BY 4.0 (free API non-commercial only); NWS forecasts and the NDFD forecast archive at NCEI are public [U]; the weather-to-demand link is R04.
variables.data_source: NWS API https://api.weather.gov (User-Agent header required) ; NOAA NCEI GHCN/LCD Central Park USW00094728 https://www.ncei.noaa.gov/ ; Open-Meteo https://open-meteo.com
variables.how_to_model: Store forecast vintages keyed by issue time and serve the latest vintage issued before the sim clock.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: Public event calendar content
variables.description: Which event fields the agent gets and from which public sources.
variables.values_or_range: None / NYC permitted events (name, type, borough, location, start and end, street closure; about one month of lead time) / + ticketed venues (MSG, Barclays, Yankee Stadium, Citi Field, USTA) / + pre-event attendance estimates
