variables.impact_evidence: [S via GitHub copies of the Socrata metadata] NYC Permitted Event Information (tvpp-9vvx) lists approved events 'that will occur within the next month', with 13 columns (event id, name, start and end, agency, type, borough, location, street side, closure type, community board, police precinct, CEMS id); ticketed events on private property are generally not street permits, so they need venue schedules [corrected by fact-check: scope and columns added]; the most frequent event types are youth and adult sports permits and farmers markets [S], so filtering for large events matters (cross-link R03).
variables.data_source: https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/tvpp-9vvx (next month); https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/bkfu-528j (historical); team and venue schedules
variables.how_to_model: Event tool returns events within a time window and radius; attendance only from figures public before the event.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: News, alerts and incident feed
variables.description: Time-stamped public alerts the agent may read: traffic incidents, subway outages, severe-weather warnings, news headlines.
variables.values_or_range: None / official alerts only (511NY, MTA service alerts, NWS warnings) / + news headlines
variables.impact_evidence: [S, GitHub copies of the 511NY developer docs] the 511NY developer API gives incidents and events; it needs a developer key and is throttled to 10 calls per 60 s (verified); subway disruptions push riders into cars [U] (cross-link R03, R05).
variables.data_source: 511NY https://511ny.org/developers/doc ; MTA GTFS-realtime alerts https://new.mta.info/developers ; GDELT news archive [U]
variables.how_to_model: Replay archived alerts at their publish time; generated shocks get synthetic alerts.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: Map and geographic knowledge given
variables.description: How much map knowledge the harness supplies versus what the model must bring from pre-training.
variables.values_or_range: None (world knowledge only) / zone list with names and adjacency / + travel-time matrix tool / + points of interest (airports, venues, hospitals, chargers)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] NYC is heavily described on the web, so models start with strong priors [U]; a travel-time tool narrows the gap between models with and without NYC knowledge.
variables.data_source: TLC taxi zones (263 zones; IDs 264 Unknown, 265 Outside of NYC); OpenStreetMap NY extract https://download.geofabrik.de/north-america/us/new-york.html
variables.how_to_model: Map tools backed by the R01/R10 engine.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: In-app market signals
variables.description: What a real driver app would show: surge or bonus heatmap, busy areas, airport queue length.
variables.values_or_range: Off / coarse heatmap refreshed every 5 min / fine heatmap every 1 min; taxis get none except via e-hail apps
variables.impact_evidence: [U] Uber and Lyft driver apps show surge heatmaps and airport queues; the surge rules and queues are R06/R07, showing them is an information choice [design]; the high rating is a design judgement because the signal reveals current local demand.
variables.data_source: none found (platform data is not public; the simulator generates the signal from its own state)
variables.how_to_model: Render from the simulator's matching state with display lag and spatial coarsening.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: Own-history log access
variables.description: Whether the agent can query a structured log of its own past trips, earnings and idle spells, beyond its own notes.
variables.values_or_range: None / current shift / all earlier days in the run
variables.impact_evidence: [S via R01] Haggag, McManus and Paci (2017): NYC taxi drivers learn by driving; [design] a log tool tests learning from data rather than from memory notes.
variables.how_to_model: Query tool over the run's own ledger; on in learning-protocol runs.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: Public vs insider boundary rule
variables.description: The written rule for what counts as fair, public input at decision time, for each role.
variables.values_or_range: Allowed: public sources, the driver-app view, own history (a robotaxi operator may also use its own fleet logs). Not allowed: future requests, unserved demand, rival platforms' internal data, the replayed day's own TLC records, realised weather
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] TLC monthly files arrive with about a 2-month lag (the team catalog lists files through Aug 2026 as of mid-Oct 2026; verified), so a real driver never has the day's trip records at the time.
variables.how_to_model: Every tool is tagged allowed or disallowed per role and checked by the harness.

variables.sub_box: Information level and the public vs insider line
variables.name: As-of timestamp discipline
variables.description: Every piece of information carries an issue time no later than the sim clock, and the harness enforces it.
variables.values_or_range: Strict (issue time <= now) / lagged (issue time <= now minus the real publication lag)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] look-ahead leakage is a standard failure of backtests and of LLM forecasting evaluations [U].
variables.how_to_model: Data store keyed by (valid time, issue time); unit tests that no tool returns rows issued in the future.

variables.name: Observation content per step
variables.description: The state fields shown to the agent each time it is asked to act.
variables.values_or_range: Clock, zone and coordinates, status (idle / en route / occupied / charging / offline), fuel or battery, earnings and costs so far, hours online, the pending offer (fields per R05-036), nearby signals
variables.impact_evidence: [P] tomslee/ridehail reports vehicle time as P1 (waiting for a trip), P2 (en route to pickup) and P3 (with passenger), the standard state split (verified in README); [design].
variables.how_to_model: Fixed observation schema versioned with the benchmark.

variables.name: Observation and action format
variables.description: How the state is rendered to the model and how its actions come back.
variables.values_or_range: JSON / natural-language summary / ASCII grid map / rendered map image (multimodal); actions via strict tool schemas vs parsed free text
variables.impact_evidence: [P] the MIT-licensed LPSim (Large-scale Parallel Simulator, GitHub Xuan-1998) exposes get_state(), a to_prompt_context() natural-language view and a TOOL_DEFINITION for OpenAI/Anthropic function calling, for LLM fleet control [corrected by fact-check: '(MIT)' was the licence, not the institution].
variables.how_to_model: Default JSON plus a short text summary with strict tool schemas; image map as an ablation.

variables.name: Action space and granularity
variables.description: The set of moves the agent can make and their spatial and time resolution.
variables.values_or_range: Accept / decline offer; reposition to a zone (263 TLC zones) or a point; wait N minutes; cruise loop (taxi); go offline or take a break; go home; refuel or charge; set destination filter; optional route choice (R10-042)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] MaaSSim models drivers who 'reject/accept incoming requests', 'strategically re-position while being idle' and 'opt-out of the system' (verified in README); [design]; the spatial unit itself is R01-009.
variables.how_to_model: Typed tools with validation; the same set for every model within a role.

variables.name: Decision cadence and wake-up rule
variables.description: When the model is called: on each event, on a fixed tick, or when it asks to be woken.
variables.values_or_range: Event-driven (offer, drop-off, arrival, idle timer every 5 / 10 / 15 sim-min) / fixed tick of 1 / 5 / 15 min / agent-set wait(until)
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D10] YC-Bench jumps to the next event and Vending-Bench clones charge sim-minutes per call; [design] calls per sim-day set both how much skill can show and the run cost (R12-063).
variables.how_to_model: Discrete-event core (SimPy-style priority queue) wakes the agent on events plus an idle heartbeat.

variables.name: Wall-clock coupling and model latency
variables.description: Whether simulated time stops while the model thinks, or slow answers cost sim time and missed offers.
variables.values_or_range: Paused (turn-based) / latency-charged (sim time advances by measured latency x factor) / real time
variables.impact_evidence: [S via R06-024] real ride offers time out after about 10-15 s; long reasoning calls can exceed that [U], so latency modes would heavily penalise slow models.
variables.how_to_model: Headline paused; latency-charged as a separate track; latency recorded on every call.

variables.name: Tool-call time cost and per-step budget
variables.description: How much sim time information queries take, and how many tool calls are allowed per decision.
variables.values_or_range: 0 or 1 sim-min per query; 3-10 tool calls per step; optional daily query cap
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D10] ProsusAI vending-bench charges 5-75 sim-min per tool call inside a working day (5 for reads, prices and notes; 25 for email, search and payments; 75 for stocking and cash collection) [corrected by fact-check: was 5-45]; [design] without any cost an agent can query everything every step for free (cross-link R09-067).
variables.how_to_model: Per-tool time-cost table and a call counter enforced by the harness.

variables.name: Invalid or malformed action policy
variables.description: What happens when the model returns an illegal, malformed or impossible action.
variables.values_or_range: No-op with error message / up to K retries / default safe action (wait) / penalty per invalid call
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 runs fell into 'meltdown' loops (verified in the paper text); [design] cheap models break format more often, so this policy can dominate their scores.
variables.how_to_model: Validate against the tool schema, return the error, count invalid calls as a reported metric.

variables.name: Fleet control interface
variables.description: How an LLM controls N cars: one call per car, one dispatcher call for all cars, or the model sets parameters that a solver executes.
variables.values_or_range: Per-car agents / central dispatcher every 1-5 sim-min / policy-parameter mode (zone targets, acceptance thresholds) run by a matcher
variables.impact_evidence: [P] LPSim README advertises 'closed-loop LLM-driven fleet optimization' over a structured state API (verified); [design] per-car calls multiply cost by N (cross-link R11).
variables.how_to_model: Fleet tool with batched assignments and rebalancing orders, validated by the fleet manager.

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: Episode horizon and shift window
variables.description: The length of one scored episode and when it may start and end.
variables.values_or_range: One shift (8-12 h) / one day (24 h, agent picks its shift) / 10-day block / week; start at home at a fixed or chosen time; starting fuel or charge
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1: agents often stopped selling after some sim-days (mean days until sales stop 8-102 by model; verified in Table 1), so long horizons expose derailment that short ones hide.
variables.how_to_model: Scenario config sets horizon and start state; shift start inside a day is an agent action.

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: End-of-episode valuation and go-home rule
variables.description: How the final position, charge and unfinished trips are valued, so the agent cannot game the last hour.
variables.values_or_range: End at home required, or penalised by the deadhead cost home; leftover charge valued at energy cost; trip in progress completed or prorated
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 valued inventory at cost and its highest-net-worth run prioritised storage over cash; [design] the team's 'take me home' feature needs a terminal rule (cross-link R09-020).
variables.how_to_model: Terminal settlement step in the ledger.

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: Memory carry-over scope
variables.description: Which notes and learnings persist between days and between runs.
variables.values_or_range: None / within one 10-day run / across runs (lifelong notes) / across models (not allowed)
variables.impact_evidence: [design] the learning test only works if notes persist across days; [P] own computation: a 10-day window already holds most of the learnable weekday pattern (WAPE 0.134 vs 0.120 for a plain 19-weekday mean) [corrected by fact-check: 0.120 is a reference level, not a proven floor].
variables.how_to_model: Memory store snapshotted at day boundaries and cleared per protocol arm.

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: Memory format, size cap and reflection step
variables.description: The form and size of stored learnings, and whether the agent gets an end-of-day turn to write them.
variables.values_or_range: Free-text notes capped at 2k / 8k / 20k tokens; key-value store; table; end-of-day reflection turn on or off
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 gave a scratchpad, key-value store and vector database (verified); [P via D11] YC-Bench found scratchpad use 'the strongest predictor of success'.
variables.how_to_model: Memory tool with a hard size cap; reflection prompt at the end of each sim-day.

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: Training window composition (days 1-10)
variables.description: Which calendar days make up the learning days.
variables.values_or_range: 10 consecutive days including weekends and holidays / weekdays only / matched day types; same month vs mixed seasons
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation, HVFHV Jan 2023 (re-verified): predicting 11 Jan from all of 1-10 Jan (including the New Year holidays) gives zone-hour WAPE 0.238 vs 0.134 from the six non-holiday weekdays, so the window decides what can be learned.
variables.how_to_model: Scenario builder picks windows from a calendar table with holiday flags (R02).

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: Test day choice (day 11)
variables.description: Which day the learned agent is tested on.
variables.values_or_range: Next day / same weekday a week later / weekend / event day / shock day / different season
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation (re-verified): in the previous 10 days a weekday target has 5-8 same-type days but a weekend target only 2-3; rolling day-type-aware zone-hour WAPE ran 0.11-0.28 for HVFHV (median 0.174) and 0.14-0.34 for yellow (median 0.198).
variables.how_to_model: Test pool stratified by day type; learning gain reported per stratum.

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: Repetition design (the 'x100')
variables.description: How the team's '10 days x 100 runs' is read: 100 independent 10-day runs, or 100 passes over the same days with accumulating notes.
variables.values_or_range: Independent replicates (fresh memory each) / repeated epochs with persistent memory / epochs with demand redrawn each pass
variables.impact_evidence: [design] repeated exact replays let notes memorise specific requests, which is overfitting, not learning; [P] own computation: even a 19-weekday mean leaves zone-hour WAPE of about 0.12, so accuracy well beyond that on replayed days is a warning sign of memorisation [corrected by fact-check: was 'gains beyond that are memorisation'; covariate-aware learners could beat a plain mean somewhat].
variables.how_to_model: Protocol config; demand redrawn from the generator on every epoch.

variables.sub_box: Horizon, episodes and the learning protocol
variables.name: Learning-gain control arms
variables.description: Comparison runs that turn 'score on day 11' into a measure of learning.
variables.values_or_range: Day 11 with memory vs (a) the same model with empty memory, (b) with expert-written notes, (c) with notes written by another model
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Anthropic, 'A statistical approach to model evaluations' (read directly): report paired differences on shared items; [design].
variables.how_to_model: Same seeds across arms; learning gain is the paired difference.

variables.name: Demand source mode
variables.description: Whether riders come from an exact historical day, a resample of it, a fitted generator, or a hybrid.
variables.values_or_range: Exact replay / bootstrap resample / parametric synthetic / replay plus perturbation
variables.impact_evidence: [U] TLC records hold completed trips only, so replay caps demand at served trips (cross-link R05-069, R05-066); [P] tabmemcheck README shows GPT-4 completing random rows of Iris and GPT-3.5 completing Titanic and UCI Wine rows, so exact replay of well-known data invites recall.
variables.how_to_model: Generator fitted per zone x hour of week with day effects; exact replay kept for validation.

variables.name: Seeds and common random numbers
variables.description: Separate random streams per component so every model faces the same riders, traffic and shocks.
variables.values_or_range: One seed per scenario with streams for demand, travel time, rider behaviour, rivals and shocks; optional antithetic pairs
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation, HVFHV Jan 2023 weekdays (re-verified): daily trips vary with CV 12.4% but pay per engaged hour only 1.4%, so unpaired day draws would swamp model gaps of a few percent; [P* via D11] CEO-Bench uses independent RNGs per simulator component. Impact is on ranking reliability, not on expected profit.
variables.how_to_model: Streams keyed by (component, entity, period); the same seed list for every model.

variables.name: Runs per model and statistical power
variables.description: How many seeds and repeats per model and scenario are needed to separate models.
variables.values_or_range: 5-100 runs per model; report means, paired differences and clustered confidence intervals
variables.impact_evidence: [S via D11, inference] observed run-to-run CVs of 0.07-1.0 in business sims mean 5 unpaired runs detect only gaps of about 0.12-1.8x the mean (about 1.77 x CV at 80% power) [corrected by fact-check: was 0.35-1.8x, which is the CV 0.2 to 1.0 range]; [P] Anthropic: clustered standard errors 'can be over three times as large as naive standard errors'; use power analysis. Impact is on ranking reliability, not on expected profit.
variables.how_to_model: Pilot on a dev model to estimate variance, then size the run count by power analysis.

variables.name: Scenario day-type mix
variables.description: Weights of ordinary, weekend, holiday, rain or snow, event and shock days in the test pool.
variables.values_or_range: e.g. 50% ordinary weekdays, 20% weekends, 10% holidays, 10% bad weather, 10% big-event days
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation (re-verified): HVFHV pay per engaged hour was $72.15 on 1 Jan 2023 (holiday, median wait 6.05 min) vs about $54 on ordinary weekdays, so the mix shifts absolute levels.
variables.data_source: TLC trip records; NOAA weather; NYC permitted events
variables.how_to_model: Stratified scenario sampler; scores reported per stratum and pooled with fixed weights.

variables.name: Data era
variables.description: Which period's data calibrates demand, prices and speeds.
variables.values_or_range: 2019 (pre-COVID) / 2022-2024 / 2025 onward (after congestion pricing started on 5 Jan 2025)
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] TLC catalog row counts (team R02 data, re-verified): yellow raw rows per day rose from 123,670 (Oct 2024) to 142,861 (Oct 2025); [S via R10] congestion pricing changed CBD speeds, so every module must share one era.
variables.how_to_model: Era tag on every calibrated parameter; mixing eras fails validation.

variables.name: Date and identity masking
variables.description: Hiding the real date, and optionally the real zone names, so the model cannot recall what happened on that day.
variables.values_or_range: Real date / weekday and season only / shifted year / renamed or mirrored zones
variables.impact_evidence: [P] tabmemcheck (Bordt et al., 'Elephants Never Forget', COLM 2024): GPT-3.5/4 completed rows of famous public tables; [S] NYC taxi data is heavily reused, e.g. the Kaggle 'New York City Taxi Trip Duration' competition data reappears in public code [fact-check: was U], so recall of specific days is plausible but untested.
variables.how_to_model: Masking layer renames dates and, in an anonymised track, zones; a real-name track keeps credit for legitimate world knowledge.

variables.name: Post-cutoff fresh test months
variables.description: Test scenarios built from TLC months published after each model's training cutoff.
variables.values_or_range: Test months at least one month after the model cutoff; refreshed every season
variables.impact_evidence: [P] the TLC Jan 2023 files used here are byte-identical (SHA-256 recomputed by fact-check) to the TLC originals in the team catalog, which lists months through Aug 2026 by Oct 2026, so new months keep arriving with about a 2-month lag.
variables.how_to_model: Pipeline pulls each new month, refits the generator and adds a fresh test season.

variables.name: Private hold-out pool, canary and contamination probes
variables.description: Keeping test seeds private, marking files so they are kept out of training data, and testing models for recall before scoring.
variables.values_or_range: Public development seeds / private test seeds; canary GUID in every file; probes asking for the scenario day's weather, trip counts and event outcomes
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D10] AppWorld ships encrypted test bundles with a canary string; [S via D08] ARC Prize calls its API-evaluated set 'semi-private' because of leakage risk; [P] tabmemcheck provides header, row, feature completion and first-token tests.
variables.how_to_model: Private seed list held by maintainers; probe suite run per model; flagged days dropped.

variables.name: Difficulty preset and noise scale
variables.description: Bundled settings from easy to hard, plus a multiplier on randomness.
variables.values_or_range: Easy: Manhattan only, deterministic travel times, no rivals, full information / Medium: whole city, stochastic travel, bot drivers / Hard: shocks, EV range, fatigue, difficult riders; noise scale 0-1.5x calibrated
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D11] CEO-Bench exposes competitor strength as a difficulty knob; [P] tomslee/ridehail ships village / town / city presets (plus game and game-big); [P] own computation: real zone-hour day-to-day error is WAPE about 0.12 for a plain 19-weekday mean [corrected by fact-check: a reference level, not a proven floor].
variables.how_to_model: Preset files over module switches; leaderboard per preset.

variables.name: Generalisation city
variables.description: Running the same agent in another city to test transfer beyond NYC knowledge.
variables.values_or_range: NYC (default) / Chicago (TNP trips; taxi trips with anonymised taxi ID) / synthetic grid city
variables.impact_evidence: [S via GitHub copies] Chicago publishes TNP trips (m6dm-c72p, 2018-2022; n26f-ihde, 2023-2024) and taxi trips (wrvz-psew, 2013-2023; ajtu-isnz, 2024 onward) [corrected by fact-check: the cited tables are closed series; newer IDs added]; [S] the Chicago taxi table carries a taxi_id column (GitHub schema copies; was U), allowing the shift reconstruction NYC data no longer permits.
variables.how_to_model: City pack (map, zones, demand, rules) behind the same interfaces.

variables.name: Solo vs shared-city arena mode
variables.description: Whether each model drives alone among scripted bots, or several models drive in one city at once and compete for riders.
variables.values_or_range: Solo plus bots / arena with 2-5 models, seat rotation and mirrored seeds
variables.impact_evidence: [P* via D11] Vending-Bench Arena: agents sharing one location formed price cartels; [S via R06/D07] rankings differ from solo play (cross-link R06-060) [uncertain: D07's fact-check found mixed evidence; Andon says Claude models were historically worse in multiplayer, but its Arena page shows Claude winning rounds 2, 4 and 6 of the first six].
variables.how_to_model: Arena scheduler rotates start zones and seeds; scores per seat and pooled.

variables.name: Passive and random floor baselines
variables.description: Simple policies that set the score floor.
variables.values_or_range: Passive: stay where dropped and accept every offer; random repositioning; for taxis, random cruising
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D10, README re-read] ABC checklist: 'A trivial do-nothing agent scores 38% pass@k and pass^k' on tau-bench (a benchmark flaw since fixed), so floors must be measured before claiming skill; impact is on the normalised score because the passive run is the floor.
variables.how_to_model: Scripted policies run on every seed; the passive score is the normalisation floor.

variables.name: Heuristic baselines
variables.description: Rule-based strategies a competent human might use.
variables.values_or_range: Heatmap follower (go to the best historical zone-hour); surge chaser; taxi rules (Manhattan core and airports, head back after outer-borough drop-offs); go home at the end
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation: zone-hour pay ranks are stable day to day (r = 0.84), so a heatmap follower should be a strong baseline; [design]. [corrected by fact-check: impact was high; a reference baseline does not change the agent's profit or the normalised score unless used as the normalisation anchor]
variables.how_to_model: Scripted policies that use only allowed information.

variables.name: Operations-research planner baseline
variables.description: An optimisation policy that plans on expected demand without seeing the future.
variables.values_or_range: Single car: dynamic programming over zone x 5-min time on expected earnings; fleet: min-cost flow or batched bipartite matching with rebalancing
variables.impact_evidence: [S via R01] Buchholz (2022, Review of Economic Studies) models NYC taxi search as a dynamic spatial equilibrium; [U] MDP methods for taxi driver revenue (e.g. Rong et al., CIKM 2016). [corrected by fact-check: impact was high; a reference baseline not used for normalisation does not change the measured profit]
variables.how_to_model: Solver reads the generator's expected rates and re-plans every 5 sim-min.

variables.name: Hindsight oracle
variables.description: The best achievable profit on the realised day with perfect knowledge of every request, used as the score ceiling.
variables.values_or_range: Exact longest path over a time-expanded graph (single car); ILP or min-cost flow (fleet); approximations for long horizons
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D11] Magentic Marketplace reports an 'Optimal (theoretical upper bound)' and Supply_Chain_Bench scores against reference policies including a best-found feasible one; [design]; impact is on the normalised score because the oracle is the ceiling.
variables.how_to_model: Computed offline per seed after the run; never shown to agents.

variables.name: Human reference
variables.description: How people do, from players using the same interface and from real driver earnings.
variables.values_or_range: Expert NYC drivers or trained players on the UI (5 or more); real-world anchor: HVFHV driver pay about $54 per engaged (passenger-on-board) hour (weekdays, Jan 2023) before idle time, the drive to pickups and costs
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 had one human (5 h, $844.05) who beat every model's worst run (best model minimum $476; verified); [P] own computation of pay per engaged hour from TLC driver_pay and trip_time.
variables.how_to_model: Human UI over the same tool API at the same information level.

variables.name: Learned RL baseline
variables.description: A policy trained by reinforcement learning on the simulator, which shows how hard and how exploitable the world is.
variables.values_or_range: Tabular Q-learning over zone x time, or deep RL (PPO); trained on development seeds only
variables.impact_evidence: [P] LPSim provides a 'Gymnasium environment wrapper for training dispatch/pricing policies' (verified); [U] RL dispatch is used in production ride-hailing. [corrected by fact-check: impact was medium; a stretch reference policy not used for scoring]
variables.how_to_model: Gymnasium wrapper around the simulator; evaluated on private seeds.

variables.name: Headline metric
variables.description: The single number used for ranking.
variables.values_or_range: Net profit per online hour after all costs (fuel or energy, maintenance, depreciation, insurance, tolls, fees, commission); fleet: net profit per vehicle-hour and in total
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation: citywide HVFHV pay per engaged hour is stable (CV 1.4%), so profit per online hour mostly measures utilisation and positioning, the skills under test; [design] team goal.
variables.how_to_model: Ledger computes net profit; online hours come from the status log.

variables.name: Normalisation and aggregation
variables.description: How profits from different scenarios are combined into one score with uncertainty.
variables.values_or_range: Per scenario (agent - passive) / (oracle - passive); aggregate with the interquartile mean and stratified-bootstrap CIs; per-family profiles
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D11] IQM with stratified-bootstrap CIs (rliable, Agarwal et al. NeurIPS 2021) recommended for business sims; [P] day levels differ ($72 holiday vs $54 weekday per engaged hour), so raw dollars are not comparable across days.
variables.how_to_model: Scoring script runs after runs are sealed.

variables.name: Risk and consistency panel
variables.description: Measures of bad days and reliability shown next to the mean.
variables.values_or_range: CVaR of daily profit (worst 10-20% of seeds), worst run, SD across seeds, stranding rate (battery or fuel out), pass^k (all k runs beat the human median)
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D11] tau-bench's pass^k; [P*] Vending-Bench 1: Claude 3.5 Sonnet's worst run was $476 against a mean of $2,217.93 (verified).
variables.how_to_model: Computed from per-run ledgers.

variables.name: Compliance, safety and service panel
variables.description: Penalties and side metrics for rule-breaking and for how riders are served.
variables.values_or_range: TLC rule violations (taxi refusals, hours-of-service, illegal stopping), unsafe instructions, discriminatory declines; acceptance and cancellation rates; outer-borough service share; rider wait (fleet); for a fleet or robotaxi operator only, an optional Manhattan-core cruising-cap toggle
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D11] Business Arena logs fines and violations and conduct panels are standard in business sims; the rules themselves are R07. [corrected by fact-check: the HVFHS cruising cap (35 RCNY 59D-21, at most 31% of available time cruising below 96th St) binds app companies, not drivers, and was reported annulled by a state court in Dec 2019 [U]; the 2025 access rules (59D-22(c)) also bind platforms]
variables.data_source: Rules of the City of New York Title 35 via https://github.com/jehiah/nyc_code_archive (see R07)
variables.how_to_model: Rule engine scans the event log; severe violations disqualify, others deduct.

variables.name: Efficiency diagnostics
variables.description: A breakdown of how time and miles were used.
variables.values_or_range: P1 / P2 / P3 time shares, empty miles per paid mile, trips per hour, average wait for the next offer
variables.impact_evidence: [P] tomslee/ridehail's P1/P2/P3 split; [S via R10] about 41% of FHV time in Manhattan below 96th Street was without a passenger in 2019; the TLC's cruising definition counts the drive to a pickup as cruising, so this is P1 + P2 [fact-check note].
variables.how_to_model: Computed from the status log and shown on the dashboard.

variables.name: Information-value metric
variables.description: The profit difference caused by giving one more layer of information, on the same seeds.
variables.values_or_range: profit(level k) - profit(level k-1) per model and day type; event-day subset for the event arm
variables.impact_evidence: [design] team plan to test with vs without event information; paired design per Anthropic's evaluation guidance [P].
variables.how_to_model: Paired runs across information levels, reported per model.

variables.name: Compute-cost accounting
variables.description: Whether API spend is only reported or also charged inside the game.
variables.values_or_range: Reported only ($ and tokens per run) / in-world charge (e.g. $100 per million output tokens, as in Vending-Bench 2) / cost-adjusted score
variables.impact_evidence: [P* via D11] Vending-Bench 2's prompt charges '$100 per million output tokens' weekly; [P via D11] HAL argues for 'accuracy and cost by default'.
variables.how_to_model: Token meter per call; optional deduction in the ledger.

variables.name: Tokens per decision and cache hit rate
variables.description: Input and output tokens per model call and the share read from the prompt cache, which together set the cost of a run.
variables.values_or_range: 8k-40k input and 0.5k-3k output tokens per call; 40-150 calls per sim-day; cache hits 0-90%
variables.impact_evidence: Low on in-sim profit unless charged, high on budget: [design, P prices, arithmetic re-verified] at 85% cache hits, 80 calls x 20k in / 1k out per sim-day costs about $3.1 (Opus 5.5), $1.7 (Sonnet 5.5) or $7.3 (Fable 5.1); Opus 5.5 cache reads cost $0.20 vs $4 per MTok uncached; 5-minute cache writes cost 1.25x input.
variables.how_to_model: Append-only conversation to keep cache hits high; token meter per call.

variables.name: Per-run budget cap and exhaustion rule
variables.description: The maximum spend or tokens per run, and what happens when it runs out.
variables.values_or_range: $20 per run (team estimate); on exhaustion the agent falls back to the passive policy, or the run ends and the remaining hours score zero
variables.impact_evidence: [design calc from P prices, re-verified] $20 covers a 10-day run only at a lean cadence (40 calls x 8k tokens per day: about $7 on Opus 5.5, $17 on Fable 5.1); the standard cadence costs about $31 (Opus 5.5) to $73 (Fable 5.1) per 10-day run.
variables.how_to_model: Budget meter in the harness; advisory task budget passed to models that support one.

variables.name: Campaign budget, parallelism and wall-clock
variables.description: Total spend across models and runs, and how fast runs finish.
variables.values_or_range: 5 models x 100 runs x $20 = $10k (team estimate); concurrency limited by provider rate limits; hours of wall-clock per run
variables.impact_evidence: [P*] Vending-Bench 1 runs took 5-10 real hours for 2,000 messages and about 25M tokens (verified); [design calc, re-verified] 100 runs x 11 sim-days at the standard cadence would cost about $3.4k per model on Opus 5.5 and about $8k on Fable 5.1.
variables.how_to_model: Run scheduler with rate-limit-aware concurrency and a budget ledger per model.

variables.name: Calibration targets and sim-to-real validation
variables.description: Real-world statistics the simulator must reproduce before any model is scored.
variables.values_or_range: Zone x hour pickups (sim-vs-real WAPE near the real day-to-day reference of 0.12-0.13); HVFHV pay about $54 per passenger-on-board hour (weekdays, Jan 2023); median request-to-pickup 3.5-4.2 min (weekdays, Jan 2023); speeds by hour (R10)
variables.impact_evidence: [P] own computation on the TLC Jan 2023 HVFHV and yellow files (re-verified against the script output; 0.12-0.13 is a reference level, not a proven floor [corrected by fact-check]).
variables.data_source: NYC TLC trip records; NYC DOT Traffic Speeds https://data.cityofnewyork.us/d/i4gi-tjb9 (minute-level data; portal update frequency listed as Daily)
variables.how_to_model: CI suite runs scripted policies and checks the targets on held-out days.

variables.name: Coordinate synthesis within taxi zones
variables.description: Since July 2016 TLC trips carry only taxi-zone IDs, so exact pickup and drop-off points must be generated for routing and the map.
variables.values_or_range: Zone centroid / uniform in the polygon / weighted by buildings or road length / snapped to curb nodes
variables.impact_evidence: [P] toddwschneider/nyc-taxi-data README: 'Starting in July 2016, the TLC no longer provides pickup and dropoff coordinates' (verified); the spatial unit itself is R01-009.
variables.how_to_model: Sample points per trip from a zone-specific point set using the seeded stream.

variables.name: Data licence filter
variables.description: Only data whose terms allow use, and ideally redistribution, in a public benchmark may feed the simulator.
variables.values_or_range: Allowed: NYC and NY State open data, US federal data (NOAA, EIA, NLR, formerly NREL), OpenStreetMap (ODbL, share-alike on derived databases), Open-Meteo (data CC BY 4.0; free API non-commercial only). Excluded: Google-Maps-derived travel times, paid feeds (e.g. PredictHQ), scraped app data
variables.impact_evidence: [P] Open-Meteo README: data CC BY 4.0, APIs 'free for open-source developers and non-commercial use', code AGPLv3; [P*] NREL is now the National Laboratory of the Rockies and its developer API moved to developer.nlr.gov (developer.nrel.gov stopped resolving 29 May 2026) [corrected by fact-check]; the other terms are [U] and must be checked on portals that were blocked here.
variables.how_to_model: Licence field in the data catalog; the build fails on unknown licences; ship fitted parameters where raw redistribution is unclear.

variables.name: Vehicle state log for the live map
variables.description: The per-vehicle, per-tick record the visualisation reads.
variables.values_or_range: Vehicle id, model id, timestamp, lon/lat, heading, status (P1 / P2 / P3 / charging / offline), battery or fuel, cumulative revenue, costs and net; event markers
variables.impact_evidence: [P] deck.gl TripsLayer (MIT) animates trips from per-trip path and timestamps arrays coloured by a categorical attribute (vendor); its demo view is centred on New York (-74, 40.72) (verified in app.tsx).
variables.how_to_model: Simulator emits path plus timestamps per vehicle segment and a ledger stream.

variables.name: Playback speed, lighting and clip export
variables.description: How fast simulated time plays on screen, how day and night are shown, and how clips are cut for social media.
variables.values_or_range: 1 sim-hour = 10-60 s; trail length; sun-position lighting vs fixed; automatic clips around surges, storms and event egress
variables.impact_evidence: [P] deck.gl trips example defaults (verified): loopLength 1800, trailLength 180, fixed ambient light plus one point light with no time of day; sun position from the NOAA solar calculator [S via sibling dossier].
variables.how_to_model: Renderer maps the sim clock to light level; clip exporter keyed on the event log.

variables.name: Model colour coding and live revenue overlay
variables.description: Visual encoding that lets viewers follow each model's cars and money in real time.
variables.values_or_range: One colour per model (colour-blind-safe palette); per-model revenue and net-profit tickers; leaderboard panel
variables.impact_evidence: [design] team visual plan; [P] TripsLayer colours trips by a categorical attribute (vendor in the example).
variables.how_to_model: Colour map from the run manifest; overlay reads the ledger stream.

variables.name: Replay and audit log
variables.description: Everything needed to re-simulate and audit a run.
variables.values_or_range: Seeds, config hashes, model ids, every observation, tool call, response and token count, ledger entries
variables.impact_evidence: [P via D10] reproducibility comes from re-simulating a logged action stream because LLM sampling is not deterministic: [P] batch_invariant_ops README: 'out of 1000 random length 100 completions we see 18 unique samples' with vLLM, and one after the batch-invariant fix [uncertain: that the requests used an identical prompt is implied, not stated; model not named].
variables.how_to_model: Append-only JSONL per run plus a sealed scoring step.
